User manual · M-VAVE FM-1

JIANT FM

All of JIANT FM on one page: every button, knob and message named as the device shows it. If you read one chapter, read Saving and loading.

Open JIANT StudioEspañolWhat's new in V10.8.21Interactive manualDownload

JIANT FM — User Manual

JIANT FM V10.8.72 for the M-VAVE FM-1 (public release; what changed since V10.8.48, the last public release, is in New in V10.8.72)

Versión en español: manual en español.

This manual is for musicians who have just installed JIANT FM and want to know how to play it, build songs with it and, above all, save their work without losing anything. It follows the firmware as it is in that version: every button, knob and message is named exactly as the device shows it.

Never used a synth or a step sequencer? Start with First steps: six short tours, button by button.

If you only read one chapter, read 12. Saving and loading. Coming from V10.6c (the last public version) or earlier: What's new in this version.

Essential commands

Navigate

HOME EDIT SEQ FX GLO ENV LFO SCL ARP SAVE
From elsewhere: the page you were last on in that section. Already inside: the first page of the next group.
SELECT
Walks every page of the section, a page a detent.
ALGORITHM
Picks the track (T1–T4, or T1–T6 with TRACKS 6).
PRESETS
Always presets: the track's sounds. SEQ: the patterns. On SEQ › STEP FX it picks the step.
KNOB 1–4
The four cards on screen. KNOB 1 picks (step, bar, slot, row).
HOME held
The MENU.

Play and record

PLAY
Start / stop. Held about 0.7 s: PANIC, all notes off.
GLO + PLAY
Restart from the top.
REC
Arms live recording on the selected track. Held alone and let go: UNDO (again: redo).
OCT− OCT+
Keyboard octave; both together: back to 0. On action pages and dialogs: back / confirm.
GLO + SELECT
Tempo, from any page.

Hold a button (layers and combos)

FX held
Punch-in effects on the keys.
LFO held
MACRO layer: KNOB 1–4 are M1–M4.
SCL held
The keys set the root.
HOME + SELECT
The GENERATOR.
EDIT + SELECT
The sound dice (OCT+ keeps, OCT− cancels).
EDIT + PRESETS
The first sound of the next / previous engine.
GLO + G4
UNDO the last big change.
SEQ + G5
Clear the cursor step.
SAVE + C5
NAME: rename.
SEQ + REC
Clear all sequences (asks first).

New in V10.8.21

HOME › JAM
Keys F3–B3 pick A–D on every track, OCT+ go, OCT− stop, REC records a take, K4 LOCK plays it.
SEQ › STEP FX
Hold a white key: a step component plays; with REC it is written into the step.
SEQ › CLAY
DRONE CLAY: a low drone and four modulators per track.

Power-on

OCT− + OCT+ at power-on
Hardware calibration.
OCT− + OCT+ held 5 s
Update mode (let go to cancel).

What's new in this version

New in V10.8.72 (since V10.8.48)

The versions V10.8.49 to V10.8.72 in one list. Where a chapter below still describes the earlier screen, this list is right.

Sequencer - SEQ EDIT (V10.8.49–V10.8.53): hold SEQ on a SEQ page. It replaces SEQ TOOLS. KNOB 1 / KNOB 2 pick the steps, KNOB 3 the ACTION, KNOB 4 its amount, D5 or OCT+ does it, F#5 is UNDO / REDO. 25 actions: STRETCH, SQUEEZE, REPEAT, NUDGE, ROTATE, SHIFT, REVERSE, DUP, TRANSP, OCTAVE, INVERT, STUTTER, ARP, MUTATE, GEN, RANDOM and more. No selection: the whole track. See SEQ EDIT. - Steps by the keys (V10.8.50–V10.8.51): two or more step keys held select those steps (SEL 5-8); step keys held + EDIT clear them; COPY, PASTE, DUP and CLEAR say which steps (COPY 5-8). See Copy, paste and duplicate.

Saving - OVERWRITE A? (V10.8.52): SAVE + C4–F4 or SAVE + OCT+ over a part with music asks first (OCT+ yes, OCT− no), once a part. GLO + G4 puts the part back as it was. See Quick store. - A saved generator draft is a project (V10.8.52): SAVE › PROJECTS › SAVE says SAVED SONG n and that project is the open one from then on; RESTORE LAST brings it back. ARRANGE's OCT+ says ROW DUPLICATED. - Old projects (V10.8.51): a project from before V10.7 says OLD PROJECT: OPEN IN STUDIO and is never erased. Felucca's first settings (PER1, PER2) are no longer read (V10.8.59). See Old projects and old settings. - JIANT Studio (V10.8.51, V10.8.54): a project library (list, rename, copy, move, delete from the phone or the computer) and a converter that opens the old projects.

Sound and the generator - OTT (V10.8.71): a two-band compressor on every track, FX › TRACK › OTT (DEPTH, TIME, UP/DN, X-OVER), from JIANT BYTE. V10.8.72: a much harder law (up to +36 dB up towards −18 dBFS, 20:1 over −22 dBFS, then a soft clip, never over −0.3 dBFS), DEPTH squared up to 70 and steeper above, TIME 48 by default (a V10.8.71 project's TIME opens 24 lower). See OTT. - DIST TYPE (V10.8.72): six new types made from JIANT BYTE's formulas, 6 RING, 7 STEPS, 8 XOR, 9 WOB, 10 SFOLD and 11 SAT. SOFT … AMP keep 0–5, and old projects sound the same. See Per track. - The generator (V10.8.68–V10.8.72): JIANT BYTE's song plans (templates by genre, 2 to 5 minutes, fills), each section its own automation (grich), call and response and EXPLORE's cut back, the drums' punch back, NEO CLASSIC with no drums. No piece goes over −1 dBFS before the master (V10.8.51). V10.8.72: OTT on the electronic genres' drums and bass, and in one seed in two on the lead; RESOUND sets it too (see GEN). - MATH: WAVE SYNC (V10.8.62) locks the formula's rhythm to the tempo, with the new preset BYTE SYNC; LOOP (V10.8.66) repeats it every 4 BAR … 1/32. - MOD AMOUNT (V10.8.51): −200 … +198 %; 100 % sweeps the whole range. - DRUM-X (V10.8.49): one GAIN, on LEVEL (KIT 2's KNOB 4 is gone; kits sound as before). - USB MIDI host (V10.8.69): more keyboards are accepted, and the connection is tried three times. - RESOUND (V10.8.54): GLO + A4 gives every track a new sound, the song kept. See RESOUND.

Screen - Big titles and the knob footer (V10.8.65): a page with no picture shows its name large; a knob turned says its page on the footer (LFO RATE 1.24 HZ). See Big titles, the knob footer and the banners. - OCT+ hints and banners (V10.8.53–V10.8.54): a page with OCT+ gestures says them in its footer; RESTART, SD MUTED, LANE, REC GRID, PROJECT n, ALL UNMUTED, ROOT, QUANTIZE and A > B NEXT BAR are said on screen; the count-in is one line, 4 3 2 1. - HOME › MACROS is back (V10.8.64), ECO's third page, with DICE MACROS (HOME + SELECT). LIFE: KNOB 3 is STEREO (was PUMP), and every depth goes further above 60. See The sections. - HOME › BEING › VISUAL and MENU › DISPLAY › SAVER (V10.8.56–V10.8.67): pictures from FM's own graphics that move with the music, on the whole screen. V10.8.72: every frame is drawn, with fewer points under load (about 20 frames a second where it drew 3 to 7). See VISUAL and SAVER. - MENU › DISPLAY › PANEL (V10.8.63): AUTO / A / B, for the screens of the late-2026 units. See PANEL. - SCL › CHORD names each degree's triad (D-, E°, F; V10.8.59). FX's DELAY draws its echoes as columns (V10.8.53). The creatures are drawn closer to their originals (V10.8.54–V10.8.55). - Gone for room: ABOUT's AUDIO LOAD lines and SEQ › STEP FX's RAMP curve (V10.8.49), FX › MASTER › EQ's curve (V10.8.53). - Less CPU (V10.8.60): more of the sound runs from RAM; the sound is the same bit for bit.

New in V10.8.48 (since V10.8.21)

The versions V10.8.22 to V10.8.48 in one list. Where a chapter below still describes the earlier screen, this list is right.

  • GATE on the reverb and the delay (V10.8.44): on FX › REVERB and FX › DLY, hold OCT+ and turn KNOB 4: its card reads GATE (0–127; 0 off). The return stays open while something is sent to it and shuts a while after that falls silent (16: a 1/16, 64: a quarter, 127: two quarters), cutting the tail: a gated room, echoes that stop with the phrase. Saved with the project. See Delay and Reverb.
  • A LEVEL page on every engine (V10.8.44): EDIT's first group ends with LEVEL: GAIN (0–12 dB), LEVEL, PAN (on a kit after KIT 2). GAIN left ANALOG's and PHASE's MORE page; OCT+ held + KNOB 4 on EDIT 1 still reaches it.
  • The ARP in time (V10.8.45): while the transport plays an arpeggio starts on its RATE's grid and stays on it; recorded, each of its notes lands on its own step. See ARP.
  • The header's load is a number (V10.8.45), 0–99, where the five bars were. MENU › ABOUT lost the CPU clock and rails lines (V10.8.45); LAST CRASH is still there (V10.8.46). The velocity diagnostic is gone from the firmware: VELOCITY_DIAG.es.md is for older versions.
  • The song's words (V10.8.47): SAVE › PART SLOTS' KNOB 2 is PLAY/EDIT (was LOAD; while the loop plays the part comes in on the next bar); the SAVE layer's STORE A–D are SAVE A–D (the screen says SAVED A); PLAY's mode LOOP is PART (PART / SONG); a song's END LOOP is REPEAT (the footer: 40 BARS · END REPEAT); a part box with no name shows its bars in the song (12 BARS) instead of USED, and PLAYING instead of NOW; the chips' legend reads ARRANGE PART+BARS; on JAM and TAKE, SEQ is PART and CAMBIO is SWITCH.
  • GENERATOR (V10.8.43–V10.8.48): it leaves SCL › HARMONY as you set it (on, the piece sits on the key's tonic and HARMONY moves it); sections half as long, and a section that comes back is varied; RADIO's loop changes every 16, 8 or 4 bars by tempo, and a STOP in the piece's last bar stops; every part moves (slow free LFOs on the filter and the shape, the pan), real envelopes by role (no part held at full sustain but organs and drones; leads little sustain and a long release), chords, leads and arps with their own filter type (BP, or HP with KEY TRK 100), the track's GAIN making up the level; a chord part on a lead's sound without its vibrato; PHONK always the drift; JAZZ's hats at half. See 8.
  • RADIO and MOOD (V10.8.39–V10.8.41; HOME › GENERATOR 4): KNOB 3 RADIO ON / OFF: when the song's last row ends (a loop: after 16 bars, 32 above 110 BPM; since V10.8.45 16, 8 or 4 bars) the generator makes the next piece by itself and it comes in on the bar line, ENTRY's way. It only goes on while a generated draft plays, not with FORM MY LOOP; press OCT+ once to start. KNOB 4 MOOD, CALM … MID … DANCE: it moves the energy and the drums (CALM: the kit lighter, gone near the end; DANCE: drums in every piece, the kick on the beats), with GENRE RANDOM it also leans the genres by their tempo, and in EXPLORE it moves the tempo. Neither is saved with the project. See 8.
  • GENERATOR (V10.8.39–V10.8.42): every genre retouched (its own traits, riffs, drums and mix), the kick tuned to the key, the genre FUGA removed (29 genres), HARD BASS with a DONK bass, DREAM POP's two arrangements, IDM AMBIENT from 76 BPM.
  • In time (V10.8.40): the tempo is exact and every track takes its place from the transport, so after a LEN or DIV change, EUCLID, a mutation or a variation of another length a track is back with the others at its next step. RESYNC: hold SEQ and press PLAY while it plays: every track from its first step on the next bar, without stopping (GLO + PLAY is still the RESTART at once).
  • DJ FILTER on MIXER (V10.8.38): on GLO › MIXER a tap of OCT+ turns KNOB 4 between BPM and DJ FILT.
  • SEQ › NOTE is back (V10.8.38), after STEP: FOCUS, PITCH, MOVE, MICRO. SEQ › BAR, the PHRASES pattern loader and GLO › SYSTEM 2 (MIDI) are gone.
  • TRANS (V10.8.38): SCL › CHORD's KNOB 4, the track's transpose (±24 semitones).
  • GAIN on every engine (V10.8.38): on the engine's first EDIT page, OCT+ held + KNOB 4: 0–12 dB (since V10.8.44 also on the LEVEL page).
  • KEY TRK NOTE in tune (V10.8.38): on LP and HP the resonance's peak sits on the note.
  • SWARM (V10.8.38): WAVE on SWARM 2's KNOB 4 (the sine, or one of eight FLOAT formulas), a tag on the picture that says what it hears (ALONE, AIR n, PROX n, AIR OFF), and MODE >T1 … >T6: SWARM's notes play that track's engine.
  • KEY TRK on FILTER (V10.8.37): on EDIT › FILTER, OCT+ held + KNOB 2 (CUT's) picks OFF / 50 / 100 / NOTE, with a tag on the curve. At 50 and 100 the cutoff follows the key (100: a semitone a semitone, around C4), on every type, the combs too; NOTE is 100 with the final cutoff on the semitones: MOD SEQ › CUT plays tuned resonances. A track's, saved with the project, OFF by default.
  • MUTATE without a page (V10.8.37): EVERY is a tag in EUCLID's picture ("EVERY 4"); set it with OCT+ held + KNOB 4 on EUCLID. OCT+ alone (when let go) mutates; OCT− goes back to the anchor.
  • Factory sounds retouched (V10.8.37): sends by role (basses dry, leads more delay than reverb, pads more reverb), a late vibrato on the leads, the plucked strings darker when played softly, and movement on the sounds that had none (the kits, ANIMAL, WEST's struck ones and basses).
  • FX › DIST, KNOB 4: NOISE (V10.8.36; 0–127, a track's): a noise that moves the gain and the tone inside the distortion: grain stuck to the note, not a hiss added (silence stays silent). Not on the AMP type.
  • FX › CHORUS, KNOB 4: MIX (V10.8.36; 0–100 %, global): at 0 the chorus as it was; towards 100 each track's dry sound goes down by its CHORUS send and one modulated voice is left, in the middle: MIX 100 and the send whole, a vibrato.
  • CLOUD reverb (V10.8.36): it starts with the note (no longer like a late delay); half the grains read just behind the present and the others 1, 2 or 3 sixteenths back, by the tempo; the tail a little lower.
  • GENERATOR (V10.8.36): the mix by genre (the lead and the arp up where they were buried, less reverb on a club's stabs, the kick's DUCK stronger) and EXPLORE with the lead / arp dialogue.
  • DRONE CLAY, complete (V10.8.27–V10.8.31; see DRONE CLAY): each modulator has its own RATE on the bar's grid (1/64 … 4BAR, dotted, triplets and polyrhythms), the drone has PITCH (−24 … +36 semitones), the hits (KICK, SNARE, HAT…) are a drum on any engine, and there are four pages: DRONE CLAY · CLAY MOD · CLAY RHYTHM · CLAY TIME. Under the scope, a thin bar a modulator shows what it adds now. A modulator at AMOUNT 0 strikes nothing, and at RATE HOLD the drone is never struck again. The keys play gestures (the whites) and the drone's degree (the last seven); RUN has four values: SONG, FREE, SONG NOKEY, FREE NOKEY.
  • WEST › DUST (V10.8.28): 1 to 95 is white noise going into the folder with the core (it folds and passes the gate with it: inside the timbre, not beside it); 96 to 127 is METAL, a metallic tone instead of the noise. It no longer crackles.
  • MUTATE is back, compact (V10.8.35; without a page since V10.8.37): EUCLID's pattern mutates by itself every EVERY bars (OFF, 1, 2, 4, 8). On EUCLID, OCT+ mutates and OCT− goes back to the anchor. See MUTATE.
  • LIVE is back, compact (V10.8.35): on SEQ › STEP FX, the black keys 1–9 change live how the selected track's sequence walks: RATE x2, x3/2, x2/3, REVERSE, PING-PONG, RANDOM, THIN, GIRO − and GIRO +. See Live sequences.
  • EUCLID (V10.8.35): on a melodic track KNOB 4 is ROLE (MELODY, CHORDS, BASS, ARP) and the MODES page is named MELODY (CONTOUR, RANGE, MOTIF, VARY). The picture is one ring of dots.
  • FILTER (V10.8.35): the types MS20 and LP24 are gone (TYPE: LP, HP, BP, COMB, COMB-). A project or a user preset that used them opens with LP.
  • ENV › STAGE is gone (V10.8.35): ENV's chain is ENV · ENV DEST · ENV 2. LOOP stays on ENV DEST.
  • FX › PUNCH IN (V10.8.27, V10.8.33): the PUNCH LANE page and the lane's picture are gone; the punch-in lane itself stays (REC records it, the generator uses it).
  • MOD (V10.8.22): turning a slot's SRC or DEST shows the whole route in full names ("LFO > FILTER CUTOFF"; E1–E8 by the engine's own names), with HELP OFF too.
  • DRUM-X (V10.8.32): the MATH formulas used as FM modulators sound clean, without steps.
  • GENERATOR (V10.8.34): twelve more progressions, the contrast section with a progression and a register of its own, motifs with a signature leap, more call and response, and a dialogue between the lead and the arp.
  • JIANT Studio and the editor (V10.8.23–V10.8.26, V10.8.33): the FM-1's screen mirror (only the rows that changed are sent), and the FM-1 tells which section, page and layer you are on, for Studio's live guide.

New in V10.8.21 (since V10.7.81)

The betas V10.8.1 to V10.8.20 in one list. Where a chapter below still describes the older screen, this list wins.

  • Song mode (HOME › JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE): play the four sequences A–D of every track live (F3–B3 pick A–D on all tracks, OCT+ GO, OCT− STOP, CAMBIO sets when a change lands). REC records the take; K4 LOCK plays it back and what you play over it is marked YOU; with a track selected, REC redoes that track for one round and OCT− undoes it. TAKE edits the changes (K1 pick, K2 move, K3 sequence, K4 bars, OCT+ new, OCT− delete). A help line on JAM and TAKE says what to do next (MENU › DISPLAY › HELP OFF hides it). GLO › LIVE is gone: JAM plays the sequences live.
  • Step components you play (SEQ › STEP FX): the PRESETS knob picks the step; the 16 white keys play components while held — STUTTER, STUTTER /2, /4, RATCHET x2 x3 x4 x8, ARP UP / DOWN / UP-DOWN, OCTAVE UP / DOWN, RANDOM, TRANSPOSE +2, CHORD, MUTE — and with REC they are written into the step with their value and length (into COMP, or COMP 2 when COMP is taken). A big banner names the key and what it does while held (also on the FX layer's punch-ins).
  • DRONE CLAY (SEQ › CLAY, from JIANT BYTE): a sequencer per track — a very low drone in the track's own voice (RATE re-strikes it with the transport, or holds it) and four modulators (shape, euclid, amount, decay, gestures) aimed at any of the track's parameters; note gestures (ARP, CHORD, HIT) play on the scale. On MONO / LEGATO it yields the voice to the steps; a TIME or PITCH punch-in restarts it from its first hit.
  • Which track you are on, always: a bar on top reads TRACK N / ENGINE in the track's own colour (T1 yellow, T2 orange, T3 red, T4 magenta, T5 violet, T6 blue); the same colours on the mixer, the beings, JAM and TAKE.
  • Macros as destinations: LFO › MACROS — KNOB 1 picks the macro, its destinations add up (16 routes in all); in the MOD matrix M1–M4 are destinations, not sources.
  • Redesigned screens: FX in the HUD look (DELAY's echoes a tunnel, REVERB cells, CHORUS L/R orbit, SLICER, MASTER, DIST); FX › SENDS as columns; GLO › MIXER channels; ENV as layers of the last notes; LFO as a satellite writing its wave; EDIT › FOCUS a horizontal heat bar with the parameter's whole name and its modulation; ARRANGE and GENERATOR a living score (sections as wide as their bars, one lane per track); SCL › KEY the scale's whole name, its notes and degrees; SCL › CHORD the chord really played (D MIN7…), its notes and intervals, the seven degrees' chords. Names are whole where they fit (ECOSYSTEM, GENERATOR, MIXER, MODULATION…).
  • Power-on: the boot "Six threads" with the signature drawn smooth and the version shown; the click at power-on is gone (the output opens after the audio has started, then fades in).
  • Removed for room: GLO › LIVE, SEQ › STRETCH, MUTATE, the sequence dice (SEQ + SELECT; the sound dice stays), GLO › GLOBAL COMP, ENV › TRACKS and the one-time teaching hints. Old projects open: their settings are kept and ignored. (MUTATE and LIVE came back, compact, in V10.8.35: see above.)

New in V10.7.81 (since V10.7.16)

The betas V10.7.17 to V10.7.80 in one list. Where a chapter below still describes the older screen, this list wins.

Drums - DRUM-X in 8 pages: KIT (MORPH SNAP TONE DECAY), KIT 2 (NOISE BODY GLUE GAIN), SOUND (PITCH DECAY LEVEL), SOUND 2 (NOISE COLOR PMOD), SOUND 3 (WAVE FILTER P.ENV), SOUND 4 (SIDE SEND KEY MAP), CROSS MOD, FILTER. BODY is the shell's resonance; GAIN is clean, 0 to +12 dB. - MATH formulas: SOUND 3's WAVE goes on past SINE FM METAL BELL to F01–F48, a MATH formula as the sound's FM modulator, played as a wavetable and drawn on screen (four moments, cold to hot). RATIO (¼ … 16, 24 values) on KNOB 4, MOD AMT in COLOR's place. Two kits are made of formulas, GLITCH FM and MATH LAB; EDIT + SELECT (DICE) gives about half the sounds a formula of their own.

Engines - MATH MORPH: ALGO B (where CHIP was) and MORPH A → B (where BEND was) glide from one formula to another. - Every engine like the kit: FILTER (TYPE CUT RES IMAGE), PLAY (POLY GLIDE UNISON VEL), GAIN 0 … +12 dB clean. - EDIT's pages by their names, the extras on one MORE, now before PLAY; FOCUS drawn in heat colours.

Harmony and sequences - SCL › HARMONY, its own tab (KEY CHORD HARMONY SCENE): PROG LENGTH EVOLVE SKIP; every melodic sequence follows the progression, shown as roman numerals in the key, the playing chord lit. CHORD's sets: POP JAZZ SOUL DREAM QUART. - EUCLID › MODES › ROLE (MELODY CHORDS BASS ARP) writes over the harmony the other tracks play; CONTOUR RANGE MOTIF shape the melody. - Step components: RAMP (END: BACK HOLD PING), FILL (where LOCK was); STUT and RATCH on the tempo grid.

Performance - Hold FX: a map of named cells (the effects by name, M1–M4 on top, the mutes T1–T6 below). - Punch-in editor: OCT+ on FX › PUNCH IN (or FX + OCT+). Each key: WHAT (an effect, or a parameter: M1–M4, CUT, PITCH, TIMBRE, VOLUME, PAN, DIST, CHORUS, DELAY, REVERB, VIBRATO), HOW (HOLD LATCH QUANT, or RAMP UP / DN, SINE, STUTTER, S&H), AMOUNT (−100 … +100 %) and TIME (1/16 … 8 bars); two slots, A and B. New effects: REVERSE, FREEZE, TAPE STOP, PITCH UP / DOWN, STRETCH. FX › PUNCH IN's knobs are the macros M1–M4. - LIFE (HOME › LIFE): the tracks move each other (FILTER TIMBRE PUMP FX). - SCENE plays on the live tracks only; its LEADER can be the keys or a track's notes.

Generator (GENE) - Seeds are fused (A+B in the name), never the same throw twice; it waits for the bar while playing; GENE 4: KEY NEW / KEEP. - DUBSTEP (the wobble, its rate moving; MATH basses), SHOEGAZE, METALCORE, CUMBIA villera, eight more progressions (neo-soul, jazz, IDM, progressive); each genre its FX STYLE; MATH, WEST and STRING more often.

Screens and settings - The song's pages live in HOME › SONG: TIMELINE ARRANGE PARTS CLIPS (SAVE saves and loads). - MENU › DISPLAY › PRESETS: SCROLL (the knob walks the sounds) or MENU (the list opens as you turn). - MENU › HELP: a knob's meaning in the header where it is not obvious. Oscilloscopes instead of decorative bars. - Defaults: LARGE off, CLICK on REC, COUNT-IN 1 BAR. - GLO held + G4: UNDO.

The beta V10.8.1 redesigns the song mode (each track its sequences A–D, CAMBIO, a JAM take with LOCK); it is not in this version. See the README.

Since V10.6c

Everything since V10.6c, the last public version, in one list; each item links to its place in the manual.

Before you update - 6 songs, not 8 (V10.6p). Songs 7 and 8 no longer open: their flash is kept for a drum sample bank. Move them into 1–6, or save a complete backup first (the editor's Save backup, or the installer's backup); the backup keeps all eight, and a restore says which songs stayed only in the file. - Very old projects retired (V10.6s): projects saved by JIANT before 1.0.3 (FUN1 to FUN6) are refused and left untouched, and a DIGITAL sound loads as FM6's init. Open them in an earlier version (V10.6c) and save them again there if you still need them. - Older projects retired (after V10.7.13, room for GENE's FORM MY LOOP): projects and backups saved in the formats FUN7 to FUNB (Felucca 1.0 / 1.1 and JIANT up to 0.5) are no longer read; at power-on such a project shows OLD PROJECT: NOT READ (since V10.8.51: OLD PROJECT: OPEN IN STUDIO, see Old projects) and its slot is empty (the flash keeps it until you save over it). The web editor cannot convert them: open them in V10.7.13 or earlier and save them again there (that saves today's format). Also gone: the old user presets' conversions (SAMPLE PERC, TRIO, LOFI's chips, 0.3 / 0.4 values: such a preset loads as stored, a retired engine's playing as ANALOG), a retired engine's track in a project now gets ANALOG's first preset (not its nearest sound), and ADD's own creature (ADD draws the being, as the other engines did before 0.9.6). - Newer FM-1 units (V10.6z): the FM-1s sold from late 2026 (logo on the front) have another flash chip. Older JIANT versions ran on them from RAM only (no saving, no GENE, no updates from the device); this version saves normally. If yours did not keep your songs, update.

Songs - SAVE opens on the song: TIMELINE, PARTS and CLIPS (V10.6o, V10.6s), then SECTIONS. See TIMELINE, PARTS and CLIPS. - A song keeps the sounds you change while it plays (V10.6z8); EDIT > RECALL brings a track's section sound back. - SAVE SONG AS copies a whole song into another project (SAVE > PROJECT).

Drums and the generator - DRUM-X: a quality pass (V10.6q), a classic CMOS cowbell, the EXTENDED key map by default with real fills and every sound chromatic (V10.6r), ACOUST gone (V10.6o), the punchy kicks and bright hats back (V10.6z9). See The keys in V10.6r: EXTENDED. - GENE (HOME's generator, GEN until V10.6m) plays the owner's curated genres, CUMBIA, EBM, BAILE FUNK, PHONK, HIP HOP (trap, drill, pluggnb, boom bap or lofi), JAZZ at every tempo and TECHNO ROCK (rock or synth 80s) among them. SCL > SCENE's DRUM role can take a kit generated for the genre (SCENE DRUM GEN). - The thermal palette everywhere: every note its own heat, the piano roll coloured by pitch class (V10.6w).

Sequencer - Step component RAMP replaces JUMP (V10.6v): a step's parameter lock glides there over 1–32 steps or 1–16 bars. - REC keeps the feel (V10.6z4): note lengths, legato as SLIDE, the velocity as played. GATE 100 % for new tracks.

Playing - Key velocity and aftertouch (V10.6z7, after Charles Vestal's Velo): F3..C5 sensed, each key calibrated as you play; MENU > CONTROL > VELOCITY, VEL MIN, AFTERTOUCH, VEL LEARN. See Key velocity and aftertouch. - Expression keys (V10.6z4): a note held + OCT− a vibrato, + OCT+ a bend (MENU > AUDIO > OCT BEND). - SWARM (EXT's Bluetooth instrument): a melody from how near you are, FAR / NEAR morph, the scale walk and CHAOS (in SELF's knob place). See EXT › SWARM. - FAR / NEAR calibration now takes the median of 2.5 s (HOLD STILL) (V10.6z8). - VOICE no longer clips on open vowels; WORDS has CONS, the consonants' length (V10.6y).

Connections - NRPN for every automatable parameter, knob moves sent as NRPN with MIDI OUT ALL (V10.6z3): docs/NRPN.md. - The editor protocol is a versioned contract (1.2): web/EDITOR_PROTOCOL.md. - The second core starts only on the stock power settings (after a SAFE START: one core) (V10.6z2).

0. Quick start

Install

  1. Open the web installer in Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Chrome on Android with a USB OTG cable (iPhone and iPad have no Web MIDI): https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/webapp/installer/
  2. Connect the FM-1 directly with a USB data cable.
  3. Coming from another custom firmware (Felucca, Skiff, baudgirl or any other)? Return to official first, with the installer's Return to official button (it also saves that firmware's backup). Writing JIANT straight over another custom firmware has left an FM-1 unable to start.
  4. Press Install. It first checks the FM-1's firmware and writes only over official V16, official V15 or JIANT (anything else: it sends you to Return to official first). Don't unplug the cable while it writes.

Return to official takes M-VAVE's own FM-1.fwsc of V16 (718,196 bytes, what M-VAVE offers now) or V15 (699,956 bytes), unzipped from M-VAVE's download page and checked byte for byte. It saves a complete JIANT backup first; to come back, press Install and restore the backup with the editor.

JIANT has no user samples: if you come from Felucca, its user samples (USR1–3) are lost on install. Keep your WAV files.

Your first sound (1 minute)

  1. Power on. The signature draws itself, then you land on HOME: six creatures, one per track. (V10.6e) The tracks start as a band in tune: T1 DRUM-X (ACOUSTIC), T2 ANALOG (PLUCK), T3 PHASE (INIT SAW), T4 FM6 (FM BASS), T5 VOICE (CHANT) and T6 ANIMAL (WHISTLE), each its preset's sound, dry.
  2. Turn ALGORITHM to pick a track (T1–T6). With the default TRACKS 4 it stops at T4: T5 and T6 appear only with TRACKS 6 (see 13).
  3. Turn PRESETS to browse sounds. Play the keys.
  4. Turn KNOB 1–4: on HOME they are the four most useful controls of the track's engine.
  5. Don't like it? Hold EDIT and turn SELECT: the sound is rolled into a new variation and you hear it at once. OCT+ OK keeps it, OCT− CANCEL brings the sound back.

Your first song (5 minutes)

  1. Hold HOME and turn SELECT (or on HOME tap HOME to its last tab, GENE). The GENERATOR opens on EXPLORE (no genre, every rule broken): press OCT+ as it is, or pick RANDOM or one of the genres with KNOB 1 first. A whole song idea appears: engines, sounds, parts, scale, tempo and effects. Press PLAY.
  2. Not your thing? Press OCT+ again: a new seed, a new piece. Too busy? Turn SELECT one detent right for GENERATOR 2 and lower DRUMS or ARP, then OCT+: the same piece with that changed. OCT− goes back to ECOSYSTEM. To go back to what was there before: hold GLO and press G4 (UNDO).
  3. Like it? Stop (PLAY), then press SAVE and turn SELECT to PART SLOTS (the page before PROJECTS, where SAVE opens). Turn KNOB 4 to the right so its card says OCT+, then press OCT+. Type a name with the keys (or keep the one offered) and press OCT+ again. The screen says SAVED.
  4. Make a variation (change some steps, mute a track) and save it into section B: on PART SLOTS turn KNOB 1 to B, then KNOB 4 and OCT+ as before.
  5. Hold SAVE and press G5: ARRANGE (the song's rows; HOME's SONG tab). Press OCT+ to add a row, set its section with KNOB 2 and its length with KNOB 3 (bars). Add a row for A, one for B. Press PLAY: the song plays the rows in order.

That's the whole loop: make music → save it into a section → chain sections in ARRANGE.

1. The panel

The names below are the ones the firmware uses (the HARDWARE CALIBRATION screen asks for them by these names).

Encoders and knobs

Control What it does
SELECT (encoder) Alone (0.9.2): walks the section's pages, one page a detent, as one chain, stopping at its first and last page (no levels, no zoom; see How navigation works). In the MENU: its rows, all four tabs in one chain. With a button held: HOME + SELECT the generator, EDIT + SELECT the sound dice, GLO + SELECT the tempo, SEQ / FX / ENV / LFO / SCL / ARP / SAVE + SELECT walk that section's chain from wherever you are (V10.7.66: LFO's and FX's dice went; V10.8.21: the sequence's). With step keys held on SEQ: COPY.
ALGORITHM (encoder) Selects the track from any page: T1–T6 (T1–T4 with TRACKS 4). The track is always ALGORITHM's (0.9.2: PRESETS no longer picks it on ENV, LFO, CHORD, ARP). In the MENU: the next / previous tab. With a layer held it does nothing (V10.7.66: the layer shows its MAP alone).
PRESETS (encoder) Always presets (0.9.2): the selected track's sounds (every engine's factory presets, then your user presets) on every page, the generator's too. On the SEQ pages it moves the step cursor instead (V10.7.60: turned slowly a step, fast a whole bar; the header says the bar and the step). The generator's GENRE is GENERATOR 1's KNOB 1. In the MENU and with a button held it does nothing, except EDIT held (V10.7): it jumps to the first sound of the next / previous engine, the engine's name on screen. With MENU › DISPLAY › PRESETS on MENU it opens SAVE › PRESETS instead of loading at once.
KNOB 1–4 The four cards (columns) on screen. A page that picks something picks it with KNOB 1 (the slot, the operator, the kit's sound, the row, a modulator, a macro; on SEQ › STEP it is SEQ, the track's sequence A–D). With a layer held, the layer's own knobs. Turning fast sweeps the whole range, slowly fine-tunes (MENU › CONTROL › KNOB ACCEL turns this off). In the MENU: KNOB n the setting on card n.
MASTER The output volume.

Buttons

Button Tap Hold
HOME HOME (0.9.2, as every section's button): from another section the HOME page last shown; on HOME the first page of the next group, round: ECOSYSTEM → BEING → SONG → GENERATOR, back to ECOSYSTEM (SONG: JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE; GENERATOR: the song generator, GEN until V10.6m). About 0.7 s: opens the MENU.
ENV The ENV section: from elsewhere the page last shown (at power-on ENV); inside it walks its pages: ENV → ENV DEST → ENV 2 (V10.8.35; TRACKS went in V10.8.16, STAGE in V10.8.35). (no layer)
LFO The LFO section: from elsewhere the page last shown (at power-on LFO); inside MODULATION → LFO → MOD SEQUENCE, round. (no layer since V10.7.66: the macros are the FX layer's knobs)
FX The FX section: from elsewhere the page last shown; inside, the next module: TRACK → BUSES → DELAY → REVERB → CHORUS → SLICER → PUNCH IN → MASTER (PUNCH IN · MACROS; MASTER · TAPE · EQ), round. Punch-in FX layer.
SCL The SCL section (0.9.2: its own, ARP apart): KEY → CHORD → HARMONY → SCENE, round. SCL layer: keys set the root.
EDIT The EDIT section: from elsewhere the page last shown (one memory for the synths, one each for FM6 and DRUM); inside the next group: SOUND → TONE → FOCUS → PLAY (FM6: SOUND → TONE → OPERATOR → PLAY; DRUM: KIT → SOUND → TONE). Always EDIT (0.9.2: clearing a step is SEQ + G5, renaming SAVE + C5). A step held + EDIT still clears that step's locks. EDIT layer: INIT, RECALL, DRUM-X sound mutes, SELECT the sound dice. Held + KNOB 1–4: MOMENTARY (the page under, put back when let go).
GLO The GLO section: from elsewhere the page last shown; inside MIXER → SETUP, round (at power-on MIXER; SETUP: GLOBAL · SYSTEM · KEY SPLIT · KEY SPLIT 2; V10.8.38: on MIXER a tap of OCT+ turns KNOB 4 between BPM and DJ FILT). GLO layer: mutes, solos, levels, tap tempo, UNDO.
SAVE The SAVE section: from elsewhere the page last shown, and USER or PART SLOTS come with their SAVE already picked (SAVE, OCT+, OCT+ as before); inside TOOLS → PROJECT → SOUND, round (at power-on PROJECTS; the song's pages are HOME's since V10.7.63). SAVE layer: play/store sections live; C5 NAME.
ARP The ARP section (ARP · ARP 2, one group): from elsewhere the page last shown; inside, back to ARP. A chord held + ARP during step recording still arpeggiates it. (no layer)
SEQ The SEQ section: from elsewhere the page last shown (at power-on STEP, the piano roll); inside the next group (V10.8.35): STEP → PATTERN → EUCLID → PLAYHEADS → STEP FX → AUTO → TRACK GEN → DRONE CLAY, round. SEQ EDIT (V10.8.53, on every SEQ page; was SEQ TOOLS): the steps selected, an ACTION, OCT+ does it; G5 CLR STEP.
PLAY Start / stop. Held (~0.7 s): PANIC. —
REC Arms / disarms recording on the selected track. REC layer: CLEAR, CLICK. (V10.7) Held past HOLD and let go with nothing else touched: UNDO (again: redo).
OCT− / OCT+ Keyboard octave (−3 to +3; both together: back to 0; on a DRUM track the kit stays on its keys: ratchets above, SHORT / GHOST / FLAM below, see 5). On action pages and in dialogs: OCT− = back / NO, OCT+ = do it / YES. —

The keys

27 keys from F3 to G5 (16 white, 11 black). They play the selected track. With a layer held they become that layer's shortcuts; on the DRUM grid they are steps and lanes; on the NAME screen they type.

Useful combinations

Combination Result
GLO held + PLAY RESTART: from the top at once, without stopping (internal clock).
SEQ held + PLAY (playing) (V10.8.40) RESYNC: every track from its first step on the next bar, in time, without stopping.
OCT+ tapped on GLO › MIXER (V10.8.38) KNOB 4 between BPM and DJ FILT, the master DJ FILTER.
OCT+ held + KNOB 4 on an engine's first EDIT page (V10.8.38) GAIN, 0–12 dB on the track (also on EDIT › LEVEL, V10.8.44). On FX › REVERB and FX › DLY (V10.8.44): GATE. (On EUCLID: MUTATE's EVERY; on FILTER, OCT+ held + KNOB 2: KEY TRK.)
PLAY held (~0.7 s) PANIC: ALL NOTES OFF. The transport stops and every sound ends at once: every track's voices, latched chords, arpeggios, punch-in repeats and the notes MIDI IN holds (a key or MIDI note let go afterwards does nothing; the next one plays as usual). MIDI OUT sends the note-off of every note it sent and All Notes Off (CC123) on the tracks' channels 1–6 (not with MIDI OUT OFF). For a note left hanging by a controller that lost its note-off; MIDI IN's CC120 / CC123 still do the same for their channel.
GLO held + SELECT Tempo, from any page.
GLO held + G4 UNDO the last big change (again: redo). Also a part saved over (V10.8.52) and a RESOUND.
GLO held + A4 (V10.8.54) RESOUND: new sounds for every track, the song kept (see RESOUND).
SEQ held (a SEQ page) (V10.8.53) SEQ EDIT (see SEQ EDIT); F#5 UNDO / REDO of the last edit.
REC held alone, let go (V10.7) UNDO too: held past HOLD (~0.5 s) with no key, knob, button or OCT touched; again: redo. Anything used while held keeps it the REC layer; a tap still arms recording.
SEQ held + REC CLEAR ALL SEQUENCES? — all six tracks' steps and automation, and the punch-in lane.
REC held + FX / EDIT / ENV / LFO / SCL / ARP / GLO Clears that part's automation on the selected track (GLO: the level and pan automation of all tracks; FX: also the punch-in lane). No dialog.
SAVE held + OCT+ / OCT− SAVE the music into the section playing / recall that section as stored.
HOME held + SELECT The generator (HOME's last pages, GENERATOR 1–4; see 8). On HOME › MACROS (V10.8.64): DICE MACROS.
EDIT held + SELECT The sound dice (see 8).
SEQ / FX / ENV / LFO / SCL / ARP / SAVE held + SELECT Into that section and along its chain, as SELECT inside it. (0.9.2: a button held + PRESETS no longer walks pages.)
EDIT held + PRESETS (V10.7) The first sound of the next / previous engine (its name on screen), instead of every preset one by one. Not while a momentary tweak (EDIT held + a knob turned) is in progress.
SEQ held + G5 CLR STEP: clears the cursor step and its locks (AUTO LIST: deletes the record).
SAVE held + C5 NAME: renames the slot on SAVE › USER, the part or the project on PART SLOTS / PROJECTS.
A step held (SEQ > STEP) + KNOB 1–4 A parameter lock on that step.
Step keys held (SEQ, the roll / grid) + SELECT / a step key + REC COPY those steps / PASTE them from that step (see Copy, paste and duplicate). Two or more held: they are selected (SEL 5-8, V10.8.51); + EDIT: they are cleared (V10.8.50).
OCT− + OCT+ held at power-on HARDWARE CALIBRATION.
OCT− + SAVE held at power-on (V10.8.63) The screen starts with PANEL A this time (see PANEL).
OCT− + OCT+ held 5 s while running Update mode (UBOOT), with a countdown from 2 s; let go to cancel.
A note held + OCT− / OCT+ (V10.6z4) Expression keys: OCT− held fades in a vibrato like raising a mod wheel (~200 ms), OCT+ held bends the note up along a fixed smooth curve (~300 ms) to MENU > AUDIO > OCT BEND's range (default 2 semitones); both ease back when let go. With no note held, OCT− / OCT+ change the octave as ever (OCT BEND OFF: always). Recorded as automation while recording (REC + EDIT clears it); with MIDI OUT ALL sent as CC1 and pitch bend (set the receiver's bend range to OCT BEND's). Both held on a note never starts UBOOT.

Key velocity and aftertouch (V10.6z7)

The FM-1's keys F3..C5 sit over a carbon pill whose resistance falls as you press harder (the method is Charles Vestal's, Velo, github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-velocity, GPL-3.0). JIANT reads it on every strike:

  • Velocity: how hard the key lands, in the first milliseconds after it touches. It is continuous (1..127: every strike between soft and hard gives a value between), then MENU > CONTROL > VELOCITY's curve and VEL MIN's floor. On a synth track a note waits for its strike at most 2.2 ms (V10.7.10: a hard limit, even when a reading of the key is lost), under what you can feel; on a DRUM track (the selected one, or KEY SPLIT's half that goes to one) it never waits: it plays at once with the strike as read so far, or the key's recent average. It reaches everything a key plays: the sound (the engines and the matrix's VEL), chords and strums, the arpeggiator, recording (only 127 records as an accent) and MIDI OUT. VELOCITY OFF: every key 100, as before.
  • The top row (C#5..G5) has no sensor (the FM-1 cannot read those seven keys' pressure), so it plays the average of your recent strikes (100 until you play the others). It has no aftertouch (a chord with sensed keys keeps theirs).
  • Calibration: every key is different, and each learns your own soft, normal and hard strikes as you play (VEL LEARN ON, the default: it moves slowly, a stray strike does not throw it). It starts from the factory calibration (measured on the owner's FM-1) and is kept in the settings, written half a minute after you stop playing. VEL LEARN RESET puts the factory calibration back. To see it at work: the page https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/webapp/vel/ (En vivo, Chrome, over the editor's USB link) shows each note's velocity and each key's calibration.
  • Aftertouch: with a key held, press it further down: its pressure (0..127) is the matrix's AT source (EDIT > MOD: any destination: filter, vibrato depth, level ...). New sounds (INIT SOUND, a new project) route it to the filter (slot 4, AT -> CUT +20) when that slot is free; saved projects and presets keep their own matrix. A resting finger does nothing (a dead zone), the value glides (no zipper), and lifting the key ends it. MENU > CONTROL > AFTERTOUCH sets how sensitive it is (LOW, MID, HIGH) or turns it OFF. It works with OCT− / OCT+ held too; it is recorded as automation with the expression keys and sent as channel aftertouch with MIDI OUT ALL.
  • A sound's VEL (EDIT > VOICE 2, KNOB 3; 0..100 %, every engine but DRUM): how much velocity reaches this sound. 100 % (every project, preset and song made before it) plays each note as hard as it was played; less brings every note's velocity toward 100 (50 %: a strike of 60 plays 80, one of 120 plays 110); 0 % plays every note at 100, as VELOCITY OFF does, but for this track only. It applies to every source: the keys, the sequencer's steps, the arp, the punch-in repeats and MIDI in; the matrix's VEL reads the same value. A step's ACCENT still plays 127, and HUMAN and a RATCHET's DECAY still vary the notes. Recording keeps the velocity you played, so turning VEL up later brings the dynamics back. The factory bass presets load at 0 % (a bass is better even), GENE's bass at 75 % (its composed ghost notes still softer); every other preset at 100 %. Kept with the sound (projects, user presets, songs); NRPN 80, and the web editor's VOICE group.

2. The screen

The look: COLORS (0.8.9; the only skin since V10.7.23)

From 0.8.9 to V10.7.22 MENU › DISPLAY › SKIN picked AIR, COLORS, BOTTOM or HUD. Since V10.7.23 there is no SKIN row (and no STYLE row): COLORS is the one look, on every page and every palette, with the knobs' cards outlined. Settings saved with another skin open in COLORS.

  • COLORS: the LENTE layout in the 0.6 colours. Black, near-black rounded cards with a small mark and the knob's name, each knob its colour on its value and its bar (JIANT, 0.9.5 as the 0.6: each parameter's own colour moves with its amount as heat, violet when low to yellow and cream when high, a centred one such as PAN or DETUNE cold in the middle and hot at either end; the other palettes their four knob colours), the knob you turn framed in its colour; the group's tab filled violet; the selected track's number in an orange box, a violet ▶ and a big violet BPM in the header; a near-black rounded panel; the beings in the 0.6 heat (violet spikes, red and orange rings, cream nuclei).
  • AIR, BOTTOM and HUD (the knob row on top or at the foot, the beings under everything) are gone with the SKIN row.

Values (cards, the header's BPM) are set in a rounded sans again (Inter Tight SemiBold), as in 0.6; names, tabs and the breadcrumb stay in the 5 x 7 pixel letters. MENU > LARGE keeps its big cards on top, with COLORS' tabs and colours.

Since 0.8.5 every page wears the skin of the design the owner approved (the HTML mock-up "LENTE"):

  • Header (top): one quiet line over a thin rule. At the left the play state (a grey square stopped, an orange triangle playing, violet while counting in) and the BPM (violet; orange while it changes), then BPM LOCK's lock and the REC dot (filled: the selected track armed; a ring: another track). In the middle what the page is of: T1 · ANALOG ACID (the track, its engine and its sound); on the song's pages (SAVE, ARRANGE, TOOLS, GLOBAL) P1 NAME (the project); on FX T1 in orange. At the right the octave (OCT +2, or the song row while a song plays), the load (V10.8.45: a violet number, 0–99, the share of the audio time the sound takes; it moves once the load is 3 away; five small bars before) and the battery (violet when USB powers it). Messages appear in the middle ("SAVED", "T1 CLEARED"...), sometimes with a second line.
  • Cards: the four boxes under the header are KNOB 1–4: the name small and grey on top, the value under it in white, and a thin violet bar under the value. The one you are turning lights orange, so it is the only colour on the cards. A value that is automated or locked has its name in violet; a dim card means "nothing here now". An action armed (SAVE, LOAD, ERASE, CLEAR...) is a violet-tinted card with its name violet and OCT+ as its value. The cards have no icons since 0.8.5, and nothing else does (MENU > LARGE's cards: a violet dot for a value that moves on its own; the header: "!" before a NO FILE message, a drawn lock and song disc).
  • Page name: changing page (or track) by hand shows the page's name over the footer for a moment, with the track and its engine at the right; on HOME the track's engine, "T1 HOME" small (on a lens page its breadcrumb lights up instead). The header, the cards and the graph stay in sight.
  • Granules: a few dots drift behind the panel's graph, as on HOME (LOAD FULL with ANIM ON). They move only when the panel redraws anyway (a knob, the LFO, the envelope), so they cost no CPU.
  • Panel (middle): the page's graph — the engine's creature, an envelope, the LFO running, the step grid, a list...
  • Footer: the step bars of the bar you edit (four under each card) or key hints, and under them a small grey breadcrumb: SECTION · GROUP · page and the page's place in the section's chain at the right (0.9.2; e.g. FX · DELAY · DLY 2 7/20, ENV · ENV · ENV DEST 2/3).

  • The tabs (0.9.2): under the header, the section's groups (FX: TRK · BUS · DLY · REV · CHO · SLC · PCH · MST; SEQ: STEP · PAT · EUCL · HEAD · SFX · AUTO · GEN · CLAY), the one you are on lit (filled violet), and a dot a page under each, the page shown lit. The cards under them, a taller panel, and the footer is the breadcrumb alone.

  • The small letters (since 0.8.5): the cards' names, the tabs, the breadcrumb, the header's middle words and the panels' small captions and chips are set in a crisp 5 x 7 pixel face, the mock-up's small mono capitals; values stay in the larger rounded face.

Colours work like a thermal camera: cold (indigo, violet) is little, hot (red, orange, cream, white) is a lot (0.8.9: the 0.6 ramp). Violet is what's selected, orange what's active.

HOME is the ecosystem: one creature per track, its species from its engine, its shape from its four knobs, swelling and heating up with its own audio (0.8.8: swimming free over the whole screen by themselves, as before 0.8.5; see the sections). (0.9.7) Each being wears a small face: its eyes shut on a hit, its mouth opens with its level. The selected track is drawn bigger, its number in violet, a muted one falls asleep (a dim outline, its eyes shut), a track asleep (TRACKS 4) is drawn as muted. On the MIXER, asleep tracks are greyed and say OFF.

Dialogs ask before anything destructive: OCT− NO, OCT+ YES. (0.8.5, as the mock-up) They carry the tabs NOTICE · DICE · NAME: a question is a card under a violet rule with its two buttons (YES in the accent); the sound dice (EDIT + SELECT) shows BEFORE and NOW side by side (the sound's being then and now) over a strip KEEP DICED …? · SELECT: DICE AGAIN · OCT− CANCEL · OCT+ OK; NAME has its cards CURSOR, CHAR, LEN and OCT+ SAVE / WRITE over the name, the keys' letters and the black keys' functions. (0.9.5) A question's card covers only itself, its tabs and its breadcrumb: the page stays in sight around it, still moving.

Messages (0.9.5): a message on a lens page shows as a small pill near the foot of the panel, over the page, which keeps drawing and moving behind it (the header says it as well; not over HOME's beings or a layer's map); nothing goes dark. The pill keeps clear of the page's own words: where the foot is written (AUTO LIST's rows) it sits in the nearest free rows, and on a page with no free rows it is left out and the header alone says it. The one-time teaching hints (EUCLID's "TURN A KNOB: A PATTERN", MOTION's and PUNCH's "REC + PLAY ...", each shown at most twice) are gone since V10.8.18; a page with OCT+ gestures says them in its footer instead (V10.8.54, see Big titles, the knob footer and the banners). Tapping a layer button says nothing (the "HOLD [X] QUICK" hints are gone): hold it and its layer shows itself.

Big titles, the knob footer and the banners (V10.8.53–V10.8.65)

  • Big titles (V10.8.65): a page with no picture of its own shows its name large, with what it needs under it: GLO › GLOBAL, KEY SPLIT and KEY SPLIT 2, EDIT › LEVEL (the scope lower, under the name), FX › PUNCH IN, and SEQ › DRONE CLAY, CLAY MOD, CLAY RHYTHM and CLAY TIME. HOME › LIFE says LIFE large with ON or OFF under it, HOME › MACROS says MACROS with HOME+SELECT DICE (V10.8.64). Pages with a picture stay as they were.
  • The knob footer (V10.8.65): turn a knob and the footer says it whole for a moment, the page's name first: LIFE STEREO 100 %, LFO RATE 1.24 HZ, GLOBAL BPM 121 BPM. The cards keep their short labels. Not with a step held, in the MENU or in a dialog.
  • OCT+ hints (V10.8.54): a page with OCT+ gestures says them in its footer, with the OCT+ key, for 1.5 s when you arrive and while OCT+ is held: an engine's first EDIT page HOLD: K4 GAIN, FILTER HOLD: K2 KEY TRK, REVERB and DLY HOLD: K4 GATE, EUCLID MUTATE · HOLD: K4 EVERY, PRESETS KEEP, SCENE DICE, PUNCH IN EDITOR, TRACK GEN MAKE, ARRANGE ADD ROW, TAKE GO, SYSTEM OPEN, HOME › VISUAL NEW FIGURE.
  • The count-in (V10.8.53) is one line of figures, 4 3 2 1, the beat now lit (with 2 BARS: BAR 1 OF 2).

Banners (V10.8.53–V10.8.54): every combination says what it did.

GLO + black keys 1–6 / 7–10 T3 MUTED / T3 ON, KICK MUTED / KICK ON
GLO + E4 ALL UNMUTED

VISUAL and SAVER (V10.8.56–V10.8.67)

HOME › VISUAL is BEING's second page (where ROUTES was until V10.7.66): a picture that moves with the music, on the whole screen (no header, tabs, cards or footer). It is made from JIANT FM's own graphics: FX's DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, DIST and MASTER pictures, the envelope's curve, the LFO, HOME's ecosystem, a track's being and ANIMAL's creature morphing (V10.8.67). They are deformed (warped, twisted, folded), repeated (kaleidoscope, trails, tiles) and broken (strips, gaps, tears). A kick scatters the pieces and they gather again, a snare turns the copies, the hats shiver, a note sends a ripple down the rows. Each song picks its own pictures (from the generator's seed, genre, mood and energy, or from the project's sounds); a new section, twelve kicks or ten seconds bring the next picture.

KNOB 1 KNOB 2 KNOB 3 KNOB 4
DENSITY WOBBLE PALETTE (MIXED, THERMAL, ORG/BLUE, GRN/RED, AMBER, MONO) REACT (how much it follows the sound)
  • A knob turned shows its name and value on one line at the foot for a moment. OCT+: a new figure (VISUAL #n). Any other button leaves the page as usual. The knobs are not saved.
  • It is light: a fixed budget of points, and it gives way when the sound is busy. Off its page nothing of it runs (V10.8.68). V10.8.72: every frame is drawn, and when the sound is busy each frame draws less instead (past 65 % load only the first picture, with 300 points; past 80 %, 150). Under load it moves at about 20 frames a second (10 while the load stays near 80 %), where V10.8.71 drew 3 to 7 with uneven gaps.

MENU › DISPLAY › SAVER (V10.8.56): OFF, 1 MIN, 3 MIN (default), 5 MIN, 10 MIN. After that long with no panel input the screen shows a VISUAL figure, a new one, on the whole screen, moving with the music. The first press, key or knob turn only brings the page back (it does nothing else). It does not start while the MENU is open. If SCREEN OFF comes later, the screen still goes dark at its time.

PANEL: the late-2026 screens (V10.8.63)

Some FM-1 units sold from late 2026 may carry another 1.3" screen, whose colours look washed out with the usual settings. MENU › DISPLAY › PANEL picks how the screen is set up:

  • AUTO (default): B on the units with the new flash chip, A on the others.
  • A: the screen as it always was.
  • B: the same, then the settings of the newer panel.

A change applies at once, with no restart (the screen says PANEL A or PANEL B). B is untested on the new units. If the screen stays dark or looks wrong: switch off, then hold OCT− + SAVE while you switch on. That start uses A; set PANEL back in the MENU. (OCT− + OCT+ at power-on is still the calibration.)

3. Pages and layers

The whole synth on one page: each section's button, its groups (the tabs on the screen) and its pages in the order SELECT walks them (the number in each dot is the page's n of the footer's n/N; orange, the page at power-on; dashed, a page only some engines or LOADs have), with the six rules, the held layers and the combos. Click it for the zoomable SVG (en español). It is generated from the firmware's chain tables (tools/gen_nav_map.py).

How navigation works: six rules (0.9.2)

Since 0.9.2 every section is driven the same way (the design the owner approved, the mock-up "navegación"): learn it once and every section is known. Until 0.9.1 each part was a lens of three levels with sets of knobs; the pages, their knobs, their pictures and every function are the same, only the way between them changed.

  1. SELECT walks the pages. Turning SELECT goes through all the pages of the section, in one chain, a page a detent, and stops at the first and the last. No levels, no zoom. FX: SENDS → DIST → AUTO PAN → OTT → BUSES → DLY → DLY 2 → DLY 3 → REVERB → … → EQ.
  2. The section's button: in, or on. From another section it brings you back to the page you were last on there. Already inside, it jumps to the first page of the next group (and goes round). On FX › DLY 2, FX goes to REVERB; on EDIT › FILTER, EDIT goes to FOCUS.
  3. PRESETS loads presets. The track's sounds in every section, the generator's pages too. On the SEQ pages it moves the step cursor instead (V10.7.60: turned slowly a step, fast a whole bar). The genre is GENERATOR 1's KNOB 1. In the MENU it does nothing; with MENU › DISPLAY › PRESETS on MENU it opens SAVE › PRESETS.
  4. KNOB 1 picks. When a page picks something (a slot, an operator, the kit's sound, a row, a modulator, a macro) KNOB 1 is the one that picks it. The track is always ALGORITHM's. One exception (V10.8): on SEQ › STEP KNOB 1 is SEQ, the track's sequence A–D; the step cursor is PRESETS' and the step keys'.
  5. Hold = the layer. Holding a button opens its layer of shortcuts, as before (past the HOLD time, MENU > HOLD, 0.4 s by default: the keys and knobs change function while you hold it, a map shows what each key does; a key or a knob opens it at once; let go and you are back). Held + SELECT: HOME the generator, EDIT the sound dice, GLO the tempo, the other sections walk their chain (V10.7.66: LFO's and FX's dice went). (Held + PRESETS no longer walks pages: rule 3; V10.7: EDIT held + PRESETS jumps engine to engine.)
  6. The screen says where you are. On top, the tabs are the section's groups, the one you are on lit and a dot for each of its pages. At the foot: SECTION · GROUP · page and n/N, the page's place in the chain: FX · DELAY · DLY 2 7/20. The same with every palette.
  • Each section remembers the page it was left on (EDIT one for the synths and one each for FM6 and DRUM); at power-on SEQ opens on STEP, ENV on ENV, LFO on LFO, SAVE on PROJECTS, the others on their first page.
  • SCL and ARP are two sections (until 0.9.1 one lens): SCL is KEY · CHORD · HARMONY · SCENE, ARP is ARP · ARP 2 (one group: an ARP tap inside goes back to ARP).
  • The generator is four HOME pages (GENERATOR 1–4, HOME's last group), no longer a screen of its own: the section buttons work there, OCT+ makes the piece, OCT− goes back to ECO. HOME + SELECT still opens it from anywhere.
  • SAVE from outside comes back to the SAVE page you left; USER and PART SLOTS come with their SAVE already picked, so SAVE, OCT+, OCT+ still stores the sound (or the section).
  • EDIT is always EDIT: clearing a step went to the SEQ layer (SEQ + G5, CLR STEP; on AUTO LIST it deletes the record; TIME turned to REST clears a note too) and renaming to the SAVE layer (SAVE + C5, NAME).
  • The MENU (hold HOME): SELECT walks every row (DISPLAY → CONTROL → AUDIO → SYSTEM), ALGORITHM jumps tabs, a knob changes the value, HOME closes it.
  • Some pages only appear when they apply: FM6's operator pages on an FM6 track, DRUM-X's pages on a DRUM track, MORE on ANALOG, PHASE, MATH and WHEEL, WORDS and LYRIC STEP on VOICE, SWARM's pages on an EXT track playing SWARM, and with LOAD ECO the SLICER and CHORUS pages are hidden; the chain skips them.

The sections and their chains

SELECT goes down each row from left to right; the button jumps to the next group's first page. Every page is the one it was in 0.9.1, with its knobs and its picture (the ones 0.8.5's lenses drew).

A group whose name is too wide for its tab is shortened there: ECO, GENE (HOME); OPS (FM6); PAT, EUCL, HEAD, SFX, GEN, CLAY (SEQ); TRK, BUS, DLY, REV, CHO, SLC, PCH, MST (FX); MIX (GLO); MOD, MOD SEQ (LFO); PROG (SCL's HARMONY). At power-on each section opens on its first page, but LFO on LFO and SAVE on PROJECTS.

Pages that left the chains: HOME's ROUTES (the macros' routes are FX › MACROS; HOME's MACROS came back in V10.8.64, and VISUAL took ROUTES' place in V10.8.56); ENV's TRACKS, TRACKS DEST and STAGE; GLO's LIVE (MANO, RIELES), COMPS and SYSTEM 2 (MIDI); EDIT's MORPH, RETRIG and ROTOR (one MORE page an engine), STEREO, VOICE and VOICE 2 (now PLAY); the DRUM kit's KIT 3, KIT 4, LEVELS and STEREO (their knobs on KIT 2, SOUND, SOUND 4 and FILTER); SEQ's STRETCH, BAR, PHRASES and MUTATE (NOTE came back in V10.8.38); SAVE's TIMELINE, PARTS, CLIPS and SAVE SONG AS (the song is HOME › SONG: JAM, TAKE, ARRANGE).

  • ECO: the six tracks' beings swimming free over the whole panel by themselves (0.8.8: as before 0.8.5), each swelling with its sound (a hit kicks it on), its number under it; the selected one larger, its number violet. (0.9.7, "today's being with a face") Each being is its species' spiky outline (the spikes as it sounds) in three isotherms, coloured by its own level like a thermal camera (quiet: cyan and blue; loud: red, orange and yellow; the inner lines warmer), and where its nuclei were a face: two eyes that shut on a hit, a mouth that opens with the level. A muted track's being sleeps (a dim outline, its eyes shut). (V10.6: the look up and the ring went with MUTATE.) The cytoplasm's granules drift behind them (drawn by the screen alone: nothing of the sound's time). LIFE (V10.7.62, where MACROS was until V10.8.64): KNOB 1–4 are FILTER, TIMBRE, STEREO (V10.8.64; PUMP before) and FX, how much the tracks move each other; LIFE large at the top, ON or OFF under it. STEREO pushes each track across the stereo field by its neighbours' sound (an offset on its own PAN), every other track the other way, so two tracks play apart; quiet, a track goes back to its PAN. A project's old PUMP value is now its STEREO. (V10.8.64) Every LIFE depth works as before up to 60 and then curves up: at 100 about 2.5 times as much (STEREO 100: hard left and right). MACROS (V10.8.64, ECO's third page): KNOB 1–4 are the macros M1–M4, the same four as the FX layer's knobs (one value each, shared). HOME + SELECT there is DICE MACROS: new routes for the macros on the tracks that sound, and new values for the four; one UNDO point (GLO + G4).
  • BEING: the track's being large, its four HOME knobs as organs at the corners (a gauge each, its value, a vein to the body), the sound's name under it. (0.9.4) A VOICE track shows its head, an ANIMAL track its creature, a DRUM-X track its kit of little beings there (see their pictures); (0.9.6) the other six engines theirs (a cell, a colony, worms, a swarm, a snail, a caterpillar). (ROUTES went in V10.7.66: the macros' routes are FX › PUNCH IN › MACROS.) VISUAL (V10.8.56, BEING's second page): a picture of the music on the whole screen; see VISUAL and SAVER.
  • ENV › TRACKS / TRACKS DEST: the six tracks' envelopes as tiles (the selected one tinted with its level now a dot; DEST: FILTER, PITCH and SHAPE as bars under each), the knobs the selected track's — ALGORITHM picks the track. ENV: the envelope large / ENV DEST's columns, as before. (TRACKS and TRACKS DEST went in V10.8.16; STAGE in V10.8.35: LOOP is on ENV DEST.)
  • GLO › LIVE (0.9.11; MANO and RIELES) went in V10.8.3; since V10.8.35 its live modifiers are on the black keys of SEQ › STEP FX (11).
  • GLO › MIX: the six tracks as strips (MIXER: LEVEL with the meter, PAN, MUTE, and on KNOB 4 the tempo or, after a tap of OCT+, the DJ FILTER; SENDS: each track's sends as bars, the knobs the selected track's CHORUS, DLY and REV). GLOBAL: the bar of sixteenths, as before. SYSTEM: the tracks that play as chips, LOAD's three settings (the one set lit), MIDI's route, the CPU load over the last seconds as a line.
  • SCL · ARP › KEY: the twelve notes round a circle (C on top), the scale's lit and joined, ROOT in the accent with the scale's name in the middle, QUANT and ALL TRK at the right, the scale on a keyboard under it; KNOB 1 sets ROOT. CHORD: the chord each degree of the key plays now (I–VII, as a key would play it: one note while CHORD is OFF or the voice isn't POLY). (V10.8.59) Each degree's tag names its triad, as HARMONY's PROG does (D-, E°, F), whatever CHORD's type; TYPE and VOICING are on the cards only; with CHORD off the name reads CHORD OFF. ARP / ARP 2: "MODE · RATE · OCT" and the pattern it plays over a triad (GATE the cells' length, SWING the off-beats late, PROB some left out); OFF says so.
  • LFO · MOD › MOD: the matrix as a net — the sources down the left (those a slot reads lit), a curve from each slot's source to its box D1–D4 on the right (DEST, AMT as a bar), the slot KNOB 1 picked framed with a pulse running along its curve. LFO: the wave under "RATE · WAVE" / LFO DEST: the LFO small on the left, the four amounts as rows lit by what the LFO sends now. MOD SEQ / MOD SEQ 2: the sixteen steps under their caption; KNOB 1 the step.
  • EDIT › SOUND: the engine's creature on the left (0.9.4 / 0.9.6: each engine its own, see below; alive with the sound, the page's name over it, the sound's under it), the scope in a well and all eight E parameters as chips on the right, the page's four lit. TONE: FILTER draws TYPE's response at CUT with its RES peak (LP, HP, BP, COMB), CUT a line; PLAY (VOICE and VOICE 2 until V10.7.64) the voices one a row as full as they sound, with POLY, GLIDE, UNISON and VEL; the others keep their pictures. FOCUS (new): one E parameter large as a gauge — KNOB 1 picks it (E1–E8), KNOB 2 sets it, KNOB 3 the source of the MOD slot aimed at it (turned up from OFF a free slot takes it, its DEST that parameter; back to OFF frees it), KNOB 4 that slot's AMT; E1–E8 as tabs under it.
  • GENERATOR 1–4 are the generator (as HOME held + SELECT, from any page): SELECT turns its page (left of GENERATOR 1: ARRANGE), GENERATOR 1's KNOB 1 the GENRE, OCT+ makes the piece, OCT− back to ECO, a HOME tap on to ECO.

PRESETS on any SEQ page moves the step cursor (V10.7.60: turned slowly a step, fast a whole bar; the header says the bar and the step).

The layers (hold the button)

A held layer shows its MAP over the page (0.8.9): the keyboard itself, F3 to G5, every key that does something named upright on it (light on the white keys, tinted on the black ones), the one held lit orange, the value now violet, a muted track pale, what cannot be pressed now dim, and each white key's note under it. The FX layer shows its effects as named cells instead (V10.7.77), and the punch-in held in large letters. The header names the layer in words, [GLO] SET. Since V10.7.66 the MAP is the only view: KNOBS and STATE, and ALGORITHM switching between them, are gone. The layers are FX, GLO, SCL, EDIT, SEQ (on the SEQ pages), REC and SAVE; ENV, ARP and, since V10.7.66, LFO have none.

SCL — any key sets the ROOT to its note name (the screen says ROOT D, V10.8.53). Knobs: ROOT, SCALE, ROTATE (the track's sequence played that many steps later, −32 … +32; this layer is its only knob since SEQ › STRETCH went) and PITCH (SEQ › TRACK's).

EDIT — F3 INIT (the track's sound back to its engine's own defaults (a plain INIT, not a preset), dry: every effect send at 0; FM6 the init voice, OP1 alone at full level; on DRUM the factory DRUM-X kit too), G3 RECALL (the sound as the current section stored it; on DRUM with its kit). Both ask first and leave the steps alone. On a DRUM track, black keys 1–8 mute each DRUM-X sound (BD SD CP CH OH TM RS CB; the screen says SD MUTED / SD ON). SELECT (while EDIT is held): the sound dice (0.9.9-seq2f, as before seq2e: SELECT is no sound parameter), with its KEEP / CANCEL dialog. The cards show ENG, No. and FAV; the presets themselves are browsed on PRESETS only (KNOB 2), FAV marked there (KNOB 3). The knobs are MOMENTARY (below).

EDIT's three gestures (0.9.9-seq2e):

  1. Tap EDIT (press and let go, no knob turned): the EDIT pages, as always.
  2. Hold EDIT, no knob turned: the EDIT layer above (INIT, RECALL, the DRUM-X mutes, SELECT the sound dice).
  3. Hold EDIT and turn any of KNOB 1–4: MOMENTARY. The knob edits its parameter on the page that was showing when you pressed EDIT (any page: HOME, a FILTER page, FX, DLY, ENV …), live, as a normal edit. Turn as many knobs as you like. The screen stays on that page with the values moving and MOMENTARY in the header; the layer never comes. Let go of EDIT and every parameter you touched glides back (about 30 ms, no click) to the value it had when you first touched it. Letting go never changes page. Nothing is kept: a save, a section store, a user preset or the autosave made during the hold stores the values from before, and nothing is recorded into the automation. A turn decides at once, even before the layer would show; a turn after the layer showed closes it and goes MOMENTARY. Up to 16 parameters a hold. Pages whose knobs are not plain parameters (steps, the kit's sounds, FM6's operators, lists, actions) say NOT MOMENTARY HERE. SELECT with EDIT held is always the sound dice, never MOMENTARY (a dice rolled during MOMENTARY stays, and that track's values are not put back).

SEQ EDIT (V10.8.53, on every SEQ page; it replaces SEQ TOOLS; the header says [SEQ] EDIT) — the roll (a DRUM track: its grid) with the selected steps marked on top. The actions work on the selected steps, or on the whole track when none are selected. Details and every action: SEQ EDIT.

4. Engines

Twelve engines, all synthesis, no samples: ANALOG, FM6, PHASE, MATH (LOFI until V10.6e), VOICE, WHEEL, WEST (in NOISE's place since V10.7.37), DRUM-X, ANIMAL, STRING (a plucked, struck or bowed string, and guitar feedback), ADD (additive) and EXT (external signals: the USB audio input, or SWARM, the Bluetooth around it). Any engine can go on any track. Pick them with PRESETS (one list over every engine) or with KNOB 2 (ENG) on SAVE > PRESETS. Each track's four HOME knobs are listed too.

The order (V10.6e): PRESETS, KNOB 2 (ENG) and the web editor's lists show the engines as DRUM-X, ANALOG, PHASE, FM6, VOICE, ANIMAL (the tracks at power-on, T1–T6), then MATH, WHEEL, WEST, STRING, ADD, EXT. Only the order you see changed: projects, user presets, favourites and backups name engines by their numbers, which stay, so everything saved before loads as it was. PROGRAM CHANGE keeps 0.9.8's numbers (see 14).

Smooth changes: switching a track to another engine fades the old one out (about 12 ms) and what you are holding (keys, or the notes the sequencer holds) goes on in the new engine, fading in; nothing is cut. Changing a list value (WAVE, CHIP, a type) while notes sound makes a short dip (about 3 ms) instead of a click; the notes go on.

  • GAIN on every engine (V10.8.38): on the engine's first EDIT page hold OCT+ and turn KNOB 4: its card reads GAIN, 0–12 dB clean on the track's level. OCT+ let go with nothing turned is still the keys' octave. (V10.8.44) The same GAIN is KNOB 1 of the LEVEL page, the last of EDIT's first group on every engine, with the track's LEVEL and PAN (the mixer's) beside it. WHEEL also has it on COLOR; ANALOG's and PHASE's MORE no longer do. (V10.8.49) DRUM-X's KIT 2 no longer has a GAIN of its own: LEVEL's is the one. A kit or project saved with that gain still sounds as it did.
  • ANALOG: two oscillators. WAVE: SAW, SQR, TRI, SIN, PWM, SYNC, RING, SAW3, PLS3 (V10.22: three pulses, oscillator 3 detuned the other way; MORPH sets the pulse width). Since V10.7.21 it has one page, OSC: WAVE, DETUNE, MIX and INT, oscillator 2's interval (±24 semitones); in SAW3 and PLS3 (V10.7.22) the page is WAVE, INT, INT 3 (oscillator 3's own interval, V10.39; no noise in those two WAVEs) and DETUNE. CUT and RES are on FILTER, NOISE, DRIVE (and MIX in SAW3 / PLS3) on FOCUS, MORPH and DRIFT on MORE, GAIN on LEVEL (V10.8.44). A random choice (GEN, the dice) keeps INT and INT 3 at 0, a fourth, a fifth or an octave (V10.38). Its filter is per voice.
  • FM6: a six-operator FM engine (Dexed's msfa), 32 algorithms drawn on screen, four voices per track. The knobs of its two pages, ALGO (ALG, FEEDBK, MOD, RATIO) and PATCH (SLOT, MOD ENV, VEL MOD, SPREAD), are macros over the patch. SLOT: the factory patches F1–F8, OWN (an edited or imported patch) and B1–B32 (a 32-voice DX7 bank sent from the web editor; empty slots are skipped). A voice from the editor or a B slot plays as its file has it: the macros go back to none (0.8.1). OPERATOR / OP ENV / OPERATOR 2 edit each of the six operators on the device (KNOB 1 picks the operator; then COARSE, FINE, OUTPUT / STAGE, RATE, LEVEL / MODE, DETUNE, KEY VEL); editing makes the patch the track's own (SLOT OWN), saved with the project. A bank voice you pick is copied into the track, so projects keep it even if you send another bank later. (0.9.6) Their panel is the algorithm as a colony of operators (OP ENV: the envelope with the operator riding it), every number they showed kept.
  • PHASE: phase distortion. WAVE / WAVE2: SAW, SQR, PLS, DSIN, SPLS, RSAW, RTRI, RTRP. LINE: MIX or RING. BRIGHT is how far the phase is bent, FEEDBK feeds the output back into the phase. Its pages: WAVES, SHAPE.
  • MATH (LOFI until V10.6e, its formulas alone): WAVE BYTE or FLOAT. The chip waves (PLS TRI SAW NOIS WRAM) and the STEP envelope are gone: a stored chip sound loads as ANALOG's nearest, one oscillator. Every MATH sound starts still (MOTION 0) with RESTART on, so a note plays in tune; the five FLOAT voices MATH KEYS, BASS, PAD, LEAD and BELL play at the note. Its pages: FORMULA and MOTION.
  • BYTE (bytebeat): CHIP the resolution (4BIT, 4B/2, 8BIT, 1BIT), ALGO the formula (B01–B48), VARIANT mutates it; then MOTION, GRIT, BEND, LOOP. MOTION speeds the formula's rhythm up or down (64 = as written; past 127, SYNC: its rhythm in time with the bar, the note only its pitch), GRIT is a rate crusher, BEND folds time, LOOP repeats a tiny stretch (high LOOP turns the noise into a tuned note).
  • FLOAT (floatbeat): ALGO (F01–F48, formulas made of sines) and VARIANT; since V10.7.69 CHIP's knob is ALGO B, a second formula, and BEND's is MORPH, from ALGO to ALGO B; GRIT's is FEEDBK. Hold a key: the formula plays in that key.
  • SYNC (V10.8.62), WAVE's third value: BYTE with its rhythm locked to the tempo. The formula's slow part (its rhythm, the arp's steps) runs from the song's clock; the note sets only the pitch. So every key plays the same pattern in time, just transposed (on BYTE a key an octave up plays the rhythm twice as fast). At 120 BPM the rhythm is what C4 plays on BYTE with MOTION 0; MOTION still sets its speed. Stopped, it runs free at the BPM. The preset BYTE SYNC (BYTEBEAT on SYNC) comes right after BYTEBEAT in the list. It has no PROGRAM CHANGE number (MATH's 18 stay as they were); GEN leaves it out, and the sound dice roll only BYTE or FLOAT.
  • LOOP with SYNC (V10.8.66, KNOB 8, MOTION's KNOB 4): OFF, then 4 BAR, 2 BAR, 1 BAR, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, then the usual LOOP amounts. A division restarts the formula at each window of the bar, so the pattern repeats exactly on the bar, wherever the note began. LOOP OFF, and every other WAVE, sound as before.
  • MORE page (RETRIG until V10.7.60): RESTART ON starts the formula from the top on every note.
  • MORPH (EDIT › MORE, on ANALOG and PHASE; its own page until V10.7.60): the wave slides continuously toward the next ones (on ANALOG SAW > SQR > TRI > SIN, on PHASE toward its next shape). 0 = the wave as chosen. On ANALOG the SHAPE modulation moves the morph too, so an LFO or envelope sweeps the wave. The page draws one cycle of the morphed wave and says which two waves it blends. KNOB 2 is DRIFT (0–100 %, 0 = off): each voice's pitch (up to about ±27 cents) and filter wander slowly, each in its own way, as old analog oscillators do. A chord comes alive; at high values it goes seasick.
  • VOICE: a formant voice (after klattsch): vowels, talk, breath. Its pages: VOWELS (VOWEL, VOWEL2, TALK, SHIFT) and SOURCE (BUZZ, BREATH, RESO, RAND). Since 0.8.5 it also sings words and lyrics (LANG: ES, EN, JA, RU, DE, FR, ZH, PT, GN): see VOICE: words and lyrics.
  • WHEEL: a drawbar organ. DRAWBARS: BARS (sixteen registrations), SUB, BODY, TOP. COLOR: PERC (OFF, 2ND, 3RD, 2SOFT, 3SOFT, 2SLOW, 3SLOW), CLICK (the key click), GAIN (0–12 dB; the DRIVE it replaced there is on FOCUS) and SPEED, the rotor's (OFF, SLOW, FAST). EDIT › MORE (ROTOR until V10.7.60): DEPTH (how much the rotary speaker swirls: 100 % as before, 0 % a still speaker) and DUST (0–100 %: an old organ's crackle and hiss while it plays).
  • WEST (V10.7.37, in NOISE's place): west-coast synthesis. A complex oscillator (a sine core, or a triangle with the RATIOs ending in T) phase-modulated by a second oscillator (MOD its depth, RATIO its ratio to the note: 0.5 … 8), into a wavefolder (FOLD how far it folds, SKEW asymmetric folds: even harmonics) and then a low-pass gate (GATE: 0 a low-pass alone, 64 both, 127 a level alone; DECAY how long the strike takes to die away, and past 80 a held note sustains; RES the gate's resonance). Every note is a strike: a pluck, a bongo, a bell. DUST (V10.8.28): 0 none; 1–95 white noise into the folder with the core, so it folds and passes the gate with it (fused into the timbre), and from 48 on some of it straight to the gate too (air); 96–127 is METAL: instead of the noise, a metallic tone tuned to the note (the earlier NOISE engine's META registers) into the folder with the core at half. A project or a user preset made with NOISE opens as WEST in a DUST sound.
  • DRUM: DRUM-X, see 5.
  • ANIMAL: animal calls from physical models, see ANIMAL below.

ANIMAL (0.8.3)

Animal calls built the way animals make them: a source that oscillates or strikes (a bird's syrinx, a cricket's file and scraper, a cicada's tymbal, a frog's larynx, a wing) exciting one or two resonators (the wing, the abdomen, the vocal sac, the vocal tract), driven by a slow layer of pressure, tension and rhythm. MODE picks the source; every mode reads the eight knobs its own way and the screen relabels them. The key sets the tension (the pitch, the carrier), the velocity the pressure; a note starts a call, so a sequence of notes is a sequence of calls, in tune with the rest of the music.

MODE EDIT 1 (KNOB 2..4) EDIT 2 What it models
CMOS TOUCH, COUPLE, CAP HYST, RATE, GROUP, FM the 40106 / 4093 "bird machine" (below)
PULSE CLICK, Q, SIZE DETUNE, RATE, GROUP, TEMP crickets, katydids, cicadas, frogs and toads
WHSTL PRESS, CHAOS, SIZE SWEEP, RATE, GROUP, TEMP birds' whistles (and a bat, transposed)
WING BUZZ, DRIFT, SIZE DOPPLR, RATE, GROUP, TEMP mosquito, bee, fly
GLOTT MOUTH, ROUGH, SIZE SWEEP, RATE, GROUP, AIR mammals: wolf, dog, roar, purr

The call's rhythm (every mode but CMOS): RATE is the syllable rate (0.05–40 a second); GROUP how they group: HOLD (one syllable as long as the note: a coo, a howl, a drone), TRILL (no gaps) or n+m (n syllables, then m silent ones: 3+9 is a field cricket's chirp of three); TEMP (°C, 22 as written) scales every rate the way temperature does in insects and frogs (Dolbear's law: a cricket at 30 °C chirps about 2.4 times as fast as at 14 °C). SIZE moves the whole animal up or down from the key, a semitone a step (64: as played, lower: smaller and higher; GLOTT: the vocal tract's length instead, every formant together, the pitch left alone). SWEEP is each syllable's pitch gesture: an exponential hook from below (+) or above (−) onto the note, up to two octaves; above 16 syllables a second it narrows, as a bird's trill can only be that fast and that wide (Podos).

  • CMOS: the owner's breadboard circuit, a 40106 / 4093 Schmitt-trigger chip, two big capacitors, three pots and a probe touched by hand ("a machine of bird, monkey and bug songs"). A fast RC oscillator (an octave above the key: C5 chirps at ~1.05 kHz, as in the video) charges and discharges its capacitor exponentially between two thresholds; its square wave is band-limited at the exact edge. A slow one gates it (the 4093's NAND) and its capacitor's voltage sweeps it (the 40106's FM): the exponential charge is the "hook" you hear at the start of each chirp. RATE the slow one (the chirps a second), CAP how long it charges against how long it discharges (short blips .. long sweeps), HYST its threshold window (the hook's depth; + rises onto the note, − falls onto it), FM 0 the gate alone (beeps), 20 gate and sweep (the bird), 40 the sweep alone (a siren), TOUCH the hand on the probe (faster, less regular), COUPLE a second fast oscillator coupled both ways (locking, then chaos: bugs), GROUP a third, very slow one that groups the chirps into phrases, speeding up as it goes (monkeys).
  • PULSE: an escapement. Each tooth of a cricket's file (each rib of a cicada's tymbal, each pulse of a frog's larynx) is an impulse into a resonator tuned to the key (the wing, the abdomen, the vocal sac). CLICK 100 %: one pulse a cycle of the resonance, the clockwork cricket's pure tone; lower, one pulse every 2 .. 64 cycles: clicks ringing it (a cicada's buzz, a frog's croak; at 1/2 a treefrog's two peaks an octave apart). Q: broadband (a katydid's rasp) to pure (a cricket). DETUNE: the pulses off the resonance (beats, an "anomalous" song) and jittered.
  • WHSTL: a syrinx as a Hopf oscillator: the tone is born when the air-sac PRESSure crosses a threshold and grows with it (its level ~ the square root of how far past: below the threshold it is silent, whatever the envelope), so every syllable has a real onset; the pitch rises a little with the level. CHAOS: noise in the pressure and the pitch, and a second harmonic.
  • WING: a band-limited pulse at the wingbeat with a slow random DRIFT of pitch; BUZZ narrows it (brighter); each syllable is a fly-by: louder and brighter as it comes, its pitch shifted by DOPPLR (higher coming, lower going). HOLD: a steady hover.
  • GLOTT: a glottal pulse into two formants. MOUTH closed (oo) to open (aa), and darker to brighter; ROUGH in two halves of what mammals do: period doubling (a subharmonic, F0/2) up to 50 %, then a logistic map jittering each cycle (deterministic chaos: a roar); AIR: breath noise. A purr: play low (C1–C2), ROUGH halves the pitch.

Presets (24): CMOS BIRD, CMOS TRILL, CMOS MONKEY, CMOS BUG · CRICKET, TREE CRICKT, KATYDID, CICADA, TREEFROG, TOAD, BULLFROG · CANARY, CARDINAL, DOVE, OWL, PEEPER, BAT · MOSQUITO, BEE, FLY · WOLF, DOG BARK, ROAR, PURR.
