They are set to sound right around C5 (the frogs' and mammals' an octave or two lower: BULLFROG and OWL C4, WOLF G4, ROAR C3, PURR C2).

ANIMAL came last in the PRESETS list in 0.8.3, after DRUM, so every sound before it kept its place and its PROGRAM CHANGE number; since 0.9.9 the list shows it third (DRUM-X, VOICE, ANIMAL …) and PROGRAM CHANGE still numbers it last. It costs no RAM (each voice's state fits the voice), about 7.6 KB of flash, and at most ~85 % of the heaviest engine's CPU with eight voices (GLOTT; CMOS, PULSE, WHSTL and WING about half): all eight voices on every mode.

VOICE: words and lyrics (0.8.5)

VOICE sings: syllables, words and whole lyrics, in Spanish, English and Japanese. Turn it on with EDIT > WORDS > LANG (OFF, ES, EN, JA), or pick a word preset: CANTOR ES, CANTORA ES, SINGER EN, UTA JA, WORD CHOIR, SCAT EN, ROBOT EN, WHISPER JA. LANG OFF is the VOICE you know (its vowels), note for note as before.

How it sings. Every note sings the next syllable of the lyric. Hold the note and the vowel holds; a TIE holds it on; at the release the syllable's last consonants sound (the s of "es", the n of "sun"). Legato notes glide from syllable to syllable, and a syllable whose end was not sung yet gets it quickly before the next one. With several voices every voice sings the same syllable: a choir. The lyric loops when it ends.

How it sounds (0.9.8). Like a singer: the hiss of s, sh, f comes in and goes softly (band-passed, ~6 kHz for s, under the vowel's level), the formants glide from sound to sound without corners, a note's vowel carries into the next syllable, held notes take a gentle vibrato after about 0.3 s (each voice of a choir its own), and the voice is never perfectly still (a little jitter and shimmer). A glide between notes eases out of the first and into the second (an S-curve, as long as GLIDE says); singing words, legato notes glide a little (~60 ms) even with GLIDE at 0.

EDIT > WORDS (VOICE tracks only): LANG, LYRIC, POS; OCT+ (TYPE) opens the lyric's typing screen.

LYRIC sings
TEXT your lyric (empty: W1)
W1–W16 the dice: phrases of real words from the language's bank (theme: THEME), each as long as the pattern's notes; a seed each, so W3 is always the same lyric
S1–S8 scat: pseudo-words of the language's syllables (la, ta, ri · doo, bop, yeah · ra, shi, n)

With LANG on the EDIT pages read POS THEME ARTIC SHIFT | BUZZ BREATH Q LOOP (the screen relabels them):

Knob Does
POS AUTO: each note the next syllable. 1–127: the next note sings that syllable of the lyric, whenever POS changes: lock it on a step to start a line there, or automate it
THEME the dice's words (W): LOVE, NIGHT, SEA, SKY, ANY, ROAD, DREAM, FIRE
ARTIC the consonants: 100 % crisp (full closures, bursts, hiss) .. 0 % slurred (a mumble)
SHIFT every formant up or down (−: a bigger voice, +: smaller, female, a child)
BUZZ, BREATH, Q as for the vowels: brightness, air (127: a whisper), how sharp the formants are. (0.9.8) BUZZ's top (~112–127) also steadies the voice: no vibrato, no jitter, a machine (ROBOT EN)
LOOP FREE: on through the lyric. 1, 2, 4, 8: back to its start every so many loops of the pattern (a chorus)

Writing a lyric. On the device: EDIT > WORDS, OCT+. It is the NAME screen with room for 63 characters (the field scrolls with the cursor): the keys type phone-style, KNOB 3 throws the dice (a phrase of the generator in the track's language and theme, to edit as you like), OCT+ sets it (also while playing), OCT− cancels. From the computer: the web editor's Sound tab shows a Lyric box on a VOICE track (LANG, LYRIC and the text; it turns accents and ñ into what the device reads). Each track has its own lyric, saved with the project section.

Text rules. - Spanish is read by rules, the way it is written: seseo (z and ce ci as s), ll and y as y, rr and an initial r trilled, j and ge gi as the jota, ch, qu, gu; diphthongs as one syllable (bien, cuidado). No accents needed; write ñ as NY (NINYO). - Japanese in romaji (Hepburn or kunrei), one note a mora: sakura 3, konnichiwa 5 (ko-n-ni-chi-wa), arigatou 5 (a long ou sung o-o); a doubled consonant (kitto) is a short stop, not a note. - English comes from a dictionary of ~2100 common words (from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary) with their syllables; a word it lacks is read by rough letter rules, which work less well. - A - on its own holds the vowel one more note (a melisma: A - MOR is a, a, mor). _ joins two words into one (MI_AMOR: mia-mor, the Spanish sinalefa). Punctuation and digits only separate words.

The screen. A singing VOICE's EDIT pages show the language and the source, the syllables sung, the word in large, its syllable's phonemes (the one sounding lit), your text from there on, and a vowel chart whose dot moves with the formants (F1 down, F2 across: where the tongue is), with the voicing and noise levels.

What to expect. This is formant synthesis, like a vintage speech chip that sings: vowels, s sh f, t k p, ch, m n l and the glides come through in context; b d g, v z and the English r are approximations, and intelligibility drops at very short notes (a syllable's consonants take 40–100 ms before its vowel). Spanish and Japanese read best (their spelling is regular); English depends on the dictionary.

Cost. No state per voice (the articulation is the track's); ~1 KB of RAM for the six lyrics and singers; ~42 KB of flash (the English dictionary is most of it); about +9 % CPU over VOICE's vowels, so four voices singing still cost well under ANALOG's eight.

Three engines draw their own creature (0.9.4)

Where every engine shows its being (EDIT › SOUND on the left, HOME › BEING large), three engines draw something of their own, in the same thermal line art (the colder the line, the less dense or quieter; white is hottest), moving only while the track sounds and resting in silence:

  • VOICE: the vocal tract, alive (0.9.9), seen close, the mouth and the neck filling the panel: the head's outline is a faint ghost (the brow, the nose, the lips, the chin, the throat) and the vocal tract a glowing tube of two walls, from the lips over the palate and the velum down the pharynx to the glottis, the trachea under it. It sings what you hear: the tongue (the tube's floor) rises and falls with the vowel's F1 and moves forward and back with F2, the jaw opens downward with F1, the lips round for o, u, w and sh and close for p, b, m, the lower lip touches the teeth for f and v, the tongue's tip, blade or body goes to the place of each consonant (t d n l r at the ridge, k g ng on the velum ..) and the tube narrows and heats there, with a hot mark where it closes; for m, n and ng the velum drops and a branch to the nose opens. Each glottal pulse is a bulge travelling up the tube (through the nose for m, n, ng), the vocal folds open and shut as a V with the voicing, and sound waves leave the mouth (the nose for the nasals); a jet of turbulence comes out of the constriction for s, sh, f, x and the bursts, and breath rises at the glottis for h and BREATH. The head nods a little at each vowel's onset and sways and breathes slowly with the level. With WORDS on it follows the syllable being sung (the phoneme, its formants and gains); without, VOWEL → VOWEL2 over TALK and BREATH (the nod at each note).
  • ANIMAL: a creature between a bird, an insect and a mammal. Its outline, legs, wing, antennae and eye are the same points in the three animals, mixed: MODE sets the animal (CMOS and WHSTL a bird, PULSE and WING an insect, GLOTT a mammal) and the creature metamorphoses to it in about half a second; SIZE leans it along insect – bird – mammal (well past the presets' sizes: PULSE turned up grows into a bird, GLOTT turned down into a bat-like bird), and CHAOS stirs it. With each call: the beak or jaw opens and the throat (syrinx, larynx) swells, song arcs leave the mouth, an insect's wings buzz (PULSE: stridulating, its hind leg rubbing; WING: flapping in a blur) and its abdomen's segments pulse, a mammal's ribs breathe.
  • DRUM-X: the kit as little beings ("BICHOS"), on EDIT › KIT (the first KIT page: the sound last struck named at the top right), on EDIT › SOUND 1–4 (the sound being edited lit and named) and on HOME › BEING; KIT 2, KIT 3 and X-MOD keep the colony (a being per sound in two rows). Each drum is a small being with eyes and a mouth, standing as a kit does: the kick large in the middle (its core hot orange), the snare flat on its stand, the toms on little legs (the floor tom on longer ones), the hi-hat two shells on a stand (together on CH, the top one lifting with its mouth open on OH), the crash on a long stem and the cowbell a small head over the kick (both BELL), the clap two little ones that clap together, the rim (RS) a spark on the snare's edge. On each hit the drum's being squashes, shuts its eyes and shouts (its mouth opens), as hard as the hit sounds (the lane's own envelope: the velocity, the accent) and springing back as the sound decays (DECAY); a GHOST squashes a little, a FLAM twice (its hit to come a shadow under the drum), a ratchet (x2 x4 x8) over and over.

They cost about what a being costs to draw (host: the EDIT panel ~113 µs against ~122 µs for ANALOG's being; the whole KIT screen with the kit's beings ~167 µs, as ANALOG's EDIT screen) and ~10 KB of flash for the three, 160 bytes of RAM; nothing in the sound.

Six more engines draw their own creature (0.9.6)

With 0.9.6 every engine has its own picture: ANALOG, FM6, WHEEL, NOISE, PHASE and MATH (LOFI then) draw theirs on EDIT › SOUND (on the left; the scope and the chips on the right as before; 0.9.7: with MENU › DISPLAY › SCOPE ON — OFF, the default, gives the creature the whole panel, centred, the sound's name a small caption in a corner) and on HOME › BEING (HOME's ecosystem keeps its beings), in the same thermal line art, the bichos' face shared with DRUM-X's beings, moving only while the track sounds:

  • ANALOG: a cell. Its membrane (three isotherms, the outer cold) is two cycles of the oscillators through the filter and the drive, drawn round in polar form: WAVE (and MORPH), DETUNE, MIX, NOISE and INT shape it, CUT on the note softens it, RES rings it; a SAW turns it into a pinwheel, a SQR into battlements. Where DRIVE clips the wave short spikes come out; a ring at CUT glows and spreads as much as RES; NOISE grows cilia; the two oscillators orbit inside at DETUNE's beat; the face shouts with the level and blinks on each note.
  • FM6: a colony of operators. The six operators are little beings wired as the algorithm (the 32 charts' cells and routes: carriers standing on the output's floor, modulators above, a pulse down each wire as fast as its modulator's RATIO). Each one is as big and hot as its LEVEL times its envelope now, has as many spikes as its RATIO, and the feedback operator curls a tail as long as FB. On OPERATOR and OPERATOR 2 the colony fills the panel with the operator picked lit (DETUNE makes it shimmer), "ALG 05 PAT" on the left and its frequency ("OP3 x1.50") on the right, the cards as before; on OP ENV the envelope as the patch has it (the stage KNOB 3 / 4 edit lit) and the operator's bicho rides it where its envelope is now: up the attack, along the hold, down the release.
  • WHEEL: nine tube worms, one per drawbar, as tall as its level (the registration's digits under them), each with a crown of as many tentacles as its harmonic; the rotor is a current that bends them (SLOW, FAST, its DEPTH), PERC makes its worm leap and shout, CLICK lets bubbles out of their mouths, DUST drifts motes.
  • NOISE: a swarm of protozoa round a queen: COLOR is how they walk (white: jittering in place; brown: drifting), FREQ how they swirl and how wide a ring they keep, PEAK how tight; in DUST each impulse makes some flare and jump; in LFSR and META they march in columns, one per bit of the register.
  • PHASE: a snail. The shell's chambers sit at the bent phase (even at DCW 0; as DCW rises they crowd where the phase rushes, which is what phase distortion does), coloured by the output; the foot's sole is the wave (WAVE and WAVE2 alternating); FB frays the spiral, SUB makes the outer whorl breathe, the eyestalks pull in on each note; with DETUNE or RING a little snail follows (RING: a thread between them).
  • MATH (LOFI): a caterpillar whose two skins are the last 256 samples out (the scope's own: nothing more is taken from the sound), held steps on BYTE, smooth on FLOAT. Its 8 segments are the byte's bits (the highest next to the head), each lit and lifting its legs with its bit; the antennae are tipped by the two lowest; the head is a bicho shouting with the level. On FLOAT and the chip waves (PLS TRI SAW NOIS WRAM) the same caterpillar, its skin the waveform and its segments lit by the wave's level.

Each draws into whatever rectangle it is given (EDIT's left panel, HOME's middle, the whole panel). About 14 KB of flash for the six, 1.4 KB of RAM (the pool); each page draws no dearer than ANALOG's EDIT page with its being did; nothing in the sound.

EXT › SWARM: a melody from how near you are (V10.6z6)

EXT (engine 15) plays an external signal (the audio input: see Sound from outside); its SOURCE SWARM makes the sound out of the Bluetooth around the FM-1 instead of the USB audio input. Since V10.6z6 SWARM is a melody, not only a drone: a lead voice plays notes on the tempo's grid, and how near something is decides what it plays and how it sounds. The devices heard around (MENU › SYSTEM › BLUETOOTH AIR) are still voices of their own underneath, a quieter bed.

Where the closeness comes from (V10.8.38: a tag on the picture says which, PROX n or AIR n with the number of devices heard, ALONE, or AIR OFF when nothing is heard and BLUETOOTH is not on AIR; the bar under it is the morph):

Source When How quick
PROX BLUETOOTH ON with a central (a phone, a computer) connected: the link's RSSI, ~90–130 packets a second, as the matrix's PROX reads it (its FAR / NEAR points and MIN / MAX / SPEED on MENU › SYSTEM › BLUETOOTH). Not calibrated: its own range (the highest level nearest). fast (~12 ms on top of PROX's own smoothing)
AIR BLUETOOTH AIR: the nearest device heard (the strongest advertisement), through PROX's FAR / NEAR points when they are stored, else by how far its level is over the weakest device heard. ~0.4 s (advertisements come a few times a second)
ALONE (SELF until V10.8.37) nothing heard: SWARM walks FAR … NEAR by itself, so it still plays. slow

PROX wins over AIR when both could give it. Calibrate PROX (FAR with the phone away, NEAR with it on the FM-1) and SWARM follows exactly that range.

Calibrating FAR / NEAR (MENU › SYSTEM › BLUETOOTH, OCT+ on the row while ON or AIR runs: the PROX page). (V10.6z8) OCT− (FAR) or OCT+ (NEAR) now takes the point over ~2.5 s: the screen says HOLD STILL… and the page counts HOLD STILL: FAR 0–100 %; keep the phone where it is until PROX FAR SET / PROX NEAR SET. The point is the median of those seconds, not one reading, so taking it twice at the same place gives the same point (the RSSI of advertisements is noisy: one reading could land anywhere). Leave the page while it takes and nothing is stored. With AIR the level the matrix's PROX reads is also smoothed four times longer and moves only once it changes by more than about a level and a half (a hysteresis): steady where you stand, it still follows a hand in or out within a few seconds. (SWARM's own AIR closeness keeps its ~0.4 s.)

FAR and NEAR. Like DRUM-X's patches A and B, SWARM keeps two states and plays between them: the closeness is the morph, all the time, by itself (FAR at 0, NEAR at 128, every value in between mixed). EDIT › SWARM and SWARM 2 edit them: KNOB 1 SIDE (FAR / NEAR), then that side's values:

Value What it does Factory FAR Factory NEAR
RATE the grid the lead plays on, in time with the transport (its own clock when stopped): 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32. The notes' length follows it (a pedal at 1/1, short at 1/32). 1/2 1/16
MOVE how much the melody does on its own: under 24 a pedal (the same note re-struck softly); 24–63 a neighbour and back; from 41 some rests; from 64 an arpeggio of the chord's tones (1 3 5 8 5 3) on the melody's note; from 81 octave jumps. 12 100
TONE sine → square, dark → open, past 90 a fold; the FM index. 24 100
NOISE noise into the lead, coloured by TONE (a breath when dark, a hiss when open). 30 12
MOD the modulators: vibrato (depth and rate), the FM's depth, and how much of CHAOS acts. 14 88

Projects and presets from before V10.6z6 open with the factory pair (the two states live in slots no EXT sound used).

The melody. On every step of the grid the lead looks at how the closeness changed since the last step: coming nearer, it goes up the scale; moving away, down; quick moves two degrees at once; still, MOVE decides (pedal, neighbours, the arpeggio). Its notes are in the track's ROOT / SCALE (SCL page), from C3 over two octaves (OCTAVE past half: three), turning back at the ends. With SCALE CHR it plays the blues (1 b3 3 4 b5 5 b7) and slides into b3, 3, b5, 5 and b7 from a semitone below now and then. The devices' own hits wait for the grid's next step too, so nothing comes in off the beat.

The devices. Every device heard adds modulation depth: one device mild, eight extreme. CHAOS is the ceiling: what acts is CHAOS × that depth (the chain of voices, the fold, the ring as before), so CHAOS 0 keeps SWARM clean however many phones are around. The factory SWARM presets set CHAOS 70–100. A device's own timbre (V10.6v) colours the lead too: the nearest one gives it its FM ratio and depth.

WAVE (V10.8.38; SWARM 2's KNOB 4): 0 is the sine, as before; 1–8 put a cycle of one of eight FLOAT formulas (MATH's) in its place, brought to the sine's level.

MODE >T1 … >T6 (V10.8.38; on the INPUT page, after THRU and KEYS): SWARM becomes a note source. Its own voices are silent and every hit plays a note on that track's engine instead (a DRUM track: its pads), the velocity the device's level, the length PLUCK's; the lead's line too. PROX in that track's MOD matrix can move its timbre.

The screen. EDIT 1 / 2 and the SWARM pages show the swarm (each device a square at its note, its place in the image) with a bar under it: the morph, FAR left, NEAR right.

FILTER (every engine)

EDIT > FILTER: TYPE LP, HP, BP, COMB or COMB- (V10.8.35: MS20 and LP24 are gone; a project or a preset that used them opens with LP. COMB and COMB- are a comb tuned to the note you play; CUT moves it, RES is how much it rings), CUT, RES, and KNOB 4: on ANALOG its own DRIVE, on every other engine the track's DIST. On ANALOG the filter is per voice; on MATH the filter page drives its per-voice filter; on the others it is a filter on the track that follows LFO DEST / ENV DEST FILTER.

KEY TRK (V10.8.37): hold OCT+ and turn KNOB 2 (CUT's): OFF, 50, 100 or NOTE, with a tag on the curve. At 50 and 100 the cutoff follows the newest note sounding (100: a semitone for a semitone, around C4), on every filter type, the combs included. NOTE is 100 and the cutoff, after all its modulation, lands on the semitones: with MOD SEQ on CUT you play tuned resonances (V10.8.38: on LP and HP the resonance's peak sits on the note, in tune). A track's, saved with the project, OFF by default (OFF is exactly the sound as before). OCT+ alone, on FILTER, is still the keys' octave, when let go.

COMB and COMB- (0.9.9-snd1): the comb is tuned to the newest note (CUT 64 = the note, ±32 semitones either side) and glides when CUT or the note moves (no zipper). RES is how long it rings, the same on every note: from a short colour (25 ms) up to ~9 s near self-oscillation at the top; a soft clip inside the loop keeps the ring bounded and a damping low-pass in the loop (opening with RES) lets the highs die first, like a string. COMB (positive feedback) is metallic and flanger-like; COMB- (negative) keeps only the odd harmonics: hollow, clarinet-like, at the same pitch.

CHORUS (0.9.9-snd2) is lighter: its LFO is read every 64 samples (16, 8, 4 at the fastest RATEs) and the three voices glide between, instead of three sines every sample; it sounds the same (-63 dB from before at the default).

DELAY DRIVE (0.9.9-snd2; DLY 3 KNOB 3, the page's free knob; 0–100): a soft saturation inside the delay's feedback loop. A quiet repeat comes back as it went, a loud one is rounded and pressed down, so every pass gets a little grittier and a little quieter, like a tape or a BBD driven hard; with FEEDBK past 100 it holds the runaway lower. 0 is the delay exactly as before (a project of before opens with DRIVE 0).

VOICE (every engine)

EDIT > VOICE: VOICE POLY, MONO, LEG (legato), UNI (unison); GLIDE; MODE RATE or TIME (how glide is measured); PRIO LAST, LOW, HIGH. The six tracks share a budget of 8 voices; FM6 plays at most four per track. (0.9.8) VOICE glides as a singer: an S-curve in pitch over the same time (the other engines: a straight line, as before).

5. DRUM-X

DRUM-X is a synthesized kit of eight sounds, BD SD CP CH OH TM RS CB, generated in real time.

  • (0.7.2) Eleven kits as the DRUM engine's presets: DRUM-X (the factory kit), 909 CLUB, 808 BOOM, LOFI DUST, INDUSTRIAL, ACOUSTIC, DUB ROOTS, TECHNO RAW, BREAKS, HIP HOP (V10.34: boom bap, suggests the pattern BOOM BAP), LATIN PERC (V10.7.8: bombo, timbal, llamador, a GUIRO on the closed hat, maracas, conga, clave, cowbell). Browsing one (PRESETS on HOME, the editor, a PROGRAM CHANGE) loads the whole kit into the section: the eight sounds' A and B sides, their LAYERs and SENDs, and the track's KIT knobs. Switching engines, INIT SOUND, a project load and GEN leave the section's kit as it is; DRUM-X brings the factory kit back. Edit any of them in EDIT > SOUND; the section saves the result.

  • Every sound has two sides, A and B. MORPH (KIT, KNOB 1, also on HOME) moves the whole kit between them: the knob to play live.

  • The pages go the whole kit first, then one sound, then the volumes and the stereo (0.6.58):
  • KIT (EDIT 1): MORPH, TUNE, TONE, DECAY. KIT 2 (EDIT 2): NOISE, FM ENV (FM struck with each hit and gone in a few milliseconds: a beater, a click, a metal edge on the attack, the tail clean), FOLD (a wavefolder after the envelope: a bright attack, a clean tail), DRIVE. (0.9.9-snd1) FM ENV and FEEDBK (KIT 3's and SOUND 4's) are on curves: most of the travel is musical (a beater, rubber, metal, a saw's edge growing on a sine; clean transients), the harsh noise only in the last steps (FM ENV past ~90 %, FEEDBK 14–15). The FM index is the same across the keyboard but eased on very high hits so it never folds into hiss; FEEDBK feeds back the mean of the last two samples (no fizz). Saved values keep their knob position, so a kit with FM ENV or FEEDBK up sounds cleaner than before.
  • KIT 3: BP, a band-pass on the metal sounds (the hats, the rim, the cowbell), OFF or 15 centres from about 1.5 to 9 kHz; FEEDBK, every sound's oscillator fed back into itself (OFF, 1–15: warm, growl, grit, noise); HANDS (OFF, 1–15): more people clapping on the CLAP. Each extra hand strikes a few milliseconds after the first (3 to 45 ms), at its own moment and level, thrown again on every hit: never in time with the tempo. OFF is the clap as before; a few is a small group, 15 a crowd. GLUE (0.9.9-snd1; OFF, 1–15): one knob of glue / limiting on the kit's bus, after its DRV: OFF is the kit exactly as before; the middle a gentle compression (about 2:1, fast attack, ~90 ms release) that pulls the hits together; the top a hard limit with makeup and a soft clip (loud and dense, the peaks held). Saved with the project (a project of before opens with it OFF).
  • X-MOD: RATE (OFF, 4BAR … 1/32, in time), DEPTH (how far MORPH swings), SHAPE (SINE, TRI, SAW, RAMP, S&H), RAND (each hit gets its own MORPH and a little tune).
  • FILTER: the kit's.
  • SOUND 1–4, one sound each: KNOB 1 is always SOUND (which one; striking a key also picks it).
    • SOUND: SIDE (A / B), PITCH, PMOD (how far the pitch falls; with the filter GR, SCRAPE: below).
    • SOUND 2: DECAY, NOISE, COLOR, of the side picked on SOUND (KNOB 1 shows it: "SD B").
    • SOUND 3: MODE (wave SIN / FM / MTL / BEL, noise filter LP / BP / HP / GR, "+" for snap), PM.TYPE (how the pitch moves: DECAY, LONG, NOISE, SINE), DRIVE (ON / OFF). (V10.7.8) GR, the guiro: a band-pass whose hit is a stroke over a guiro's ridges, ticks at 24–64 Hz (PITCH sets the rate). SOUND's PMOD becomes SCRAPE, the stroke's length (0–173 ms), and the hit's velocity picks long or short: an accent (127) plays the whole stroke, "rrrrip", a soft hit only its start, "chk" (the length goes with the velocity's fourth power). Any sound can take it (a scraped tom, a scraped clap); the kits of before never had it, so they sound as they did.
    • SOUND 4: LAYER (OFF, 1–15): a second oscillator at an out-of-tune interval, frequency modulated by the sound, more as it goes up: from a metal edge to a clang with no note, so the sound melts into the rhythm and stays out of the harmony (the factory kit has it on the snare, the hats and the cowbell); FEEDBK (OFF, 1–15): that sound's own (added to KIT 3's); SEND: that hit alone into one effect, OFF then CHO, DLY, REV with 16 amounts each, on one knob ("REV 75%"), on top of the track's own sends (V10.7.10: every factory kit comes with all SENDs OFF, dry; a saved project keeps its own). The dice (DICE ALL; the sound dice) set LAYER and FEEDBK boldly. Each sound with a LAYER costs a little CPU (about as FEEDBK).
  • LEVELS / LEVELS 2: the level of each sound (KICK, SNARE, CLAP, HATCL, HATOP, TOM, RIM, BELL).
  • STEREO: IMAGE (automatable) sweeps the kit through its placings in the stereo field. 0 (MONO): every sound in the middle; the first turns open it; from there each step is another placing (each sound moves on its own curve), so turn it until the image sits right. The kick stays near the middle. DRV, DIST and the FILTER work on the kit's sum, so with them the image narrows (the page draws the sounds grey).
  • KIT 3, X-MOD, LAYER, FEEDBK and SEND are saved with the section's kit.
  • Mutes: GLO held + black keys 7–10 mute the groups KICK, SNARE, HAT, PERC; EDIT held + black keys 1–8 mute each sound.
  • EDIT held + SELECT rolls the kit dice (0.9.9-seq2f, again; DRUM's presets: PRESETS). EDIT held + F3 (INIT) brings the factory kit back.

The kit in every octave (0.8.5)

The keys play the kit on the same keys at every OCT (C the kick, D the snare, F# the closed hat …); OCT now changes how they play, not which sound. The screen says it when you press OCT on a DRUM track:

OCT What a key does Recorded (REC) as the hit and its sound's mode
+3 RATCHET x2: the hit twice a step while held x4 (0.9.18: a sound's x4 spills two hits a step over two steps, as heard; was x2)
+2 REPEAT: the hit once a step while held, a roll at the step rate a hit on every step held (ON)
+1 REPEAT 1/2: the hit every other step while held (0.9.17: every OCT half as fast again; 0.9.13 had already halved them) a hit on every other step held (ON)
0 the kit as it always was none (ON)
−1 SHORT: half the decay SHORT
−2 GHOST: short, softer (~45 %), darker: a ghost note GHOST
−3 FLAM: a soft grace hit, then the hit ~20 ms later (whatever the tempo) FLAM
  • The ratchets are in time: playing, the hits fall on the step's RATCH grid (each step's start, then every step/n, swing included); stopped, every step/n of the track's DIV from the press. Letting go stops them.
  • Each sound has its own mode on each step (0.8.5): a hi-hat roll recorded onto a step that has a kick ratchets the hi-hat only, a ghost snare leaves the kick as it is. The mode applies to that sound's hit and to its notes on the step (a low tom on TM); the last hit you record on a sound sets it.
  • Live recording keeps what you played: the step you hit gets the hit and its sound's mode; hold a ratchet over several steps and every step it is held into is written too (and plays from the sequencer, so the next pass sounds exactly as you heard it). Let go before the middle of the last one and that step is put back, as with a held synth note.
  • See and edit it on SEQ > STEP (the DRUM grid): KNOB 2 picks the sound, KNOB 3 HIT goes --, ON, x2, x4, x8, SHORT, GHOST, FLAM for it on the cursor step (left back to -- takes the hit and its mode away). A sound's x2 x4 x8 spill over the steps after it as RATCH does (0.9.18: x2 a hit a step, x4 two, x8 four). The step's own RATCH (SEQ > COMP) repeats its other sounds: a sound with its own x2 / x4 / x8 or recorded ONCE is left out of it.
  • MIDI (0.8.5): notes 35–81 still play the GM drum map exactly as before. The notes around it, which used to play their octave of 36–47 plain, are now these octaves, by pitch class: 23–34 SHORT, 11–22 GHOST, 0–10 FLAM, 82–93 REPEAT 1/2, 94–105 REPEAT, 106–127 x2 (0.9.17; 84 the kick every other step, 96 the kick once a step, 108 the kick x2, 24 the kick SHORT, 114 the closed hat x2). The keys send those notes to MIDI OUT. A song or MIDI setup that sent drum notes below 35 or above 81 (a kick on 24, say) will now hear these variations: move them into 35–81 (36–47 for the kit's own) to keep the old sound. Notes stored in the steps play as before, whatever their number.
  • With the ARP on, the keys feed the arp plain (no ratchet, SHORT, GHOST or FLAM). The DRUM grid's lane keys are always the centre octave.

One kit per section, shared by every track on DRUM: while another track plays DRUM-X, browsing kit presets on a different track keeps that kit ("KIT OF T4 KEPT", 0.8.1); load kits on the drum track itself. The kit is saved with each section of a project (not with user presets — see 12).

The keys: EXTENDED (V10.6r)

(V10.6r) EDIT › KIT 4, KNOB 2 KEY MAP: EXTENDED (the default of a new DRUM-X track; a kit load keeps the track's choice) or CLASSIC (the octaves as described above). EXTENDED gives each octave a job, its name on screen when OCT changes:

OCT EXTENDED
+2 / +3 RATCH SETS: the hits ratcheted, as above
+1 FILLS: real fills, nine kinds (snare rolls from 8ths to 16ths to 32nds, tom descents, flams, unisons, 3-3-2…) in three lengths; a crash on the next downbeat
0 DRUM-X KIT: the kit as always
−1 KICK / TOM: the kick (lower keys) and the tom (upper keys) played chromatically; or, with KEY MAP on one sound (KICK … BELL), that sound chromatic over the 27 keys (BELL for cowbell melodies)
−2 FX KIT: the sounds as variants (longer, fed back, folded, noisier); V10.7.10: no delay or reverb of their own any more (the kit's SENDs and the track's FX as any hit)
−3 FLAM

A note recorded in EXTENDED plays back on the same sound at the same pitch. The sound itself: V10.6q rewrote the engine for quality (no new knobs: cleaner noise, no aliasing on FM, the 808 clap's bursts, smoother FOLD / DRIVE / FEEDBK curves) and made the cowbell a classic CMOS one (two squares at 1.47, band-passed, a click and a tail; COLOR mixes, rings and FMs it, still tonal); V10.6z9 brought back the kicks' punch (their pre-V10.6q body, NOISE off by default on a cube curve, a short knock when raised) and the bright hats. KIT 4's ACOUST is gone (V10.6o).

6. The sequencer

Each track has its own 64-step pattern with its own length (LEN), division (DIV), swing and gate, so patterns of different lengths turn against each other.

Finding your way: the SEQ chain

The sequencer's pages are one chain in eight groups, as every section: SELECT walks them a page a detent (no wrap), a SEQ tap jumps to the next group's first page (round), and the tabs at the top are the groups, STEP · PAT · EUCL · HEAD · SFX · AUTO · GEN · CLAY, the one you are on lit with a dot for each of its pages; the footer says SEQ · PATTERN · LENGTH 3/17 (18 on a VOICE track).

(V10.8.38) The chain is STEP · NOTE · LENGTH · RHYTHM · TRACK · EUCLID · MODES (MELODY on a melodic track) · PLAYHEADS · STEP FX · STEP FX 2 · AUTOMATION · AUTO LIST · LYRIC STEP · TRACK GEN · DRONE CLAY · CLAY MOD · CLAY RHYTHM · CLAY TIME. LYRIC STEP shows only on a VOICE track, TRACK GEN not on an EXT track. Gone: STRETCH (V10.8.20), MUTATE's page (V10.8.37: EVERY is on EUCLID), BAR and the PHRASES pattern loader (V10.8.38). NOTE came back in V10.8.38.

Group (tab) Pages What they do
STEP STEP · NOTE STEP: the piano roll (a DRUM track: the grid); KNOB 1 is SEQ, the track's sequence A–D. NOTE: edits the cursor step: FOCUS (the chord, or one of its notes, drawn orange), PITCH, MOVE (a step left or right) and MICRO (off the grid).
PATTERN (PAT) LENGTH · RHYTHM · TRACK LENGTH (LEN, DIV, SWING, GATE) draws the notes as long as GATE plays them and the odd steps late by SWING; steps past LEN are dark. RHYTHM: SPAN and FIT. TRACK (PITCH, CHANCE, HUMAN, REC GRID) outlines where PITCH moves the notes.
EUCLID (EUCL) EUCLID · MODES See EUCLID and MODES.
PLAYHEADS (HEAD) PLAYHEADS Its extra heads over the roll as lines while they play.
STEP FX (SFX) STEP FX · STEP FX 2 The step's two components; the white keys play components, the black keys bend the sequence live (11).
AUTO AUTOMATION · AUTO LIST · LYRIC STEP A mark under each step with a record (a lock orange, automation white); on AUTO LIST the record picked has its step framed, the cards giving its row, step, parameter and value.
TRACK GEN (GEN) TRACK GEN The generator for the selected track alone: GENRE, SEED, ROLE (a kit: BUSY), ENERGY; OCT+ makes it.
DRONE CLAY (CLAY) DRONE CLAY · CLAY MOD · CLAY RHYTHM · CLAY TIME See DRONE CLAY.

One picture (0.9.17) on the pages that work on the steps: a strip of the pattern's bars, small, on top (the one you edit tinted) and under it the bar's piano roll across the whole width: 30 semitones, the scale's rows tinted, the cursor a frame round its column, the playhead an orange line, a step with a component a small mark on top, a parameter lock a mark at the foot, a key held on the track a mark at the left of its row (a DRUM track: the grid, with its keys). The page's own marks go over it. EUCLID, TRACK GEN and DRONE CLAY draw their own pictures.

  • SEQ from another page comes back to the page you left; at power-on STEP, the piano roll.
  • PRESETS on a SEQ page moves the step cursor (V10.7.60): turned slowly a step, fast a whole bar; the header says the bar and the step. The step keys move it too.
  • SEQ held opens SEQ EDIT on every SEQ page (V10.8.53; see SEQ EDIT; G5 CLR STEP clears the cursor step; on NOTE with a note in focus, that note alone), SEQ + REC clears everything (it asks), SEQ + PLAY while it plays is RESYNC, a held step + a knob is a parameter lock (on STEP), step keys held
  • SELECT copy, a step key + REC pastes, and step keys held + EDIT clear those steps.
  • In time (V10.8.40): every track takes its place from the transport at each step it enters, so a track whose LEN or DIV changed under it (the knobs, EUCLID's STEPS, a mutation, a variation or a sequence of another length) is back on the others' grid at its next step. Left free on purpose: the live modifiers' playheads (the black keys of STEP FX), a JUMP, FIT's own clock and an odd LEN with SWING. RESYNC (SEQ held + PLAY, playing) starts every track from its first step on the next bar.

Writing steps

  • SEQ > STEP on a melodic track is a piano roll. KNOB 1 is SEQ, the track's sequence A–D (V10.8; the step cursor is PRESETS' and the step keys'), KNOB 2 transposes the step, KNOB 3 is TIME, KNOB 4 is VEL (below). A step holds up to four notes.
  • VEL (KNOB 4, V10.8; it was FLAG: – / ACC / SLD / A+S): 1–127 is the step's velocity (a step with none recorded shows 96, what it plays at). A turn stops at 127; past it, one detent each: ACC (accent, plays at 127), SLD (slide, keeps the velocity), A+S (both). Turning back down from ACC returns to VEL 127. (The DRUM grid: SEQ, LANE, HIT, ACC.)
  • A note's length (0.8.4): KNOB 3 (TIME) is one range, REST ← TIE ← NOTE → 2 ST → … → 16 ST. On a note, turning right lengthens it: the steps after it become TIEs, one a detent (the card says 3 ST, the roll draws the longer bar); a chord keeps all its notes. Turning left shortens it (its last TIEs become RESTs) down to NOTE, then the step itself becomes a TIE, then a REST, as before (a fast turn stops at NOTE first). It lengthens over RESTs and empty steps only: the next note stops it (the screen says NEXT NOTE; turn that step to TIE or clear it with SEQ + G5 to go on). At most 16 steps or LEN; near the end of the pattern it goes round to step 1, as the sequencer plays it. So any note, recorded or written, can be made longer or shorter afterwards with no REC. (On a DRUM track nothing changes: hits have no length.)
  • Step recording: on STEP, while stopped, press REC (the screen says KEYS WRITE STEPS). Play a note or a chord: it goes into the cursor step, and when you let go the cursor moves on. Not armed, the keys just play.
  • Length: while the keys are held, turn KNOB 1: the note or chord lasts that many steps (1–16, ties after it). It is written when you let go, and the cursor jumps past it. SELECT does the same (0.9.9-seq2c), the note's bar growing on the roll as you turn.
  • Cursor (0.9.9-seq2c): armed and stopped with no key held, SELECT moves the cursor a step left / right (round inside LEN) instead of walking the pages; not armed it walks the pages as everywhere. DRUM-X's grid as before.
  • Arpeggio: while the keys are held, press ARP: the chord is written as an arpeggio into the roll. KNOB 1 is now its resolution (1/16, 1/8, 1/8., 1/4: a note every 1–4 steps), KNOB 2 the order (UP, DOWN, UP-DN, RND), KNOB 3 the octaves (1–3). The screen shows the settings; letting go writes it, the cursor after it. KNOB 4 (and 2–3 without ARP) still makes parameter locks on the step.
  • SEQ held + G5 (CLR STEP, 0.9.2; until 0.9.1 an EDIT tap) clears the cursor step and its locks and moves the cursor on; on NOTE with a note in focus it deletes that note alone. Turning TIME (KNOB 3) down to REST clears the step's notes too.
  • On a DRUM track, STEP is a grid: white keys are the 16 steps of the page, black keys 1–8 pick the lane (and play it), black key 9 held is ACC (white keys then toggle accents), black keys 10 / 11 page down / up when LEN is over 16. Knobs: STEP, LANE, HIT, ACC.

Live recording

Press REC anywhere (not on STEP while stopped): the track is armed; while stopped the transport does not start: PLAY starts it (with a count-in if COUNT-IN is on). What you play is recorded into the pattern, quantized to its steps, overdubbing. Knob moves on the selected track are recorded as automation. MENU > AUDIO has the CLICK (OFF / REC / ON), CLICK LEVEL and COUNT-IN (OFF, 1 BAR, 2 BARS).

How a note is held is recorded too (V10.6z4): its length goes into the step it ends in (the step's LEN, in 1/16 of a step; a note held to the step's end, or tied, plays the track's GATE), a legato (the next key down before the last one is up) on a LEGATO / UNISON track records a SLIDE so it plays back as one gliding envelope, even when the next note came in late (MONO and POLY: the notes touch, retriggered), and the velocity is kept as played (only 127 marks an accent; 111–126 used to come back as 127). REC GRID (100 % by default) snaps where notes start, not how long they are; set it to 0 % (REC + B3) to keep your timing too. A note played in the very first moment after PLAY goes to step 1 (it went to the last step).

Pattern pages

  • STEP FX (step components v2, 0.9.9-seq2d; the pages were COMP and COMP 2 until V10.7.59): up to two per step, STEP FX the first (C1), STEP FX 2 the second (C2). Pick the step on the roll (PRESETS or a step key; a key on the DRUM grid), then SELECT to STEP FX. Every component is the same four fields: KNOB 1 ACTION, KNOB 2 LENGTH (1–32: the steps it stays on, from its own on, as the track plays them), KNOB 3 CONDITION (on which passes of the pattern it acts), KNOB 4 VALUE. On the roll a step with components shows a small mark per component on top (violet pitch, orange time, grey flow, white sound), and a thin line of the same colour over the steps its LENGTH covers. (0.9.9-gen3) The cards show every value whole, in short: ACTION as below (STUT, TRANS, RAND), LENGTH as "8 ST", CONDITION as "1:4", "!3:8", "50%", "1ST", the card's label MONO / POLY where the step is either.
  • ARP: an arpeggio over its LENGTH, replacing those steps. VALUE: NOTES (the step's chord) or SCALE (up from its lowest note), the range, ORDER (UP DN UD RND: up, down, up-down, random) and RATE beside it (16 = 1/16, 32T, x1 … x8 past 1/64, in the track's time).
  • SEQ: the note walker. Each pass of the pattern this step plays the pattern's next programmed note (pass 1 its first note, pass 2 the second …): the same notes you wrote, recombined in time. VALUE: the note it starts from, LOOP or PING (bouncing back and forth).
  • OCT+ / OCT-: the steps of its LENGTH 1–3 octaves up / down, then back.
  • RATCH: every step of its LENGTH split into x2 … x8 parts; DECAY FLAT, FADE (each softer) or RISE.
  • STUT (stutter): this step again in place of the next ones (EVERY 1 … 4 steps; the steps between silent).
  • MUTE: its LENGTH of steps silent (CUT: what the track sounds is cut first).
  • TRIG (KNOB 1's last): an Elektron-style trig condition, MUTE the other way round: its LENGTH of steps play only on the passes its CONDITION holds, and are silent on the others (no CUT, no VALUE). The card shows the CONDITION as any: "4:4" plays on pass 4 of every 4. Example: play only on the 4th pass: TRIG 4:4. After it, PRE reads its condition (true on the passes it played); C2 ELSE over a C1 TRIG acts on the passes it plays (it did not mute), a C2 TRIG ELSE plays the passes C1 did not act. Its mark is MUTE's (grey). Also on GLO > COMPS. It is saved as a MUTE with a VALUE of its own: firmware before TRIG loads it as a MUTE CUT with the condition as it is (the opposite passes).
  • TRANS (transpose): the notes moved MOVE degrees (−7 … +7, in the scale). RANGE FIX: whenever its condition holds; RANGE 2 … 16: it adds a MOVE each pass its condition holds, round RANGE places (back to 0), acting every pass.
  • RAND: each note up or down the scale at random, up to 1–7 degrees.
  • LOCK: the step's parameter locks (hold the step and turn, see Parameter locks) only when its condition holds, held over its LENGTH. VALUE shows how many locks the step has.
  • RAMP (V10.6v, in JUMP's place: a JUMP of before is dropped): the step's first parameter lock is the parameter and its target; the value glides there FROM KNOB (the knob's value) or OPP (the other end of its range), over 1–32 steps or 1–16 bars, along a CURVE: LIN, EXP, LOG, S, STEPS, ZIGZAG. It never restarts itself while it runs, and glides back to the knob at its end and on STOP. No lock on the step: nothing. Not on GLO > COMPS.
  • SHIFT: the steps after it played from another place, round within the pattern (a playback map: the steps themselves never move), on the passes its condition picks. CHORD: the step's note played as a chord.
  • SOUND (a DRUM track): SHORT, GHOST or FLAM hits. BEND (kept from before): the note glides ±12 semitones.
  • CONDITION: ALWAYS; 25 / 50 / 75 %; 1ST / !1ST (the first pass after PLAY); FILL / !FILL (FX held); PRE / !PRE (the track's last condition held / did not); NEI / !NEI (the same, the track before); N:M / !N:M (pass N of every M, M up to 16). Passes are counted per track, per lap of its pattern.
  • MONO / POLY: C2's condition ELSE makes the step MONO: one component acts, C1 if its condition holds, else C2 (the card's label says MONO). Any other condition on C2 is POLY: both act, C1 on the step, C2 over the result.
  • Example: four notes on steps 1 5 9 13, each with C1 MUTE at !1:4, !2:4, !3:4, !4:4 (one note a bar), and on step 1 C2 TRANSP +1 RANGE 4 at 1:4, LENGTH 16: a 16-bar melody, every bar different, then again.
  • Projects before 0.9.9-seq2d load migrated: ARP NOTES / SCALE an ARP over the TIEs after it, ARP SEQ the SEQ walker, TRIG a MUTE with the opposite condition, FILL MUTE !FILL, EVERY each component's condition, OCT OCT+ / OCT- (ALT: both slots, 1:2 and 2:2), TONAL a FIX TRANSP to the loop's end, WALK / CLIMB an adding TRANSP, ECHO RATCH (DECAY DOWN; EVEN FLAT), PULSE STUTTER over the empty steps, JUMP / REV JUMP, KILL MUTE CUT, TOUCH SOUND. Not quite the same: KILL's step is now silent; ARP SEQ walks instead of arpeggiating; EVERY beside a TRIG, FILL, alternating OCT or a WALK at a rate is dropped; OCT RND becomes 50 %; WALK / CLIMB UP-DN and RND go UP, CLIMB moves 7 degrees (an octave on a seven-note scale); JUMP x2 jumps once a pass. Saved again, the project is v2 (firmware before seq2d refuses it). The step's own CHANCE and RATCH stay on the CHANCE page.
  • Global components (0.9.9-seq2f; gone in V10.8.21 with its page, GLO > COMPS; what follows is how it was): GLO > COMPS (GLO's third tab, after MIX since V10.37) is a lane of 16 steps on the transport's 1/16 (one bar, looping) whose components act on several tracks at once. The white keys pick its step, KNOB 1–4 are ACTION, LENGTH, CONDITION, VALUE as on COMP (actions MUTE, TRIG, STUTTER, OCT+ / OCT−, RATCH, TRANSP, ARP on each track's own notes, RANDOM; conditions as the tracks', without NEI and ELSE; the passes are the bars since PLAY, the lane has its own PRE and its own dice). Black keys 1–6 turn the tracks it applies to on and off (the roll shows them as small marks under each step); COMPS 2: STEP, TRACK, that track ON / OFF, and MODE: POLY (the default) the global transforms the step first and the track's C1 / C2 run on the result (a track's ARP inside a global STUTTER); MONO while a global acts on a track, that track's own components do not. One component a step; its LENGTH counts global steps. An empty lane changes nothing. Example: step 1 STUTTER LENGTH 2 at 4:4 on all tracks, step 3 MUTE LENGTH 14 at 8:8 on T1 alone: every fourth bar stutters, bar 8 drops the drums. The lane is saved with the project (and in each section's slot); projects before seq2f load with it empty.
  • A long chord slide (0.6.83): the glide into a chord lasts as long as that chord, its TIEs included; GLIDE sets how much of it (127: all of it). A chord held over TIEs on slow steps (e.g. DIV 1/4 at 120 BPM: ten steps, 5 s) slides that slowly and smoothly; new notes fade in as they glide.
  • LENGTH (the PATTERN group's first page; PATTERN until V10.7): LEN (1–64), DIV, SWING, GATE — the pattern's length, its step's note value, its swing and the length of every note (a step's own length: STEP's TIE, or MICRO for its start). GATE is 100 % for new tracks (V10.6z4; INIT, a new project, power-on; was 50 %): notes play their whole step and retrigger the next one (a SLIDE or TIE makes them legato). Projects and user presets keep the GATE they were saved with (one saved at 50 % loads 50 %); clearing steps leaves GATE as it is; GEN sets its own per part.
  • Moving a note or a chord that came in early or late: NOTE, KNOB 1 FOCUS on the step, KNOB 3 MOVE moves it sideways a step at a time (FOCUS ALL: the whole chord with its TIEs; one note focused: that note alone).
  • STRETCH lost its page in V10.8.20. STRETCH, SQUEEZE, REPEAT and NUDGE are back in SEQ EDIT (V10.8.49; hold SEQ, see SEQ EDIT), on the selected steps or the whole track. The SCL layer's KNOB 3 is still ROTATE (−32 … +32: the sequence read from another step, without moving the steps), and a step's micro timing is NOTE's MICRO.
  • MICRO (0.6.92, NOTE's KNOB 4; it was the TIMING page's OFFSET): the focused step's own place off the grid, in 64ths of a step (0.9.1; it was sixteenths), from −32/64 (half a step early) to +31/64 (late): a 64th of a 1/16 step is about 2 ms at 120 BPM. A 64th a detent (turned faster, more: knob acceleration); the card shows +5/64; 0 puts it back on the grid. Early steps really sound early: the step before ends that much sooner and the grid is kept. The piano roll draws the notes where they play. A chord shares its step's offset; moving, stretching or repeating steps keeps it; saved with the project. REC GRID (TRACK's KNOB 4) is the recording quantize that writes it: 100 % (the default) live recording snaps to the grid; lower, the step keeps that much of where you played it (0 %: all of it, to the nearest 64th), early or late; 50 % half way to the grid. Projects from before 0.9.1 play exactly as they did (their sixteenths are 4/64 each). A project saved with 64ths still loads on older firmware, which plays each step at the sixteenth at or before its 64ths (up to 3/64 sooner).
  • TRACK (0.6.92; it was SHIFT + HUMAN): the whole track's settings. PITCH (±24 semitones; not on drums). CHANCE: the whole track's chance, 100 % plays every step as written, lower thins it out (each step's own chance, from the dice or the editor, scaled). HUMAN (one amount, 0–100 %): the track plays like a person, each note a little different every time round, the steps staying as written — its velocity up or down at random (up to ±50 at 100 %), its start a little late (up to 40 ms, never more than a third of the step, never early; a chord's notes stay together, a STRUM keeps its spacing), its length longer or shorter (up to ±40 %), and its envelope's DECAY and RELEASE a little longer or shorter (up to ±20). 0 % plays exactly as written (the default). Kept when you change the sound; automatable. A project saved with the old VEL / TIME / GATE loads with the smallest of the three as its HUMAN. REC GRID: see MICRO. The old C.LEN (the components as a lane of their own length) is gone: components live on their steps, EVERY says how often they play.
  • AUTOMATION: PLAY turns the track's automation on or off, EVENT and LOCK count the records, CLEAR erases them (OCT+, with a dialog). The automation is what you record by turning a knob while REC is on and the track plays (a value that moves along the pattern), and the parameter locks (a value a step, see below): this page shows how many of each the track holds and whether they play; the page's hint says so. AUTO LIST is where to see and edit each one.
  • AUTO LIST: every automation event and lock as a list. KNOB 1 the row, 2 the step, 3 the parameter, 4 the value.
  • EUCLID and MODES (V10.6): a euclidean pattern written live from four knobs, and four amounts that add to it. See EUCLID and MODES below.
  • PLAYHEADS (its own group; it was FUGUE), after the Fugue Machine: three more playheads (heads 2, 3, 4) read the same steps as the track's sequencer. KNOB 1 HEAD picks one, KNOB 2 RATE (OFF, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, x1, 3/2, x2, x3, x4 of the track's), KNOB 3 DIR (FWD, REV, PING, RND), KNOB 4 INTVL, its interval in degrees of the scale (−14 to +14; a drum track keeps its lanes). A head plays each step's notes with the step's velocity, accent and chance and the track's GATE (no components, locks or ratchets: those are the sequencer's): canons, counterpoint, patterns phasing against themselves. The page draws the steps, the sequencer's playhead and each head where it is. Saved with the section; the heads start and stop with the transport.
  • AUTO LIST: on + ADD LOCK, OCT+ adds a lock; on a record, OCT+ switches it between LOCK and AUTO; SEQ + G5 (DEL REC; until 0.9.1 EDIT) deletes it.

EUCLID and MODES (V10.6)

Under the EUCLID (EUCL) tab of the SEQ chain, after TRACK, there are three pages: EUCLID writes the selected track's pattern as a euclidean rhythm, MODES (named MELODY on a melodic track) adds to it, and MUTATE (V10.8.35; without a page of its own since V10.8.37) makes it change by itself every few bars.

EUCLID in one minute

Drums (a DRUM-X track):

  1. Pick the track with ALGORITHM, press SEQ and turn SELECT to EUCLID (or tap SEQ until the EUCL tab lights).
  2. KNOB 4 LANE starts on ALL: turn KNOB 1 DENSITY (1–8) for a whole kit, KNOB 2 STEPS and KNOB 3 ROTATE for its length and groove.
  3. To tweak one sound, KNOB 4 to its lane (BD SD CP CH OH TM RS CB): HITS, STEPS and ROTATE now write that lane only.
  4. SELECT one detent right, MODES: ACCENT, GHOST, RATCHET, VARY.
  5. On MODES, OCT+ a new variation, OCT− the one before. On EUCLID (V10.8.35), OCT+ mutates the pattern now and OCT− goes back to what the knobs dialled. To undo: GLO + G4, or hold REC alone and let go.

Melodic (any other track):

  1. Set the key first on SCL (ROOT, a SCALE other than CHR): the screen says SCL. Or leave it: EUCLID finds the key of the other tracks (FROM Tn), else picks one (NEW KEY).
  2. SEQ › EUCLID: KNOB 1 HITS (exactly that many notes), KNOB 2 STEPS, KNOB 3 ROTATE, KNOB 4 ROLE (V10.8.35): what the track plays, MELODY, CHORDS, BASS or ARP.
  3. MELODY (a melodic track's MODES page): CONTOUR (the melody's shape: WALK, UP, DOWN, ARCH, WAVE, LEAP, RANDOM), RANGE (2–15 notes), MOTIF (OFF, 2, 3, 4, 8: a motif repeated as a sequence) and VARY.
  4. OCT+ / OCT− and the undo as above. Stop a song first: while a song plays the page says SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT.
Page Track KNOB 1 KNOB 2 KNOB 3 KNOB 4
EUCLID DRUM-X, LANE ALL (V10.7) DENSITY (1–8) STEPS (2–64) ROTATE LANE (ALL BD SD CP CH OH TM RS CB)
EUCLID DRUM-X, one lane HITS STEPS (2–64) ROTATE LANE
EUCLID melodic HITS STEPS (2–64) ROTATE ROLE (MELODY CHORDS BASS ARP; V10.8.35)
MODES DRUM-X ACCENT GHOST RATCHET VARY
MELODY (MODES on a melodic track) melodic CONTOUR (WALK UP DOWN ARCH WAVE LEAP RANDOM) RANGE (2–15) MOTIF (OFF 2 3 4 8) VARY (0–100)
EUCLID, with OCT+ held (V10.8.37) any — — — MUTATE's EVERY (OFF, 1, 2, 4, 8 bars)
  • The picture (V10.8.35): one ring of dots, the cycle of STEPS at the turn playing: the hits in the track's colour (an accent larger), the step playing white, and ROTATE's mark outside its first step. On DRUM-X it shows the lane picked (ALL: a step any lane hits). The earlier picture's concentric lanes, their list, the roll and VARY's turns are gone.
  • HITS, STEPS, ROTATE: the hits spread as evenly as the steps allow (a euclidean rhythm), ROTATE turns them round. On DRUM-X each of the eight sounds has its own HITS, STEPS and ROTATE (LANE picks the one the knobs edit); the pattern's length is their least common length, up to 64.
  • LANE on DRUM-X (V10.7): nine values, ALL (the default) then BD SD CP CH OH TM RS CB. Turning LANE itself writes nothing.
  • ALL: KNOB 1 is DENSITY (1–8, default 4) instead of HITS, and DENSITY, STEPS and ROTATE write a whole kit that plays: a kick, the snare on the backbeat (steps 5 and 13 of 16), closed hats (the open hat chokes the closed one), and as density rises sparser clap, open hat, tom, rim and bell. ROTATE turns the kick and the percussion (the groove); the snare and the hats stay. Each density sets every lane's HITS / STEPS / ROTATE, so picking a lane afterwards shows those values.
  • One lane: HITS, STEPS and ROTATE (and MODES, OCT+ / OCT−) write only that lane; the other lanes stay exactly as they were (if the lane's STEPS make the pattern longer, least common multiple up to 64, the others repeat).
  • MODES: four amounts (0 = off) that add to what is generated. DRUM-X: ACCENT (a second euclid, of accents), GHOST (soft hits between), RATCHET (some hits x2 / x4), VARY. Melodic (the page is named MELODY): CONTOUR (WALK, UP, DOWN, ARCH, WAVE, LEAP, RANDOM), RANGE (2–15 notes), MOTIF (OFF, 2, 3, 4, 8: repeated as a sequence) and VARY.
  • ROLE (V10.7.67; on EUCLID's KNOB 4 since V10.8.35): MELODY, CHORDS, BASS or ARP, on the harmony the other melodic tracks play, bar by bar; else the key's (SCL › HARMONY moves it).
  • VARY loosens the even grid: some hits move one to three steps (towards the offbeat, more in the second half, so it answers the first); on a melodic track, notes held over the gap after them. (V10.7: VARY only moves hits, it no longer adds a pickup or leaves a hit out, so HITS is exactly the number of hits / notes that sound: HITS 3, three hits.)
  • VARY in turns (V10.16): with VARY above 0 the pattern is four turns of the cycle (STEPS 16: 64 steps; as many as fit in 64), each varied anew, A A' A'' B: the first close to the even grid, the middle ones by VARY, the last the most (on DRUM-X its end gets rolls on the snare and hats). On a melodic track the later turns answer the first one's motif: some notes kept, some new, by VARY. HITS stays exact in every turn. VARY 0: one turn, as before.
  • VARY in two halves (V10.28): 0 to 50 varies the current sequence without adding bars (one turn; each value a different variation, 50 the most moved); 51 to 100 brings in the four parts A A' A'' B, further apart the higher.
  • All at 0 by default (V10.28): EUCLID starts with no HITS (DRUM-X: DENSITY 0), MODES and VARY at 0, to build from nothing.
  • When the track already has a sequence (recorded, edited, or a generator song; not an untouched factory pattern), EUCLID transforms it with the same notes: VARY moves its hits and keeps its held notes. Turning HITS, STEPS or ROTATE switches to the euclidean rhythm but still uses your notes (the screen says YOUR SEQ / YOUR NOTES). On DRUM-X only the lanes the sequence had.
  • EUCLID is reversible (V10.31): it keeps your whole sequence (notes, chords, velocities, components, micro timing) and gives it back as it was when everything is at rest again (VARY and MODES 0, your own rhythm) or when HITS / DENSITY go to 0 (YOUR SEQUENCE BACK). The whole copy is the last track EUCLID took; for another track taken earlier, its rhythm and notes come back.
  • A melodic track's notes: inside the track's SCL (ROOT / SCALE) when it is set (the screen says SCL); else in the key the other tracks' notes fit best (FROM Tn); else a new scale and root (NEW KEY). The melody keeps the register the track had at the first turn (an empty track: around C4).
  • Live: turning a knob writes the track's whole pattern again, at once (its automation stays). A new gesture after two seconds is an UNDO point (GLO + G4). On MODES / MELODY, OCT+ is a new variation (NEW VARIATION: the same settings, new notes and details) and OCT− the one before (VARIATION BEFORE). On EUCLID (V10.8.35), OCT+ mutates when let go (MUTATED) and OCT− goes back to the anchor (ANCHOR). While a song plays the page says SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT.
  • The EUCLID and MODES settings live in RAM for the session; the pattern itself is saved with the project like any pattern.

MUTATE (V10.16; no page since V10.8.37)

MUTATE was removed in V10.8.20, came back compact in V10.8.35, and since V10.8.37 has no page of its own: it lives on EUCLID.

On SEQ › EUCLID, hold OCT+ and turn KNOB 4: you pick EVERY — OFF, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars. EUCLID's picture shows it as a tag ("EVERY 4"; nothing when OFF). With EVERY on and the transport playing, that track's EUCLID pattern mutates by itself every so many bars: the change is worked out in the last beat and the new pattern comes in on the next bar.

  • The anchor is what you dialled with the knobs of EUCLID and MODES / MELODY (each time you turn one, that is the anchor). Every mutation starts from the anchor, not from the mutation before: the pattern orbits what you built and never drifts far.
  • What changes: always a new seed (on a melody, some of the anchor's notes crossed with new ones), and by chance HITS (DENSITY), ROTATE and the amounts of MODES / MELODY. How far: as far as VARY says (a quarter at least). On DRUM-X with a lane picked on LANE, that lane mutates.
  • By hand: on EUCLID, OCT+ alone (when let go) makes a mutation (MUTATED) and OCT− goes back to the anchor (ANCHOR).
  • It does not mutate while a song plays (ARRANGE's chain); stopped, it starts from the top again.
  • V10.16's settings that are gone: AMOUNT, MODE and WHAT, and its page's picture. Old projects open all the same.

DRONE CLAY (SEQ › CLAY, V10.8.21)

A sequencer per track, from JIANT BYTE: a very low drone in whatever voice the track has, and four modulators that strike gestures on any parameter of the sound, each at its own rhythm. Four pages under SEQ's CLAY tab (V10.8.27):

Page KNOB 1 KNOB 2 KNOB 3 KNOB 4
DRONE CLAY CLAY (OFF / ON) DRONE (the note: the track's root in octave 0–3) PITCH (−24 … +36 semitones) RATE (HOLD, 1/64 … 4BAR, dotted, triplets, 1/5 1/10 1/20 1/7 1/14 1/28)
CLAY MOD MOD (1–4) DEST SHAPE AMOUNT
CLAY RHYTHM MOD (1–4) RATE (1/64 … 4BAR…) EUCLID DECAY
CLAY TIME RUN (SONG, FREE, SONG NOKEY, FREE NOKEY) SEED — —
  • The drone: a very low note (C0 to C3 on the track's ROOT) that is held. RATE HOLD holds it and never strikes it again (V10.8.30); any other RATE strikes it again on each step of that value, with the transport. On a DRUM track the drone is the kit's kick.
  • The modulators: KNOB 1 MOD picks which of the four the other knobs edit (the same one on CLAY MOD and CLAY RHYTHM). DEST is where it goes (OFF, PITCH, CUTOFF, SHAPE, VOLUME, PAN, DIST, CHORUS, DELAY, REVERB, LFO RATE, VIBRATO, the engine's eight EDIT knobs by name, VOICE CUT, LEVEL), SHAPE the gesture it strikes, AMOUNT how much. On CLAY RHYTHM, RATE is that modulator's own grid (V10.8.27), EUCLID the steps of that grid it strikes on ("--" none, FUSE two rhythms drawn from SEED and joined, 1/1 every step, then 1/4 … 7/8, 3/16 … 9/16, 5/12, 7/12 and the polyrhythms 2/5 … 5/13) and DECAY how long each strike lasts before it lets go.
  • The shapes (SHAPE): the hits first (KICK, SNARE, HAT, OPEN HAT, CLAP, RIM, TOM, ZAP, BITHAT, NOISE DN, SWELL, CRASH), then the tables (SINE, S&H, DRIFT, SPRING, STAIRS, BOUNCE…), the gestures (RAMP UP, RAMP DN, TRI, GATE, ENV UP, ENV DN, RISER, STUTTER…), the notes (ARP UP / DN / UPDN / RND, CHORD m, CHORD M, SUS4, m7, CLUSTER, +OCT, +5TH, GLIDE DN: real notes on the scale, two octaves over the drone) and FM x1/2 … x7. The hits are a drum on any engine (V10.8.27); on a DRUM track they play the kit's pads.
  • AMOUNT 0 strikes nothing (V10.8.30): a modulator at AMOUNT 0 does nothing, and does not re-strike the drone.
  • The bars (V10.8.29): under the scope, a thin bar a modulator runs from the middle to what it adds right now; the bar of the MOD the knobs edit is in the track's colour. A modulator without a DEST has no bar.
  • RUN: SONG runs while the transport plays; FREE runs always, stopped too. SEED changes the variation (the FUSE rhythms).
  • The keys (V10.8.31): with CLAY ON, while the drone runs, the white keys (the first twelve, F3 to C5) play no notes: they strike a gesture on the MOD picked, as hard as you play, for as long as its DECAY says. OCT− and OCT+ pick the group: 0 the hits, +1 the tables, +2 the gestures, −1 the notes, −2 the FM ones. The last seven keys (C#5 to G5) pick the drone's degree on the track's scale. The other black keys do nothing. On a DRUM track the whites are the kit's pads. For the keys to play notes as usual, set RUN to SONG NOKEY or FREE NOKEY.
  • In MONO / LEGATO the drone gives the voice to the steps; a punch-in on time or pitch restarts it from its first hit. Saved with the project.

Parameter locks

On SEQ > STEP (the BAR group), hold a step (a grid key, or the note being entered on the roll) and turn a knob: that step gets its own value of the parameter that knob edits on the sound page you visited last. Tap EDIT while holding the step to clear its locks. (V10.8.50) Step keys held on the roll or the grid (the track not armed) + EDIT clear those steps whole: notes, components and locks (CLEAR 6-7); one UNDO point. Automation events and locks share 64 records per section (all tracks together); when they run out the screen says AUTOMATION FULL. (V10.5) What you record is thinned so far more fits: at the stop (and while recording, once over 56 are used) each knob's curve keeps only the records it needs, within 1/32 of the knob's range. A stretch where the value stays put becomes one record that holds it; a stretch that moves steadily becomes one RAMP record, which glides there step by step from the record before (SEQ › AUTO LIST shows it as RAMP; the step component RAMP is another thing, see COMP).

SEQ EDIT (SEQ held, V10.8.53)

Hold SEQ on any SEQ page (STEP, NOTE, LENGTH, EUCLID …): the screen becomes SEQ EDIT (the header says [SEQ] EDIT). It replaces the SEQ TOOLS of V10.8.48. It shows the selected track's roll (a DRUM track: its grid), the selected steps marked by a bar on top. Every action works on the selected steps; with no selection, on the whole track (steps 1 to LEN). Let go of SEQ and you are back on your page. While a song plays (not the loop) it says SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT.

The knobs (while SEQ is held)

Knob Card Does
KNOB 1 START (after A3: MOVE) the selection's first step (MOVE: the whole selection slides, its width kept)
KNOB 2 END (after A3: WIDTH) its last step (WIDTH: how many steps)
KNOB 3 ACTION the action, from the list below
KNOB 4 BY, AMOUNT, 64THS or MODE the action's amount (turning ACTION sets its default)

With no selection KNOB 1 and KNOB 2 read ALL; turn one of them to start a selection. A3 switches them between START / END and MOVE / WIDTH. The selection belongs to the track: it stays when you let go of SEQ, change page or change track, until you clear it.

Selecting with the keys - B3, C4, D4, E4: bar 1, 2, 3 or 4 (steps 1–16, 17–32 …; past LEN: NO SUCH BAR). - G3 or OCT−: no selection (ALL STEPS): the actions work on the whole track again. - Without SEQ held, on the roll: hold two or more step keys (the screen says SEL 5-8). One key alone clears it.

Doing it - D5 or OCT+ does the ACTION. The screen says what and where: STRETCH x2 5-8, TRANSP +3 1-16, GEN TECHNO 5-8 #1791. - F#5 is UNDO of the last edit (UNDO STRETCH x2 5-8); again: REDO. Each action is one UNDO point, so GLO + G4 takes it back too.

Keys that act at once (no ACTION needed)

Key Does
F3 CLEAR the selected steps (none: the whole track's steps; its held notes end)
F4 CLR AUTO: the automation and locks of the selected steps (none: the whole track's); the steps stay
C5 DUP: the selection copied right after itself, LEN grown (64 at most: NO ROOM); the copy is then selected
E5 COPY the selection (none: steps 1 to LEN), into the clipboard of Copy, paste and duplicate
F5 PASTE onto the selection's first step; with no selection it replaces the whole sequence, LEN the copy's (as PASTE SEQ did)
G5 CLR STEP: the cursor step and its locks (NOTE with a note in focus: that note; AUTO LIST: the row's record)
C#5 / D#5 NUDGE < / >: the notes 4/64 of a step earlier / later together (NUDGE +8/64)
G4 · A4 · B4 DRUM: the lane's CLEAR, REVERSE, FILL (every step, every 2nd, every 4th, off) on the lane picked with black keys 1–8 (LANE SD)
REC CLEAR ALL SEQUENCES? (all six tracks; it asks)
PLAY (playing) RESYNC

The actions (KNOB 3; KNOB 4 sets the amount)

ACTION KNOB 4 Does
STRETCH x2–x4 the steps that many times longer; the steps after them move along and LEN grows (64 at most); held notes stay held, locks and automation go with their steps
SQUEEZE /2–/4 the steps that many times shorter (of each group the first one that plays); LEN shrinks; TOO SHORT when there is nothing to squeeze
REPEAT x2–x8, FILL the steps played that many times in a row, with their locks (FILL: as many as fit in 64 steps)
NUDGE −32 … +31 (64ths) every note's MICRO moved by the same amount, each held at MICRO's range
ROTATE −15 … +15 the steps turned round inside the selection
SHIFT −16 … +16 the selection slid along the track, the steps it passes go round it (AT THE EDGE when it cannot)
REVERSE — the steps backwards (a note keeps its TIEs after it)
DUP · COPY — as C5 and E5
PASTE OVER, INSERT as F5; INSERT moves the steps from there on along, LEN grown
CLEAR · CLR AUTO · CLR STEP — as F3, F4 and G5
VEL RND 5–100 % each note's velocity varied by up to that much
NOTE RND 1–7 each note moved up or down by up to that many scale degrees
HUMANIZE 1–16 (64ths) each note's MICRO moved at random, up to that much either way (HUMANIZED)
TRANSP −12 … +12 the notes moved that many semitones
OCTAVE −2 … +2 the notes moved that many octaves
THIN 5–100 % that share of the notes left out, at random
INVERT — the notes mirrored round the middle of the lowest and the highest
STUTTER x2–x4 each note a ratchet of that many
ARP UP, DOWN, UP+DN, RANDOM a chord with TIEs after it becomes its notes, one a step
MUTATE 5–100 % that share of the notes changed a little: a degree or two, the velocity, the place
GEN ANY or a genre the track's generator writes inside the selection only, with a new seed each time; the rest stays
RANDOM 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 new notes in the scale on that grid (a DRUM track: hits; 1/32: ratchets)

NOTE RND, TRANSP, OCTAVE, INVERT and ARP are for notes: on a DRUM track they say NOTES ONLY. The others work on a kit too.

Copy, paste and duplicate

Steps (0.9.9-seq2h). On SEQ's roll pages (STEP, NOTE, ..; a DRUM track's grid too), stopped or playing, the 16 white keys are the steps of the bar shown (the cursor's bar, as on the grid and COMP):

  • COPY a step: hold its key and turn SELECT (one detent is enough).
  • COPY a range: hold its first and last keys and turn SELECT: every step between them.
  • COPY the bar: hold keys 1 and 16 and turn SELECT.

  • PASTE: hold a step key and tap REC: the clipboard lands from that step on, going round within LEN (4 steps pasted at 14 with LEN 16: 14 15 16 1).

  • SELECT a range (V10.8.51): hold two or more step keys: those steps are the track's selection for SEQ EDIT (SEL 5-8).

  • CLEAR a range (V10.8.50): hold the step keys and tap EDIT: every step between the first and the last key is cleared (notes, components, locks), one UNDO point.

The screen says which steps (V10.8.50): COPY 5-8, PASTE 9-12, DUP 9-12, CLEAR 6-7. The footer shows [n] while the clipboard holds something. What is copied: each step whole (notes, length / TIEs, accent, slide, ratchet, MICRO, chance, both components with their LENGTH and N:M; on a DRUM track its lanes' hits, accents and lane modes) and the steps' parameter locks. The clipboard stays when you change track, bar or section: select another track and paste. DRUM <-> melodic is refused (DRUM <-> NOTES: NO). UNDO (GLO + G4) takes the last paste back.

REC tapped with no step key held, or with the clipboard empty, arms / disarms as always. On a melodic track armed for recording the keys write (or record) notes, so copy and paste wait until REC is off; on the DRUM grid the white keys stay the steps (a key pressed on an empty step for a copy or paste does not leave its hit there). On the roll the held keys still sound their notes.

A whole sequence: hold SEQ (SEQ EDIT, on any SEQ page) with no steps selected (G3 first if some are) and press E5 COPY: the track's steps 1 to LEN go to the same clipboard. F5 PASTE replaces the selected track's whole sequence with it, from step 1, its LEN the copy's (NOTHING COPIED when there is nothing). It works on another track or after changing part; DRUM ↔ melodic is refused as above; UNDO takes it back. With steps selected, E5 copies those steps and F5 pastes onto the selection's first step.

Duplicate (V10.8.50): in SEQ EDIT, C5 DUP pastes the selection (none: the whole track) right after itself and makes LEN longer to hold it (64 at most: NO ROOM).

A part into another (A → B): hold SAVE, press F3 (PLAY A; while playing it comes in on the next bar), then, once A plays, D4 (SAVE B): B now holds what A had. Stopped, SAVE › PART SLOTS does it with names: PLAY/EDIT A, then SAVE into B (12).

An ARRANGE row: on HOME › ARRANGE, KNOB 1 to the row and OCT+: a copy of it right after, selected (16 rows at most). The screen says ROW DUPLICATED (V10.8.52; ROW ADDED on an empty song).

To copy Gesture
Steps (two keys: a range; keys 1 and 16: the bar) step keys held + turn SELECT; paste: a step held + REC
A track's whole sequence SEQ held + E5 COPY (no selection); paste: SEQ held + F5 PASTE
Steps right after themselves SEQ held + C5 DUP
Part A into part B SAVE held + F3 (PLAY A), then SAVE held + D4 (SAVE B)
An ARRANGE row OCT+ on ARRANGE

Scale

ROOT, SCALE and QUANT are global: one scale for the whole song. Whatever track you set them on (knob, SCL layer, MIDI, a project load), every melodic track follows it at once; drum tracks have none. Each track keeps its own TRANS.

  • SCALE: CHR, MAJ, MIN, DOR, MIX, PEN, MPEN, HARM, PHRY, LYD, LOC, MEL, BLUES, WHOLE, DIMHW, DIMWH.
  • QUANT: OFF; SNAP (keys snap to the scale); WHITE (the white keys walk the scale, black keys are silent); SEQ (as SNAP, and the sequencer's notes snap too as they play).
  • SCL > ALL TR, KNOB 4 (0.7.6; SCL 2 until then; it was called STRN) moves every sequence up or down the scale (±14 degrees), on every track at once. It is global and saved with the project: if your notes sound lower or higher than the piano roll shows, look here. When it is not 0 the piano roll says ALL TR and its value, and PLAY says it too. 0 = off.
  • The RESO reverb and the SLICER's pitch steps follow the scale too.
  • (0.8.3) A section keeps its key: ROOT and SCALE are stored with each section, so a song can change key from one section to the next (GEN's PARTS does it for pop genres: the last section a whole step up). When the song brings in a section, the keys, CHORD, ALL TR and the RESO reverb follow its key, also with a DRUM track selected (then the first melodic track's key counts; until 0.8.3 a DRUM track selected kept the key before).

CHORD (0.6.81)

SCL > CHORD makes a key play a chord on the track (after the Omnichord and the Orchid):

  • CHORD: OFF; in the scale (every chord in key, nothing to think): TRIAD, 7TH, ADD9, SUS2, SUS4, built on the key's degree (a key outside the scale takes the scale note below; CHR: the major scale of ROOT); shapes on any key: MAJ, MIN, 7, MAJ7, MIN7, POWER. In a mode of seven notes (MAJ MIN DOR MIX HARM PHRY LYD LOC MEL) the chord is the mode's own on that degree (every other note of the scale). (0.8.3) In the scales of five, six or eight notes (PEN, MPEN, BLUES, WHOLE, DIMHW, DIMWH) every other note made odd stacks (C minor pentatonic's "triad" on C was C F Bb), so each tone is now the interval the chord asks for where the scale has it, else the nearest one it offers: a major or minor third (none: the chord becomes a suspension), a perfect fifth (else diminished over a minor third, augmented over a major one), a minor or major seventh (else a sixth), the ninth. Every tone stays in the scale: a pentatonic key gives triads, sus4 / sus2 chords and sixths (C minor pentatonic: Cm, Eb, Fsus4, Eb/G, Bbsus4; 7TH on F: F7sus4), whole tone augmented chords, the diminished scales diminished and dominant sevenths.
  • VOICING: CLOSE (root position); LEAD (each chord takes the inversion nearest the last one: voice leading, the Orchid's smoothness); OPEN (the second tone an octave up); +BASS (the root an octave down added).
  • STRUM: 0 all at once; up from there, the notes come in one after the other, low to high (up to ~63 ms apart), as a harp.

Letting the key go ends every note of its chord (those still to strum never come). The chord records into the step, live and in step recording alike (0.6.83: step recording took the key's note alone), and the ARP arpeggiates it. The keys of every note sounding light up, the chord's whole shape too: a way to see and learn the chords. With STRUM (0.6.84) a recorded chord goes whole into the one step where the key went down (its later notes no longer spill into the next step), and the sequencer strums every chord step back the same way, low to high (within half the step's gate). STRUM at 0: the steps' chords as before, all at once. A drum track, MONO, LEGATO and UNISON play the root alone. MIDI notes play as they come.

ARP

ARP: MODE, RATE, OCT (1–4), GATE. ARP 2: SWING, PROB, HOLD, ORDER (NOTE / PLAY). Modes: OFF, UP, DN, UPDN, RND, ORD, REPEAT, DNUP, UP+8, CONV, DIVG, PINKY, THUMB, WALK, CHORD, TRNS (the keys and incoming MIDI transpose the track's sequence by their distance from C4, without playing notes). Key latch: with MODE OFF, HOLD ON keeps the notes sounding after you let go; the next chord replaces them.

In time (V10.8.45). While the transport plays (or counts in), an arpeggio's first step falls on its RATE's grid of the transport: a key that comes up to 20 ms after a step starts on it at once, a later one waits for the next step, and from there it runs on the sequencer's time, so it stays on the grid. While recording it never starts late (no 20 ms grace: it waits for the next step), and each arpeggiated note is written on its own step (MICRO 0), whatever REC GRID. Stopped, the arpeggio starts from the key, as before.

Clearing

To clear Do
The selected track's steps and automation REC held + F3, or SAVE > TOOLS > CLEAR SEQ
The selected track's steps (or only the steps selected) SEQ EDIT F3 CLEAR (SEQ held)
All six tracks' steps, automation and the punch-in lane SEQ held + REC, then OCT+
Everything (NEW PROJECT): every track its power-on sound (V10.7.11: T1 DRUM-X ACOUSTIC, T2 ANALOG PLUCK, T3 PHASE INIT SAW, T4 FM6 FM BASS, T5 VOICE CHANT, T6 ANIMAL WHISTLE, dry), no steps or automation, the mix, effects, tempo and SLICER at their defaults, the song empty, macros at 0, the factory DRUM-X kit. Saved projects, user presets, MENU, CLOCK, TUNE and MIDI stay SAVE > TOOLS, TARGET PROJECT, ACTION CLEAR (CLEAR PROJECT?), then OCT+ (UNDO brings the music back)
Only one part's automation on the selected track REC held + FX / EDIT / ENV / LFO / SCL / ARP / GLO
(not a clear) A heavy test song, to measure the CPU on the device and listen for clicks (every live track chords of four with two step components a step and long glides, the kit on every lane, every FX on, 160 BPM) SAVE > TOOLS > 6 CPU TEST, OCT+, then PLAY (UNDO brings your music back)
The track's automation, keeping the steps SEQ EDIT F4 CLR AUTO (with steps selected: theirs only), or SEQ > AUTOMATION > CLEAR
Some steps step keys held + EDIT (V10.8.50)

A track clear says T3 CLEARED with SEQ+REC: ALL TRACKS under it as a reminder of the all-tracks combo.

7. ARRANGE: songs, sections and scenes

The pieces

  • A project is a song. There are 6 projects (V10.6p: 8 before; songs 7 and 8 are gone, their flash is kept for a drum sample bank: move them into 1–6 or keep them in a backup before updating).
  • Each project has 4 sections (parts), A–D. A section is a full snapshot of the music: every track's sound, steps and automation, the DRUM-X kit and its mutes, the punch-in lane, the SLICER, the macros, plus the tempo and global effects.
  • Each project has one arrangement: up to 16 rows, each a section played for 1–64 bars, optionally with a scene, and an END rule.
  • (V10.8) Each project also has one JAM take: every track playing its own sequence A–D, each change written where it sounded.
  • The song's pages are HOME's SONG group since V10.7.63: JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE (HOME, tapped to the SONG tab; SAVE + G5 goes straight to ARRANGE). SAVE keeps what stores and loads: TOOLS, PART SLOTS, PROJECTS, USER, PRESETS (12).

That's 24 sections in total (6 × 4).

Your first song, step by step

  1. Make a loop: record it (REC), write steps, use EUCLID or the generator (Your first song (5 minutes)).
  2. Store it as section A: hold SAVE and press C4 (SAVE A). The screen says SAVED A (STORED A before V10.8.47). It works while playing. To give it a name, save it on SAVE › PART SLOTS instead (12).
  3. Make B, C, D: change the music (steps, sounds, a track muted…) and hold SAVE + D4 (SAVED B), then E4 (C) and F4 (D). SAVE + F3–B3 plays a section back to check it (playing: on the next bar).
  4. Open the song: stop (PLAY), tap HOME until the SONG tab and turn SELECT to ARRANGE (or hold SAVE and press G5). With no rows it says NO ROWS.
  5. Add the rows: OCT+ adds a row (ROW ADDED): the first is A, 4 bars; each next one is a copy of the row picked, after it (V10.6o). KNOB 1 the row, KNOB 2 its PART A–D, KNOB 3 its BARS (1–64). For example A 8 · B 8 · A 8 · C 4 · D 8.
  6. END and scenes: KNOB 1 past the last row is + ADD, then END: there KNOB 2 picks STOP (once), x2–x8 or REPEAT (LOOP until V10.8.47). A scene: set the mutes (GLO held + black keys 1–6) and macros you want, KNOB 1 to the row, KNOB 4 right: SCENE STORED (left: SCENE CLEARED).
