  7. Play it: stopped, press PLAY on ARRANGE. The song plays from the top; PLAY again stops it and the music you had before comes back (SONG END). From any other page: hold SAVE + D5 (PLAY: THE SONG) and PLAY plays the song; SAVE + D5 again goes back to PLAY's mode PART (V10.8.48's banner still reads PLAY: THE LOOP). With no rows it says ADD A SONG ROW; a row on an empty section: the song won't start (PART EMPTY).
  8. Delete a row: stopped, on ARRANGE, KNOB 1 to the row, OCT−: DELETE SONG ROW?. OCT+ deletes it, OCT− keeps it. It cannot be undone.
  9. Or play it instead of writing rows: JAM and TAKE.

The ARRANGE page (HOME › ARRANGE)

ARRANGE is the third page of HOME's SONG group (JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE; until V10.7.63 it was a SAVE page; SAVE + G5 from anywhere). (V10.8.14) Its panel is the song as a score: the rows as blocks as wide as their bars, one lane per track; with no rows it says NO ROWS.

Knob On a row On + ADD On END
KNOB 1 (ROW) choose the row
KNOB 2 (PART) its section A–D; turned left past A: DELETE SONG ROW? adds a row (same section as the row above, 1 bar) STOP, x2 … x8, REPEAT (LOOP until V10.8.47)
OCT+ adds a row after the one picked, a copy of it, and selects it (V10.6o; 16 at most: 16 ROWS)
OCT− (V10.4) DELETE SONG ROW? for the row picked: OCT+ deletes it, OCT− keeps it (stopped)
KNOB 3 (BARS) its bars (1–64) adds a row
KNOB 4 (SCENE) right: store a scene (SCENE STORED); left: clear it (SCENE CLEARED)
  • PLAY on ARRANGE plays the song from the top; again: stop. (Until 0.8.4 OCT+ did too; now it adds a row.)
  • When the song ends (or you stop it), the music you had before pressing PLAY comes back (SONG END).
  • (V10.6z8) A sound you change while a song plays stays. Change a track's preset, its engine, a sound knob (EDIT, ENV, LFO, FX, MOD… anything a preset sets), an FM6 patch or the DRUM-X kit while a song (or a generated song, or a quick chain) plays, and that track keeps your sound over every section after it: the sections still bring their steps, pattern (LEN, DIV, swing, gate), arpeggio, scale, mix (level, pan) and mutes. Stopping brings the music you had before PLAY back (SONG END, your unsaved edits too) with your sounds over it (V10.7.6), and PLAY again keeps holding them. They follow the sections again after a new throw of the generator, a project or section loaded, a live section jump, or, for one track, EDIT layer RECALL (G3; it works while a song plays now): the section's stored sound back, and the next sections' after it.
  • END: STOP plays the song once, x2–x8 that many times, REPEAT forever. The footer gives the song's length and its end: 40 BARS · STOP, 40 BARS · x2, 40 BARS · END REPEAT.
  • If a row points to an empty section the song won't start: the screen says PART EMPTY.
  • While a song plays, step editing, the generator and EUCLID are blocked (SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT).
  • To delete a row you can also use SAVE › TOOLS (TARGET SONG, ACTION DEL ROW: the row ARRANGE has selected). To delete the whole arrangement: TARGET SONG, ACTION CLEAR (CLEAR SONG ORDER?). Neither can be undone.
  • The arrangement is saved automatically (about 2 seconds after a change, while stopped). See 12.
  • The per-track FROM and VAR of a row (the TIMELINE page, V10 to V10.7) have no page now; a song that has them still plays them.

JAM and TAKE (HOME › SONG)

(V10.8) JAM is the song played by hand. Every track has its sequence in each of the parts A–D; on JAM you choose, track by track, which one plays, while it plays. The panel is six tracks × four parts: the cell each track plays framed, one asked for and not in yet dashed, the cell KNOB 1 and KNOB 2 point at ringed white.

JAM TAKE
KNOB 1 TRACK CHANGE: the take's change you edit (n/N)
KNOB 2 PART: the part A–D (the cell; SEQ until V10.8.47) WHEN: moves it (bar.beat.16th)
KNOB 3 SWITCH: when a change lands (AT ONCE, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, BAR; CAMBIO until V10.8.47) PART: its sequence A–D
KNOB 4 TAKE: FREE or LOCK BARS: the take's length
OCT+ GO: the picked track to the picked sequence, on SWITCH's step (stopped: at once) a new change (TAKE FULL when there is no room)
OCT− that track stops on the next bar; after a LOCK round: undoes the round (ROUND UNDONE) deletes the change
F3–B3 part A–D on every track (playing: on the next bar; PART EMPTY if nothing is stored there) —
REC records the take —
  • The take: press REC on JAM (JAM REC NEXT BAR; stopped: JAM REC: PLAY). From the next bar line it writes the tracks' sequences as they are and then every change where it sounds, a 16th exact. REC again or stopping ends it on a bar line. It replaces the take there was; stopped, it is kept with the project (JAM TAKE KEPT). Holding SAVE and pressing E5 does the same from any page (the map still reads SONG REC).
  • LOCK (KNOB 4 to the right, with a take): the take plays round and round and you jam over it; a track you moved yourself is drawn white and says YOU until the take's next change of it.
  • One track again: in LOCK, pick a track and press REC (REC TRACK): from the next bar that track's changes are recorded for one round of the take and replace the ones it had (TRACK DONE). OCT− then brings the take back as it was (ROUND UNDONE).
  • TAKE shows the take whole, the change picked ringed and its track lit; with no take the cards say -- and the knobs say NO TAKE.
  • Choosing a sequence on JAM (or SEQ › STEP's KNOB 1, which is the same switch for the selected track) ends a song or quick chain that was playing and puts PLAY back to PART (the loop).

TIMELINE, PARTS and CLIPS (SAVE › SONG)

Gone in V10.8: the song mode above, HOME › JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE, took their place.

SAVE SONG AS (SAVE › PROJECT)

The page went in V10.7.20; SAVE › PROJECTS does it. KNOB 1 picks the destination project (1–6; it is not opened), KNOB 4 to the right arms SAVE, OCT+. A used destination asks OVERWRITE PROJECT n?; then the NAME screen, where KNOB 3 says whether the whole SONG or only the LOOP is written. It copies the whole song: sections A–D (with the unsaved edits of the one playing), the tempo and globals, the rows, bars, END and scenes, and PART / SONG. Stop first (STOP TO SAVE). The project you copied from stays open and unchanged; open the copy with PROJECTS' LOAD.

Scenes

A scene is stored per row and recalls, when that row starts: the track mutes (T1–T6), the DRUM-X group mutes, the macros M1–M4 and the punch-in note effects being held. It stays in effect through the following rows that have none. Scenes apply when a song plays, not in a quick chain.

Playing sections live (SAVE layer)

Hold SAVE:

  • F3–B3: play section A–D. While playing it comes in on the next bar; stopped, it loads at once.
  • Tap two or more of F3–B3 in one hold: a quick chain — they play in turn, each for its longest pattern's length, round and round, starting on the next bar (stopped: at once).
  • C4–F4: SAVE A–D (STORE A–D until V10.8.47), the music now into A–D; the screen says SAVED A (works while playing; see 12 for when it reaches flash). F3 then D4 copies part A into B.
  • OCT+: SAVE into the section playing (PLAY A PART FIRST if none). OCT−: RECALL it as stored.
  • D5: PART / SONG (LOOP / SONG until V10.8.47) — in SONG mode, PLAY from any page plays the arrangement.
  • E5: records the JAM take (V10.8; the key still reads SONG REC), as REC on JAM: see JAM and TAKE. Before V10.8 it wrote the sections you played into the arrangement's rows.
  • G5: jump to ARRANGE.
  • C5: NAME, on SAVE › USER, PART SLOTS or PROJECTS.
  • KNOB 1: pick another project; it switches when you let go of SAVE (stopped only) and loads its section A.

8. Dice and UNDO

GEN — the song generator (HOME + SELECT)

Hold HOME and turn SELECT, from any page, or on HOME walk the chain with SELECT (ECOSYSTEM · LIFE · BEING · JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE · GENERATOR 1 · 2 · 3 · 4) or tap HOME to its next group (ECOSYSTEM → BEING → SONG → GENERATOR). The GENERATOR is HOME's last group, four ordinary pages: SELECT turns the page, KNOB 1–4 set the four values shown (PRESETS loads the track's sounds there, as everywhere), OCT+ makes the piece and OCT− goes back to ECOSYSTEM (the piece stays; UNDO, GLO + G4, brings back what was there before); every section button works from there. On GENERATOR 1–3 the panel shows the song as ARRANGE draws it (no song yet: the sections) and a line of state (READY, PLAYING, SONG READY, or DRAFT · SAVE KEEPS · OCT+ NEW); on GENERATOR 4, a radio. PLAY runs and stops the transport without leaving the screen (0.6.97).

The generator can't make a piece while a song plays (SONG mode, SAVE + D5, ARRANGE's PLAY, or a quick chain): OCT+ says SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT. Stop the song, or turn SONG mode off with SAVE + D5 so PLAY plays the loop. (RADIO, below, is the exception: it changes the piece by itself on the bar line.)

A part set OFF stays off (V10.8). The piece always has two melodic parts at least, but only parts left on AUTO are filled in for that (BASS first, then CHORDS). The GENRE is kept between visits (V10.8); power-on and NEW PROJECT start on EXPLORE.

Page KNOB 1 KNOB 2 KNOB 3 KNOB 4
GENERATOR 1 GENRE: EXPLORE (no genre, every rule broken, below), RANDOM (half its throws are mutants of two genres, named A+B) or one of the 29 genres (below), in that order SEED 0000–9999 ENERGY 0–100 % FORM: LOOP, PARTS, SONG, MY LOOP
GENERATOR 2 DRUMS BASS CHORDS ARP — each OFF, 10–100 %, or AUTO (the genre's); OFF stays off (V10.8)
GENERATOR 3 LEAD (as above) COMPLEX 0–100 % SWING AUTO or 0–100 % HUMAN 0–100 %
GENERATOR 4 KEY: NEW or KEEP ENTRY: ALL or BUILD RADIO: OFF or ON (V10.8.39) MOOD: CALM … MID … DANCE (V10.8.39)

RADIO (V10.8.39; GENERATOR 4, KNOB 3). ON, the generator goes on by itself: on the last bar of the piece (a song: its last row's last bar; a loop: every 16 bars above 110 BPM, 8 above 74 BPM, 4 slower; V10.8.45, it was 32 / 16; since V10.8.68, with MOOD at −15 or lower, half as many) it throws a new seed and makes the next piece, which comes in on the bar line as an OCT+ would, ENTRY's way. (V10.8.43) A STOP in that last bar stops: the next piece is made only once the bar has played through, or the song has reached its own END. It only goes on while a piece the generator made is playing as a draft (not yet saved), never over a saved song, and not with FORM MY LOOP. Press OCT+ once to make the first piece and PLAY. GENERATOR 4's panel is a radio: its speaker pulses with the beat while RADIO is ON and it plays, the dial's needle is MOOD, and RADIO n counts the pieces it has made. Not saved with the project.

MOOD (V10.8.39–V10.8.41; GENERATOR 4, KNOB 4), from CALM through MID (the middle: nothing changes) to DANCE, in steps of 5 from −50 to +50: - the energy: it is added to ENERGY (up to ±60). - the drums, with every GENRE: towards CALM the kit goes down, the kick first, shorter and darker (a light hand down to −25; near −50 only a soft closed hat is left); towards DANCE the kick is whole and the snare, clap and hats come up, longer and driven, with a kick on the bar's first and third beats from +25 and on every beat from +40. A genre whose drums are no four on the floor (half-time, breaks, electro, jazz) keeps its own kick's places. - the genre, with GENRE RANDOM: of a few genres drawn, the one whose tempo sits nearest the mood (about 80 BPM calm … 150 dance); the further from MID, the more it leans. - the tempo, in EXPLORE: pulled towards about 72 BPM (CALM) or 138 (DANCE). With RADIO ON and MOOD on the DANCE side, the next piece takes the tempo of its range nearest the piece before. - the sound and the form, towards CALM (V10.8.68): longer attacks and releases (a pad's and a texture's most, an arp's least), a softer filter envelope, wetter sends (the pads' and the texture's reverb, the lines' delay). From −25, chords a genre would stab are held or swell in instead. The piece gets shorter: the song plan is fitted to at most about four minutes at −50 (five at MID), then every row of SONG and PARTS is cut, a little at −5 and to about 40 % of its bars at −50 (never under 4 bars; the build is cut only from −25). With RADIO, a loop brings the next piece after half as many bars (from −15, see RADIO above). The build's DJ FILTER sweep (below) never plays from −15. - towards DANCE (V10.8.68): the kick's pump (the master's DUCK) deeper, held between 40 and 60. Every DANCE piece has drums, except NEO CLASSIC's. Not saved with the project.

What V10.8.43–V10.8.48 changed in every piece: - SCL › HARMONY is yours (V10.8.43): a throw no longer touches its four values. With HARMONY on, the piece and each of its sections sit on the key's tonic chord (no contrast progression, no break on the subdominant) and HARMONY's progression moves them; off, as before. - Shorter sections (V10.8.45): PARTS' and SONG's rows half as long as before, none much over 24 seconds (shorter at slow tempos); MY LOOP's as they were. (Since V10.8.69 SONG and PARTS take their rows and lengths from a song plan instead, below.) Each row has its own macro values, a small step from the row before (an arc, V10.8.46), and a section that comes back plays its lead, its arp and the free drum lines as ARRANGE's VAR 1 / 2: it never returns identical. - Parts that move (V10.8.46): a melodic part without a vibrato gets a slow LFO free of the notes (5 to 20 s, each part its own period) on the filter and on the shape (the bass: its filter only), and wanders across the stereo over two or four bars (the bass stays in the middle); a lead's and an arp's notes also move the shape with their envelope. - Envelopes by role (V10.8.45–V10.8.48): real decays and tails; no part is held at full sustain but held organs and drones. A lead has a long decay, little sustain (about 37 % at most) and a long release; a plucked lead and the arp are short; stabbed chords come in fast and fall; held chords swell in, hold (about 75 % at most) and fade long; the bass is firm in. Towards MOOD CALM the attacks are softer and the releases longer. - A filter type each (V10.8.48): on ANALOG and PHASE the chords, the lead, the arp and the texture take their own filter TYPE (LP, BP or HP), never the same band as the part before; BP and HP with KEY TRK 100 (FILTER's tag reads 100), so the band follows the notes. The bass keeps its filter; FM6, STRING and MATH parts, acid and dub keep their sound's; never a COMB. - GAIN makes up the level (V10.8.48): the track's GAIN (EDIT › LEVEL) is the piece's own, so what a low sustain or a band takes away is made up (a lead or an arp up to +8 dB, chords and bass half as much). - Details: a chord, pad or texture part on a lead's sound loses that sound's fast vibrato (V10.8.43); MOOD DANCE's drum decays a little shorter and its pump deeper; the build's high-pass rises smoothly over its last bar (V10.8.46; since V10.8.68 a low-pass sweep, below); PHONK always takes the drift map (V10.8.46); JAZZ's hi-hats and ride at about half level (V10.8.47).

What V10.8.51–V10.8.72 changed in every piece: - Song plans (V10.8.69, from JIANT BYTE): SONG and PARTS lay out ARRANGE from a plan of the genre's family. The club's plans (the classic, the DJ's long in and out, drop after drop, the groove's), the song's (the pop song, the band's, a short one), hip hop's (the hook first, or the verse first) and the arc's (the layers in to a climax, one layer alone first, two crests). A seed picks one plan and throws its rows: some play in half the seeds, some by ENERGY (a second drop, the last chorus again). A row is an intro, a groove, a break, a build, a drop or an outro, each played by one of the piece's sections. ENERGY sets the lengths: high, longer drops; low, longer intros, breaks and outros. The plan is then fitted to two to five minutes, and the drum fills are placed at the rows' ends, the ones into a break, a build or a drop first. PARTS plays its plan at half length. The 24-second cap of V10.8.45 is gone. - The timbre moves (V10.8.69): in each section every melodic part's timbre (the engine's E6 knob) rises over its loop, more with COMPLEX; in the break it goes back down. - Each section its own automation (V10.8.70, JIANT BYTE's): the kit's TONE rises over the build; its DECAY rises toward the turn (only up, so the kit keeps its punch); a snare roll is muted into the turn; with COMPLEX past 55 the hats' offbeats get an 80 % chance; the delay is thrown on the lead's last note; the arp's filter ramps over the build; a stab chord lands in a melodic part (genres that stab their chords, not EXPLORE); the break's pads get a slower attack and a longer release. Not with FORM MY LOOP. - Call and response and EXPLORE's cut stay (V10.8.70): in one piece in two, where the lead speaks (two notes or more in a half bar) the arp is silent, and it answers in the lead's gaps; in almost half the EXPLORE pieces the cycle's last beat or two are cut, silent but for the drums and one odd track. - The mix (V10.8.68–V10.8.69): the drums keep their punch (the kit's DECAY and DRIVE, the heavy kits' DIST, CLIP 60–85 with a heavy kit, else 35–65); PHONK's and BAILE FUNK's 808 3 dB lower; the delay ping-pongs in three pieces in four. - No clipping (V10.8.51): each genre has its own headroom. Every part comes down by the same amount, so no piece's track or mix goes over −1 dBFS before the master (before, up to +13 dBFS). The master's leveler brings the loudness back. - The build's DJ FILTER (V10.8.68): in a third of the pieces the build ends with a smooth low-pass sweep that opens into the drop (a third of those dip and open again). It was a high-pass. Never towards CALM. - NEO CLASSIC never has drums (V10.8.68), not even with MOOD DANCE. - EXPLORE (V10.8.68): chords in every piece, the arp and the lead in four pieces in five; wetter, and the delay ping-pong; more pads, strings and drones on the chords (no stab, hoover or guitar there) and a drone instead of noise on the texture, the pads and textures often swelling in; no chip or hoover leads (an electric piano instead); a role on a random engine half as often as before; locrian rarely; fewer odd tricks a piece; the step components mostly arps and echoes (RAND and BEND rarely). - OTT (V10.8.72): the electronic genres put FX › OTT (see OTT) on the drums and the bass, at a DEPTH set by the genre: 40: HOUSE, DEEP HOUSE, MINIMAL TECHNO (MINIMAL: the bass alone, its LEVEL two steps up); 44: TECH HOUSE, TRIBAL (the drums alone), REGGAETON, IDM GLITCH (the drums, no bass), TECHNO ROCK's synth throw; 48–54: DRUM & BASS 48; ELECTRO, BREAKBEAT, DEMBOW, ELECTRO METAL and HIP HOP's trap, drill and pluggnb 50; HARD TECHNO, EBM and BAILE FUNK 54; 60: HARD BASS, PHONK, DUBSTEP. MOOD DANCE (+15 and up) adds 4. In one seed in two the lead gets a hard one, DEPTH 60–78 (when there is no lead, or it is a riff already up front, the texture takes it), in every genre above but MINIMAL TECHNO, DEEP HOUSE, TRIBAL, REGGAETON and ELECTRO METAL. Three tracks at most, never the pads. Each role has its own settings: the drums TIME 44, UP/DN a little less upward, X-OVER 45; the bass TIME 52, X-OVER 26 (its sub whole); the lead TIME 48, X-OVER 55. Each OTT track's LEVEL comes down a little (more the deeper it is), so no piece goes over −1 dBFS. None on the acoustic and organic genres (CUMBIA, JAZZ, NEO CLASSIC, DREAM POP, SHOEGAZE, KRAUT, METALCORE, IDM AMBIENT, IDM WEIRD), on HIP HOP's boom bap and lofi, on TECHNO ROCK's rock, on EXPLORE, nor at MOOD CALM (−15 or lower); every other track's OTT is turned off. RESOUND sets the genre's OTT, or clears it, on the tracks it gives new sounds; a track it does not touch keeps its OTT. Every section of the piece gets the same OTT: it does not change from section to section. The rest of the piece is as it was: the same seed still makes the same piece.

The piece is deterministic: the same settings make the same piece every time, so a seed you like can be dialled back. OCT+ with the settings unchanged throws a new seed (another piece); turn a knob and press OCT+ and you get the same piece with that one thing changed — every part draws its random numbers from its own stream, so BASS turned leaves the drums and the lead as they were. The last piece's name is its genre and its seed (HOUSE 0421).

A genre's throws differ (V10.6z10). Each throw of a genre takes its own bass (one of the genre's three archetypes, a few of its steps moved), its own groove (the genre's extra kicks in a place or two of its idiom, the hats and the percussion from the genre's pools where they are not its identity: cumbia's guiro, the dembow's 3 + 3 + 2, jazz's ride stay; now and then a euclid on a percussion lane; IDM's breaks one of four), its own progression (the genre's own a third of the time, else one its harmony's grammar writes), its own sounds (another of the engine's presets of the same type a third of the time) and a tempo around ENERGY's place in the genre's range. In PARTS and SONG the sections develop: their bass, chords and arp a variation of A's, the lead's motif developed another way, a one-chord piece's sections denser or thinner, higher or lower. And OCT+ never throws the core (progression, bass, map, groove) of one of the genre's last eight throws: it tries other seeds first. A seed is still its song.

The genres, as KNOB 1 turns them after EXPLORE and RANDOM (V10.6n: the owner's list, in its order): MINIMAL TECHNO, HARD TECHNO, HARD BASS, HOUSE, DEEP HOUSE, TECH HOUSE, TRIBAL, CUMBIA, REGGAETON, DEMBOW, ELECTRO, BREAKBEAT, DRUM & BASS, IDM GLITCH, IDM AMBIENT, IDM WEIRD, KRAUT, EBM, NEO CLASSIC, ELECTRO METAL, TECHNO ROCK, DREAM POP, PHONK, BAILE FUNK, JAZZ, HIP HOP, DUBSTEP, SHOEGAZE, METALCORE — 29 since V10.8.41, when FUGA went (V10.6w: HIP HOP's throws each one of trap, drill, pluggnb, boom bap or lofi; TECHNO ROCK's techno rock, rock or synth 80s; JAZZ in swung eighths, its BPM the half of the felt tempo). Each one knows its tempo range, its scales and chord progressions, its drum map and kit, its bass archetypes and register, how its chords, arp and lead speak, which sound recipe each role takes, how human it plays and its space (reverb type, delay type and time, how wet).

(V10.7.8, the owner's ask) CUMBIA's güiro is a güiro: DRUM-X's filter GR on the closed hat (LATIN PERC's, with its llamador, maracas, conga and clave), a long stroke on each beat's "e" and a short one on its "and", another short one on 2's and 4's "a" leading into the next beat (digital keeps its on the beat), the accents the long strokes; villera is now RKT (the owner's reference, MC Caco's, ~92 BPM): a short kick and the clap on every quarter, the güiro's stroke on the beat and a "chk" on its "a" pulled ~28 ms early (MICRO: the triplet's pull), the conga on the "and"s, the bass and the keys low under the drums. REGGAETON is harder and has more room: the kit and the 808 driven (romántico's clean), the 808 shorter, the plucked arp a minor riff up front, the pad and the hook under it, LATIN PERC's conga and clave. BAILE FUNK is ultra-minimal: the tamborzão's "tum tcha" on 3, 6 and 12 two tom shots (low on the tom, high on the clap's lane), the cowbell's answer, no snare, clap, hats or chords, the 808 short, punchy and gliding up at the bar's end, the chant's chops sparse.

A clean base (0.9.9-gen1): every piece starts from NEW PROJECT's state — every track's parameters, sound, steps, step components, p-locks and automation, MUTATE, the song's globals (but the clock, tune, MIDI and routing), the punch-in and global component lanes, DRUM-X's kit (GLUE, octaves, sends, layers), FUGUE's playheads, PLAY's SONG mode — so nothing of the piece before, or of your edits, carries into it: the same settings and seed make the same project whatever was there. Kept: the tempo under BPM LOCK, the project's name and your own sections (PARTS never writes over them); UNDO brings the old music back.

Sound archetypes and pattern grammar (0.9.9-gen1). Each role of a genre plays a sound archetype set in the engine's real parameters: the engine and its factory preset (a bass always the archetype's engine), the oscillator wave, the filter type, cutoff, resonance and envelope amount, the amp envelope, glide, drive and chorus, an LFO on the filter, each with a small random range so two seeds differ but stay the sound. Some of them:

Archetype Where (V10.8.72's genres) The sound
ACID (the 303) BREAKBEAT (0.9.9-gen2, after X0X's Open303) ANALOG saw (or square), one oscillator, no noise; LP low (~400 Hz at rest), RES 104–120 (high, never ringing on its own), the envelope high on it (~2 kHz at the peak) with a short decay (400–900 ms) over a sustain (the note's body: ANALOG's one envelope is the level's too); an ACCENT opens the filter ~2 octaves more and plays louder; LEGATO, so a SLIDE holds the gate and the next note glides (MODE TIME, ~55 ms whatever the interval) without retriggering the envelope; DIST after
TECH BASS HARD TECHNO, TECH HOUSE, TRIBAL, TECHNO ROCK ANALOG saw or square, short, resonant LP, envelope, drive
EBM BASS EBM, ELECTRO METAL ANALOG square through the resonant LP filter (V10.8.35; the MS20 before), short, envelope, drive
808 REGGAETON, DEMBOW, PHONK, BAILE FUNK, HIP HOP a sine's long boom, glide 30+, driven
WOBBLE DUBSTEP fat saws, resonant LP moved by an LFO on the beat (1/8)
REESE DRUM & BASS SAW3 detuned, a slow LFO on the filter, chorus
OCTAVE BASS ELECTRO ANALOG saw or square plucked by the filter envelope
UPRIGHT JAZZ a triangle, short and plucked
SUB MINIMAL TECHNO, DEEP HOUSE, IDM AMBIENT, DREAM POP a sine, LP low
DONK (V10.8.42, in SUPERSAW's place) HARD BASS PHASE (RESO DROPS / FB BASS), mono, driven, a SUB under it
FM BASS HOUSE, CUMBIA, IDM GLITCH, IDM WEIRD FM6 FM BASS / HARD BASS

Over the genre's drum map, bass archetypes, chord play, arp and lead, a pattern grammar a genre adds: on the bass, ACCENTs off the kick, SLIDEs into the next note (its glide), octave jumps on the offbeat sixteenths (each 0–3 by genre: ELECTRO jumps most, REGGAETON, DRUM & BASS, PHONK, HIP HOP and DUBSTEP slide, EBM and HARD TECHNO accent; the acid bass keeps the 303's own rules, after X0X's TB-3PO (0.9.9-gen2): one 16-step line, ~68 % of the steps a note (the bar's first always), the mode's degrees over the chord (the root most), an octave up a third of the time and down now and then, ACCENTs on ~30 % of the notes, SLIDEs on ~25 % (never into a rest), now and then a TIE, every other bar a few notes re-rolled); DRUM-X GLUE where the genre bus-compresses (the techno family, EBM, DnB, dubstep); now and then the closed hat rolled on the beat's last sixteenth every other loop (HARD TECHNO, REGGAETON, DEMBOW, ELECTRO, BREAKBEAT, DRUM & BASS, IDM GLITCH, IDM WEIRD, TECHNO ROCK, PHONK, HIP HOP); A role's sound is always its archetype (no more neighbour recipes swapped in).

Leads and drums (0.9.9-gen2). A lead's vibrato is a singer's, not a siren's: LFO PITCH 1 (~19 cents), 5.1–6.3 Hz, faded in over 160–450 ms so the attack is clean, the filter's LFO off under it; otherwise no pitch LFO, only a slow, subtle one on the filter. Pads never get more than a tiny, slow pitch drift (EXPLORE included). The drums leave room for the bass and the lead: every lane's DECAY shorter (the kick's tail, the clap, the hats, the toms most; the 808 and DUB kicks shorter too), the kits' pitch sweep, FM and drive offsets halved, the snare's FEEDBK 2–4, MORPH moving less, GLUE at most 8, the drum track's LEVEL 94 (was 106) and drier sends.

EXPLORE (0.8.6), the first choice and where the screen always opens (at power-on, after NEW PROJECT, every time you open GEN), follows no genre and breaks their rules on purpose, so every seed is a very different piece (LAST: EXPLORE 0421): - Tempo from 76 to 154 BPM, now and then an extreme (60–76 or 168–180); MOOD moves it (above); any drum map (the procedural IDM's too) and kit, its sounds pulled far from the kit's; any three bass archetypes against any kick rule; any chord play, voicing, arp and lead; a role may take another role's kind of sound (a plucked bass, a bell lead, an organ texture). - The key: a mode of seven from the SCALE page, the exotic ones likeliest (phrygian, lydian, harmonic and melodic minor; locrian too, but rarely since V10.8.68), the lead on a pentatonic, hexatonic or gapped set over it. Harmony: one to four chords on any degrees in any order (non-functional moves), any quality, now and then a borrowed, secondary or flat-side chord (the out-of-key notes), a family and colours thrown too; a PARTS song's last section may move anywhere (a semitone, a tritone ..), not just a whole step up. - Time: a chord 8 to 48 steps, the loop 8 to 64 (odd metres: 3/4, 5/4, 7/8 ..); each track its own LEN and DIV (1/8, 1/32, 8T, 16T: polyrhythm), a track's own swing, drum hits off the grid. - Sound: any engine on any role, ANIMAL and VOICE included (VOICE singing words in ES / EN / JA, a phrase or scat), FM6, ANIMAL and VOICE on two tracks at most; DRUM-X's octaves per sound on the steps (x2 x4 x8, SHORT, GHOST, FLAM); wide pans, glides, vibratos, detune, distortion types (V10.8: glide, vibrato and detune less often and shallower: less pitch wobble). - Motion: step components scattered (RAND, OCT, BEND, ECHO, PULSE, WALK, CLIMB, ARP, TONAL, some every other loop), PLAYHEADS on a track or two; the delay's grain pitch (V10.8: one piece in ten, an octave up or down) and spray, ping-pong, any reverb. - What it keeps: it always plays (two melodic parts at least, the genres' levels, the shared voice budget, the delay short of self-oscillation), the SCALE page and the CHORD page say the key and the chords it plays, and every note is in that key but the coloured chords' own tones and the approaches. The same seed is the same piece; the genres' pieces are untouched by it; a genre's piece after it starts from the clean base (DIV 1/16, no PLAYHEADS).

What a piece is made of:

  • Drums from a map of priorities (after Mutable Instruments' Grids): every step of every lane has a level, a hit where the level clears the density DRUMS sets, so ghosts go first as you turn it down and the kick's anchors last. Then the snare's ghost notes on the best positions (the sixteenth before 2 and 4 first), the hats' accent cell (house, funk, garage, machine), a small variation on the even bars (COMPLEX), the genre's fill on the phrase's last bar (a snare roll, a tom run, the kick dropped, a hat roll, a linear funk fill, Blue Monday's sixteenth kicks, a dub rim, a break before the one) and the snare laid back where the genre plays late (TIMING). ENERGY and the amounts decide how much plays; the kick is never dropped from the one.
  • The key (0.8.3): a mode of seven notes for every genre (its list: major, minor, dorian, mixolydian, phrygian, lydian, harmonic and melodic minor), written to the SCALE page (ROOT, SCALE, and QUANT SNAP unless you chose another QUANT) on every track, so the keys you play afterwards, the CHORD page, ALL TR and the RESO reverb are in the piece's key. A genre that sings pentatonic or blues (in V10.8.72: DEEP HOUSE) gets the mode that holds it (dorian or aeolian; major for the major pentatonic) and its lead keeps to the pentatonic notes: the chords stay real chords and every note is still in the SCALE page's scale. The chord track's CHORD page is set to the piece's chords (TRIAD, 7TH, ADD9, SUS2 or SUS4, as its progression is coloured), VOICING LEAD, a strum where a guitar plays them; CHORD is off on the other tracks.
  • Harmony (0.8.3): each genre has a family (modal loops; seventh-chord loops; functional pop; colour washes; film; jazz) and progressions written as degrees of the mode, each loop ending on the chord that leads back to its first (IV–I, bVII–i, V–i, bII–i ..): i bVII, i iv7, i bII (phrygian), I V vi IV, vi IV I V, I vi IV V, i bVI bIII bVII, the Andalusian i bVII bVI V, the Aeolian bVI bVII i, i7 bIIImaj7 bVII7 iv7, ii7 V7 Imaj7, Imaj7 vi7 ii7 V7, the bossa's Imaj7 II7 ii7 V7, I bVII IV I .. A mode that would turn one of its chords diminished (dorian's vi, lydian's #iv) never takes that progression: the genre's next one, else the mode's own loop. Then the cadences and colours the genre allows: the minor key's dominant raised before its tonic (the leading tone: HARD BASS, CUMBIA, NEO CLASSIC, JAZZ, HIP HOP), jazz's turnaround (ii–V in the last bar), a secondary dominant on the second half of the chord before its target (V/vi, V/ii, V/IV: NEO CLASSIC, JAZZ; with COMPLEX), a major key's IV going minor before I (mixture: KRAUT, NEO CLASSIC), the flat side borrowed in major (bVII, bVI: KRAUT, NEO CLASSIC). Harmonic rhythm by genre: a chord every bar, every two or four bars, or one chord for the whole loop. Chords are triads, sevenths, ninths (never a b9), add9, sus2 / sus4 (a perfect fourth only), sixths, quartal stacks, power chords, recoloured by the genre (plain, rich, suspended, quartal, power, parallel).
  • Bass from about fifty archetypes written against the kick: house offbeat and bounce, deep walking sixteenths, techno rolling sixteenths and octave bounce, Detroit, EBM, italo, psy, UK garage, Jamerson, around the kick, on the one, slap, Good Times, jazz walking and two-feel, boogie, country, ska, tumbao, bossa, rock eighths, punk sixteenths, McCartney, Peter Hook, motorik, angular post punk, indie, one drop, steppers, rockers, dub, boom bap, trap 808s, DnB, jungle, wobble, pedal, fifths, Suicide, Kraftwerk; and acid by the 303's rules (accents on 3–5 steps, slides on 2–3, an octave jump after a slide, the accents varied over the bars). The root at every chord change (a chord that comes in mid-bar gets its root there), the archetype's third, fifth and seventh the chord's own (a borrowed or raised chord's too), approaches by a semitone into the next root on a weak beat (they always resolve: a thinner bass never leaves one hanging), a pickup at the end of the fourth bar; the kick doubled, answered (the bass stays off the kick's steps), interlocked (and a note right after it) or sustained under it, as the genre does.
  • Chords voiced (0.8.3): of each chord's inversions and spreads, the one nearest the last chord, voice by voice (common tones held, the least motion: about 4.6 semitones a change in all, against 5.5 before), in C3..G5, no second below G3 and no close third at the very bottom; close in the hand for stabs and comping, spread (drop 2) for the washes and film, rootless (3 5 7 9) where jazz and deep house have the bass on the root, moved in parallel for techno and impressionism; played held, swelling, stabbed on the offbeats, pulsed, dubbed through the delay, skanked, comped, pushed, as a drone, sparse, broken (UK garage) or trance-gated, each held to its own chord's end.
  • Arp: an order over the voiced chord — up, up and down, down, Alberti, Glass's groups, a Reich pulse, a sequencer, a walk, cycles of 3 or 5 against the bar (polymetric), a trance gate, octaves — in sixteenths or eighths, with holes (ARP), in D3..D5; each chord's figure from its first note; only the chord's tones.
  • Lead (0.8.3: composed, not walked): a one-bar motif — a rhythm cell (a long note and two short, a tresillo, a pickup into three, a dotted push ..) and a contour of steps (a third now and then, a leap turned back by a step, an arch, a fall, a rise or a wave) — developed over the four-bar phrase by a template: a period (antecedent closing open on the 2nd or the 5th, consequent closing on the tonic), a sentence (the motif, its sequence, a continuation climbing to the climax two thirds in, the cadence), A A B A', call and response (the answer the call's contour turned), the techno hook A A A A', or the dub's with a bar of space; one operator on a varied bar (its last note left out, its end moved, a neighbour into its last note). The motif moves to each bar's chord the voice-led way (its first note the chord tone a step from the last note; the same chord: the motif as it was). The rules every lead keeps: a chord tone on beats 1 and 3, on 2 and 4 a chord tone or a passing note that moves by steps, passing and neighbour notes between, mostly steps (60 % of its moves), never more than an octave, a leap past a fourth followed by a step back, a range of about a tenth, the phrase closing on a stable degree (the tonic, the third or the fifth on a chord tone) and held, no minor ninth or tritone over the chord's root, no avoid note held (a fourth over a major third), a borrowed or raised chord's tones followed (the minor key's b7 becomes the leading tone over its V). Or: a hypnotic ostinato on an euclid (its cell's notes on the chord at the beats), a machine's figure moved with the chord, long notes as a guide-tone line (each the chord tone a step or a third on, a short figure stepping into it now and then), a tintinnabuli line (stepwise, a chord tone on each long note, a passing note between). Never above A5 (B5 in a section lifted a step); high notes softer. Each lead, figure and drum pattern is the genre's own for a seed (the same seed in two genres: two tunes).
  • Sounds by recipe a role: sub, acid, Reese, FM bass, rock bass, Hook's chorused bass, wow bass; pad, strings, choir, organ (WHEEL), electric piano, stab, dub chord, pluck, bell, lead, vox lead, chip, keys, drone, noise, texture, hoover, a shoegaze wall, a tremolo guitar. A recipe picks an engine, a factory sound whose name fits, moves its parameters a little, shapes the envelope, the filter (type, cutoff, resonance, the envelope on it), a slow LFO, drive, chorus, glide, the voice mode. The kit is one of seven (the factory kit as it is, 909, 808, click, industrial, soft, breaks; the dub kit is gone since V10.6p) written over the factory DRUM-X kit, the drum track's TONE, DECAY, NOISE and DRIVE with it.
  • Mix: level, pan and sends by role and by how wet the genre is; HUMAN sets SEQ > TRACK's HUMAN on every track by the role (hats and leads more, the kick none) scaled by how human the genre is (a band more than a machine); SWING the genre's unless set; DUCK, CLIP and PUNCH on the master; the delay's TYPE, PING-PONG and TIME and the reverb's type the genre's.
  • With TRACKS 6 the sixth track is a texture (a drone, noise, a choir, an organ, strings) in long notes.
  • FORM: LOOP writes one loop (2 or 4 bars). PARTS also stores sections A (the piece), B (a break: no drums, no bass) and C (a drop: the drums denser) and fills ARRANGE (PLAY plays the song, as 0.6.81's DICE ALL did); since V10.8.69 its rows come from a song plan at half length (above; it was A B A C). (0.8.3) The sections are one piece in one key: B starts the loop on its predominant (the same chords turned: IV–I–V–vi for I–V–vi–IV; a one-chord loop goes to its subdominant and back), the motif and the figures the same, moved onto those chords; where the genre lifts (in V10.8.72 none of the 29 does; EXPLORE about a third of the time) C is a whole step up, a real key change stored in the section with its SCALE page (pop's last chorus). The modal loops (MINIMAL TECHNO, TECH HOUSE, EBM, KRAUT ..) keep their loop in every section. SONG writes a club form: A the drop, B the intro (drums and bass), C the build (the chords in, their filter opening over the loop, a roll at its end, the delay thrown on the last step) and D the break (no drums, no bass, the chords wetter; 0.8.3: on its predominant, but in the modal loops). Since V10.8.69 ARRANGE's rows come from a song plan of two to five minutes (above; until V10.8.68 B C A D C A, no row over about 24 s). The genres written as an arc (IDM GLITCH, IDM AMBIENT, IDM WEIRD, KRAUT, NEO CLASSIC, DREAM POP, SHOEGAZE; and EXPLORE) get an arc instead (thin, in, apex: on its predominant). Sections of yours (stored by you, not by GEN) are never overwritten: then the piece stays one loop.

Every piece replaces every track's steps, sounds, kit, mix and automation. Mutes are left as they are. The roles that play go on the first tracks (drums on the DRUM track), so with TRACKS 4 you hear the most important ones.

FORM MY LOOP: your loop made a song

Set FORM to MY LOOP and press OCT+: GEN turns the loop you are playing into a whole song, by the rules of the GENRE you picked. Nothing of your loop changes: its tracks, steps, sounds and mix stay as they are, and they are section A, the song's peak (its drop). Every other section is the genre's, played on your sounds. GEN:

  • listens to your loop: its key and mode (major, minor, dorian, mixolydian, phrygian or harmonic minor; each note weighed by its length, its velocity and whether it falls on the beat; the bass, the lowest notes, tell the tonic). Where your loop does not decide (a power riff with no third, an 808 on its root and fifth), GEN takes the genre's own mode, then the minor one, and the darker one when your loop is distorted (a track's DIST) or the genre is a heavy one: a dark loop stays dark, an E-F riff is E phrygian. DRUM-X counts too where it plays a pitch: a lane with little noise and a long ring (an 808, a tuned tom) and the notes of an EXTENDED kit's chromatic run (KICK / TOM or a lane's CHROM). A loop of drums alone has no key: GEN's own key and progression for the genre are used.
  • harmonises it again with every seed: a chord a bar (a half bar in a one-bar loop) that contains your loop's notes there (its root, third and fifth what sounds most, the bass note one of them, little of yours a semitone off them; a seventh where your loop plays it; power chords in the genres that play them). A quarter of the seeds keep the chords heard in the loop; the others draw each bar's chord by how well it fits, the genre's own chords and, in a dark loop, the minor ones more likely: another progression under the same loop, still in its key and mode.
  • adds the parts your loop lacks, only on empty tracks (no note; never on yours), by BASS, CHORDS and ARP on GENERATOR 2 (AUTO: the genre's; OFF: none): a bass where your loop has none, chords on that seed's progression where it has none, and on the arp's track a counter-melody made of your melody: the same notes moved an eighth or a beat, its first half answered, turned upside down round its first note or kept to the beats, an octave away, in your key (no melody in the loop: an arp of the chords). Their sounds and mix are the genre's. No empty track: nothing is added and the screen says NO EMPTY TRACK: ARRANGED (the other sections are still the genre's, on your sounds).
  • brings the genre into the song around the drop: B, the verse, plays the genre's drums (its own pattern: REGGAETON's dembow, HARD BASS's kicks, ...) on your kit, and the genre's bass, chords, arp and lead on your tracks' sounds, over the genre's own progression in your key (its borrowed chords and colours included); C, the build, the genre's parts on the drop's chords, its drums the verse's or your loop's (half the seeds) over four bars with a roll on the snare, clap or rim getting faster and louder, the kick out at the end, in a third of the seeds the DJ FILTER's low-pass sweep opening into the drop (V10.8.68; a high-pass before), the chords' filter rising, a stutter into the drop; D, the break, no drums and no bass, on the genre's chords or the drop's from its predominant, wetter, the synths an octave up on its last bar.
  • arranges it with SONG's rows, each seed its own: the club's plan or an arc (an arc more often in the genres that play one), the verse in the groove and in some of the intros and outros, the rows' lengths, each section's energy (how busy the arp, the lead, the chords' pulse); the intro and the outro with the drums thinned (the off-beat sixteenths out) and few layers, the layers coming in by the genre's priorities, fills at the phrases' ends (ARRANGE's FILL), and every drop row your whole loop as it is. RANDOM picks the genre by your tempo and drums (four kicks a bar from 100 BPM HOUSE, over 138 BPM HARD TECHNO, else KRAUT from 110 BPM, DREAM POP below); EXPLORE picks a different genre each seed, one whose tempo is near your loop's, and harmonises more freely. Muted tracks of yours stay muted. The tempo and the swing stay your loop's.

It is a SONG as GEN's are: PLAY plays it (ARRANGE shows its rows), SAVE keeps it (all its parts and its rows, as any GEN song: a draft until you save it). OCT+ again throws another seed: another song from the same loop (the parts it added are made again). UNDO (GLO + G4) brings your loop back as it was, in PART mode (LOOP before V10.8.47), the song gone (from a song you had saved, open it again from SAVE > PROJECT: it is still there). An empty loop: THE LOOP IS EMPTY, nothing made.

Sound dice (EDIT + SELECT)

(0.9.9-seq2f: EDIT + SELECT is the sound dice again; seq2e had given it to the presets, which stay on PRESETS.) The sound dice: the selected track loads a random factory preset of its engine and each engine parameter moves up to a quarter of its range. On DRUM, both sides of every kit sound are rolled around the factory kit. You hear it at once under KEEP DICED SOUND? (DRUM: KEEP DICED KIT?): turn SELECT again for another roll, OCT+ OK keeps it, OCT− CANCEL brings back the sound you had before the first roll (only that track's sound: the music plays on). After OK, GLO held + G4 still undoes it.

Sequence, LFO and FX dice (gone)

These dice are gone: the LFO's and the FX's (LFO + SELECT, FX + SELECT) were removed in V10.7.66 and the sequence's (SEQ + SELECT) in V10.8.21. The sound dice (EDIT + SELECT) stays; SEQ, LFO and FX held + SELECT now walk their section's pages.

Macro dice

The LFO layer went in V10.7.66, and with it F3 (new routes) and G3 (clear them). Random macro routes are still thrown at power-on for every track that has none (two a track, never on PITCH), and by the generator on every track that is not muted. See 10.

UNDO (GLO held + G4)

One step back over the last big change. Pressing it again goes forward (redo). The transport keeps playing. (V10.7) REC held alone does the same: hold REC past HOLD (~0.5 s) and let go without touching anything else (no key, knob, button or OCT): UNDO; hold it alone again: redo. Used with anything else it stays the REC layer (CLICK, REC Q, A3 …), and a REC tap still arms recording. GLO + G4 still works. G4 breathes on the GLO map when there is something to undo; with nothing, it says NOTHING TO UNDO.

UNDO covers: DICE ALL, a sound diced, a track cleared (REC F3, TOOLS CLEAR SEQ), CLEAR ALL SEQUENCES (SEQ + REC), NEW PROJECT, INIT and RECALL (EDIT layer or TOOLS), clearing the automation (SEQ > AUTOMATION), and a section loaded with SAVE › PART SLOTS › LOAD. It restores the music as it was: sounds, steps, automation, the kit, the punch-in lane, the macros, the tempo and global effects. It also covers every SEQ EDIT action and a range cleared with step keys + EDIT (V10.8.49–V10.8.53), a RESOUND (V10.8.54), DICE MACROS (V10.8.64), and a part saved over with the SAVE layer, SAVE + C4–F4 or SAVE + OCT+ (V10.8.52: GLO + G4 puts the part's old content back; again: saves it again).

UNDO does not cover: section jumps, quick chains and RECALL from the SAVE layer, switching project with the SAVE layer's KNOB 1, CLEAR SONG, deleting a row, SONG REC, the other saves (SAVE › PART SLOTS, SAVE › PROJECTS, user presets), user preset loads, sounds picked with PRESETS, or ordinary knob turns. It is not available while a song plays (SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT). It keeps only one step, in RAM: it's gone after power-off.

RESOUND (GLO held + A4, V10.8.54)

For a song you like with sounds you don't: hold GLO and press A4. Every track that plays a part gets a new sound for its role: a bass gets a bass, the chords a chord sound, the drums another kit. The notes, the steps, the pattern and the song stay, the next parts keep the new sounds, and the music plays on. For a generated song the sounds come from its genre; for your own song, from a genre near its tempo. Each press is a new throw (the screen says RESOUND #1234); GLO + G4 brings the sounds back (one UNDO point). Nothing to work on: NOTHING TO RESOUND. The GLO map names A4 RESOUND (V10.8.71).

9. Effects and master

FX's chain: TRACK · BUSES · DELAY · REVERB · CHORUS · SLICER · PUNCH IN · MASTER

(0.9.2; 0.9.9-snd2: MASTER last, the end of the chain) FX is one flat chain of 20 pages in eight groups (19 until OTT came in V10.8.71), its tabs TRK · BUS · DLY · REV · CHO · SLC · PCH · MST: SELECT walks every page (SENDS → DIST → AUTO PAN → OTT → BUSES → DLY → DLY 2 → DLY 3 → REVERB → REVERB 2 → CHORUS → SLICER → SL BUS → SL BUS 2 → SL PITCH → PUNCH IN → MACROS → MASTER → TAPE → EQ), an FX tap jumps to the next module (round), and there is no module picker any more (until 0.9.1 SELECT zoomed TRACK ↔ BUSES ↔ EFFECT, PRESETS picked the module and the FX tap its page). PRESETS loads the track's sounds, as everywhere.

Group Pages What the screen shows
TRACK SENDS (CHORUS DLY REV DIST) · DIST · AUTO PAN · OTT The track's set: its picture (the four sends as columns, DIST's curve with TYPE and TONE, AUTO PAN's swing with WAVE and RATE; OTT: its name large and its two bands, below).
BUSES BUSES The modules as tiles, each its picture small; with LOAD ECO CHORUS and SLICER are dark ("ECO"). Knobs: DLY (the delay's MIX), REV (the reverb's SIZE), CHO (the chorus' DEPTH), SLC (the SLICER's DEPTH).
DELAY · REVERB · CHORUS · SLICER · PUNCH IN · MASTER DLY · DLY 2 · DLY 3 — REVERB · REVERB 2 — CHORUS — SLICER · SL BUS · SL BUS 2 · SL PITCH — PUNCH IN · MACROS — MASTER · TAPE · EQ The module large. PUNCH IN: the macros M1–M4 on its four cards, OCT+ the punch-in editor (V10.8.33: the lane's picture is gone); MACROS: the macros' routes. With LOAD ECO the chain skips CHORUS and SLICER.
  • FX from another page comes back to the FX page you left.
  • The footer says FX · DELAY · DLY 2 7/20; the header shows the track, T1, in orange.
  • The pictures follow the values (a turn redraws them) and, while it plays or sounds, the sound (0.8.5, FX live): the echoes swell with the level and a pulse runs along them, the reverb's tail swells and a line sweeps it, the chorus waves run at RATE (V10.8.53: DELAY draws each echo as a column of heat cells, the first as high as MIX, each next one lower by FEEDBK, as far apart as TIME, the one sounding yellow, with 1/8 · 5 ECHOES over them; REVERB its tail as columns of cells; CHORUS two sines), the slicer frames the step playing, MASTER's meter follows the output, DIST's level is a dot on its curve, AUTO PAN's dot swings. Stopped and silent they hold still (drawn by the screen alone; nothing of the audio's time).

Per track

  • FX: DIST amount and the three sends (CHORUS, DLY, REV).
  • DIST: amount, TYPE (0 SOFT, 1 HARD, 2 FOLD, 3 CRUSH, 4 RECT, 5 AMP, and since V10.8.72 the formula types 6 RING, 7 STEPS, 8 XOR, 9 WOB, 10 SFOLD, 11 SAT, below), TONE (darker / brighter). AMP is a guitar amp: two valve stages that clip unevenly (low DIST clean, then crunch, then lead), the bias breathing with the level, and a speaker cabinet with its presence peak; TONE moves the cabinet's brightness. NOISE (V10.8.36, KNOB 4, 0–127): a low-passed noise moves the drive's gain and TONE's corner, so grain appears round every harmonic of the note; nothing is added (silence stays silent, the level as it was). Not on AMP.
  • The formula types (V10.8.72, from JIANT BYTE's formula effects, as fixed code): DIST sets the formula's amount instead of a drive, and there is no low cut and no make-up gain; TONE and DIST's fade-in work as on the other types, and DIST 0 is still off. RING: ring modulation by a sine from 110 Hz (DIST low) up to 990 Hz (DIST full). STEPS: the wave in steps, 32 levels at low DIST down to 2. XOR: the samples' bits flipped by DIST's value (digital grit). WOB: the level dipped by a triangle twice a beat, as deep as DIST (stopped, on a clock of its own). SFOLD: a sine wavefolder, more folds as DIST rises. SAT: a saturation driven up to 21 times, its level coming down to half as DIST rises. NOISE moves the formula's input and TONE's corner. The page draws SOFT's curve with the type's name. The SENDS have no drive of their own: SENDS' fourth knob is this same DIST.
  • AUTO PAN: the track's pan swung left and right around its PAN. DEPTH (0 = off), RATE, SYNC (BEAT: RATE in divisions 4BAR … 1/32, locked to the bar; FREE: RATE in Hz), WAVE (SIN, TRI, SAW, SQR, S&H).
  • OTT (V10.8.71): the track's two-band compressor, below.
  • FILTER: see 4.

OTT (FX › TRACK, V10.8.71)

A two-band compressor on each track, from JIANT BYTE. It brings the quiet parts up and squeezes the loud parts down, in a low band and a high band, then drives the two into a soft clip. It sits after DIST in the track's chain. The page is TRACK's fourth, after AUTO PAN.

  • DEPTH (0–100 %): how much. 0 = off: the track skips OTT completely, the sound is exactly as without it (bit for bit) and it costs no CPU. The depth is squared up to 70 and rises faster above it (V10.8.72): 30 does about a tenth of what 100 does, 50 a quarter, 60 about a third, 70 half, 80 about 85 %, 90 nearly all of it. 30–60 is musical, 80–100 brutal.
  • What 100 does (V10.8.72, much harder than V10.8.71): each band is pulled up towards −18 dBFS, almost a dB for every dB it is under, by as much as +36 dB (a band at −46 dBFS comes up about 27 dB); over −22 dBFS it is squeezed 20:1, by as much as −36 dB. Then the two bands together are driven up to +9 dB into a soft clip: dense and saturated, never a hard clip, never over −0.3 dBFS. Very quiet sound (under −66 dBFS) is not brought up, so no hiss comes with it. Each block's peaks are read first, so a hit after silence is not boosted by the silence's gain, and a gain going down acts at once. (V10.8.71: up to +28 dB under −12 dBFS, about 10:1 over −15 dBFS, a limiter over −3 dBFS.)
  • TIME (8.8 ms … 1.41 s): how fast it follows each band's level (the release; the attack is about 1 ms up to 50 and slower above). The default is 48 (V10.8.72, about 33 ms on the card: it pumps with the kick; V10.8.71: 72, 185 ms). A project or user preset saved with V10.8.71 opens with each track's TIME 24 lower (its 72 comes in as 48).
  • UP/DN (−100 … +98 %): the balance. Turned left, less upward (the quiet parts come up less); turned right, less downward (the loud parts are squeezed less). 0: both in full.
  • X-OVER (63 Hz … 4.2 kHz, 187 Hz by default): where the low band ends and the high band starts.
  • The page: OTT's name large, OFF under it at DEPTH 0, and two columns, LOW and HIGH. In each, the band's level as it plays (dim grey cells) and the gain it gets right now: a bar up or down from the middle line with its dB, coloured by how much (cool a little, hot a lot).
  • HOME: on ECO a track with OTT on shows an OTT tag under its number, in the same colour.
  • CPU: under the overload guard OTT works at half its depth; while the load stays over 90 % it eases out. The sound is never cut.
  • Saved with the project and with a user preset (SAVE › USER): all four values, even at DEPTH 0. Projects and presets from before V10.8.71 open with OTT off. The web editor reaches it too (editor protocol 1.4); a change made on the device, by GEN or by RESOUND is not pushed to it (it reads it again).
  • GEN (V10.8.72) puts OTT on the drums, the bass and, in one seed in two, the lead of the electronic genres' pieces, and RESOUND sets or clears it on the tracks it gives new sounds (see GEN).

SLICER (one, on a bus)

  • SLICER: MODE OFF, GATE, STUT; PAT 1–16; RATE 1/8 … 32T; DEPTH.
  • SL BUS / SL BUS 2: ON / OFF for what goes in: T1–T6 and FX (the delay, reverb and chorus returns). Everything on chops the whole mix after the effects; with FX off the tails ring free.
  • SL PITCH: the repeats follow a 16-step pitch sequence (±24 semitones). KNOB 1 the step, KNOB 2 its pitch, LEN, QUANT (CHR or SCL: the song's scale).
  • Each section keeps its own SLICER settings. With LOAD ECO there is no SLICER (its tracks go straight to the mix).

Delay

  • DLY: TIME (synced divisions 4BAR … 1/32, or free times from 5 ms to 2.95 s; V10.8: the dotted 1/4D, 1/8D, 1/16D too, placed by length: 4BAR, 2BAR, 1/1, 1/2, 1/4D, 1/4, 1/8D, 1/8, 1/16D, 8T, 1/16, 16T, 1/32; saved projects keep their times), FEEDBK, TONE (below the middle darker, above thinner), MIX. FEEDBK behaves like an analog delay's (a tape, a PT2399; 0.6.86, 0.6.89): with TONE in the middle (50 %) each repeat is a copy of what went in; at 100 % the echoes hold their level for a long time (they fade very slowly and are never cut off), and past 100 % they grow into themselves and hold, saturating softly instead of clipping (turn it back down to let them die). Up to 80 % it is as before. TONE is resonant: from the middle down a low-pass sweeping from ~8 kHz to ~250 Hz, from the middle up a low cut sweeping from ~70 Hz to ~3 kHz, both with a peak at the cutoff, so the repeats get darker or thinner and narrow to a band each pass (dub style), and at either end with FEEDBK high the loop self-oscillates at that band.
  • Long times (0.8.4): every division plays its real length up to 2.97 s, the longest (before, anything past 1.49 s was cut to 1.49 s: 1/2 below 81 BPM, 1/1 below 162 BPM, 2BAR, 4BAR). To fit them the delay's line runs at three rates, chosen by TIME on its own:
TIME Line Top end of the repeats
up to 0.74 s full rate full range, as before
0.74 s – 1.49 s half rate flat to ~9.5 kHz, -3 dB at ~10.4 kHz
1.49 s – 2.97 s a quarter rate flat to ~4.7 kHz, -3 dB at ~5.2 kHz

So the longer the time, the darker the tail, like a tape or bucket-brigade delay. Only the top end is lost: there is no grit or aliasing (anything folded back is more than 70 dB down) and no extra noise. The rate is applied once, so the repeats do not get darker with each pass (only TONE and FEEDBK do that). MOD, the GRAIN delay, PING, WIDE, TYPE and TONE work the same at every rate. On the two slower rates the first echo comes ~1 ms (half) or ~4 ms (quarter) late; the repeats stay exactly TIME apart. When TIME crosses 0.74 s or 1.49 s (knob, tempo, automation, a project or section load, an external clock) the delay fades out over 3 ms and starts again empty. That leaves a short gap: the echoes already in the line are dropped, but there is no click. A clock that wavers around a boundary does not restart it again and again. Long echoes come back at full level even when nothing else is playing. - DLY 2: WIDE (the right echo later), and the GRAIN delay: PITCH (±12 semitones per repeat) and SPRAY. With LOAD LITE or ECO the GRAIN delay plays as a plain delay (the card says LITE / ECO). MOD (0.6.86): the tape's drift, slow WOW and fast FLUTTER on the repeats (0, the default: none, exact copies; ~20 a tape's; up to a seasick chorus); the repeats stay bright while they drift (0.6.89); saved with the project. - DLY 3 (0.6.90): TYPE: ANALOG (the default: the soft saturation, the resonant TONE, FEEDBK past 100 % self-oscillating) or DIGITAL (clean repeats, TONE a plain filter, FEEDBK 100 % at most: past it the repeats just hold, never grow). PING: ON sends the repeats left, right, left … across the stereo field, each one FEEDBK softer (TIME up to 1.49 s since 0.8.4, the right side at twice TIME; WIDE and the GRAIN delay out of it). Saved with the project. - GATE (V10.8.44): on DLY, hold OCT+ and turn KNOB 4 (its card reads GATE while OCT+ is held; MIX keeps its value; OCT+ alone is still the octave). 0 (the default): off, the delay exactly as without it. Above 0 the delay listens to what is sent to it: open while that is louder than about −36 dB, held GATE / 64 of a quarter after it falls (16: a 1/16, 64: a quarter, 127: two quarters), then MIX and FEEDBK glide to 0 (about 12 ms): the repeats stop with the phrase, and the line starts empty when the gate opens again. Saved with the project.

Reverb (five models)

REVERB > TYPE picks the model; SIZE is the decay on every model. KNOB 3 and 4 change meaning with the type:

TYPE What it is KNOB 3 KNOB 4
ROOM Classic room DAMP PRE (pre-delay, ms)
SPRING Amp spring tank DAMP PRE
SHIMR (shimmer) Rises an octave on every pass DAMP AIR (±24 st: darker and lower / airier and higher)
RESO Four strings tuned to the song's scale FOLLOW (OFF / T1–T6: the chord follows the lowest note that track plays) PITCH (the chord 0–14 steps up the scale)
CLOUD Granular wash that starts with the note (V10.8.36: half the grains just behind the present, the others 1, 2 or 3 sixteenths back); SIZE at max freezes it DAMP AIR

REVERB 2: MOD (modulation depth), RATE, FILT (input tone: darker / brighter; 0.6.86 resonant, a band at the cutoff to carve the room's place), WIDE.

GATE (V10.8.44): on REVERB, hold OCT+ and turn KNOB 4 (its card reads GATE while OCT+ is held; PRE keeps its value). 0 (the default): off. Above 0 the reverb's return is open while what is sent to it is louder than about −36 dB, held GATE / 64 of a quarter after it falls (16: a 1/16, 64: a quarter, 127: two quarters), then cut over about 6 ms: the gated snare of the 80s, or a tail that never covers the next hit. It works on every TYPE. Saved with the project.

With LOAD LITE, SHIMMER and CLOUD play as ROOM and RESO as SPRING; with LOAD ECO every reverb plays as SPRING. The settings stay; the TYPE card shows LITE or ECO under its value.

Changing the model (the knob, automation or motion, a project or song section, MIDI, the editor, or LOAD going LITE / ECO and back) cuts the old model's tail with a short fade (under a millisecond, no click) and the new one starts silent. Since 0.8.4 coming back to CLOUD starts an empty cloud, a frozen one too (it used to resume the cloud left from before).

Chorus

CHORUS: RATE, DEPTH, STEREO (0 as always, down to mono, up to about twice as wide) and MIX (V10.8.36, KNOB 4, 0–100 %): at 0 the chorus as it was; towards 100 each track's dry goes down by its CHORUS send and the three voices become one, in the middle: MIX 100 and the send whole, a vibrato. Hidden with LOAD ECO (a track's chorus send card then says ECO).

MASTER

  • CLIP: saturation that adds character, not volume.
  • PUNCH: fattens the DRUM tracks.
  • DUCK: the kick pulls the rest down; REL is its release.

DJ FILTER (0.9.1; GLO › MIXER's KNOB 4 after a tap of OCT+, V10.8.38)

On GLO › MIXER, KNOB 4 is the tempo (BPM) or the DJ FILTER: a short tap of OCT+ on that page turns it from one to the other, and the card's label says which, BPM or DJ FILT (with a note held OCT+ is the expression key, as everywhere). Since V10.8.54 the screen also says it: KNOB 4: DJ FILTER or KNOB 4: BPM. From V10.8.3 to V10.8.37 it had no knob on the device (GLO › LIVE, where it had gone in V10.37, was removed); MIDI, the web editor and automation reach it as before.

One knob on the whole mix, just before CLIP and the leveler. In the middle (OFF) it is out of the chain: nothing is processed and the sound is exactly as without it. Turned left it is a low-pass sweeping down (darker: from ~15 kHz a detent off the middle to ~70 Hz at the end); turned right a high-pass sweeping up (thinner: from ~30 Hz to ~6 kHz). The sweep follows the ear (each detent the same musical step), with a mild resonance that grows a little toward the ends. The card shows the cutoff and the side (1.2k LP, 400 HP, OFF) and a small response curve where the bar would be. - It glides: the cutoff follows the knob in ~6 ms, no zipper; going into the chain, out of it and from one side to the other it crossfades (~6 ms), so crossing the middle never clicks. Turning the knob, it stops once in the middle. - Automation: armed and playing, turning it records it on the selected track (SEQ › AUTOMATION, AUTO LIST shows DJ FILT rows; automation only, no lock); a stop or the loop's restart brings back where the knob was. The editor can set and record it too. - Saved with the project (in the place a never-used global had: every older project loads with it OFF). Firmware before 0.9.1 loads a newer project without its DJ FILTER and its automation. - Cost: nothing in the middle; on, about 200 instructions a sample on the FM-1 (the CPU TEST song +1.7 % on the host).

10. Modulation and macros

  • ENV DEST: the envelope to FILTER, PITCH, SHAPE; LOOP ON: with the note held, the envelope goes back to the attack when it reaches sustain (an ADSR-shaped LFO).
  • ENV 2 (V10.22, after ENV DEST): a second ADSR per voice that goes nowhere by itself: pick SRC ENV2 on a MOD slot and send it to any DEST, like the LFO.
  • LFO: RATE, WAVE (SIN, TRI, SAW, SQR, S&H, DRIFT: V10.36, a smooth random wander for drones and pads that breathe; with RATE 4BAR … 16BAR it drifts slowly), MODE, FADE; LFO 2: PHASE. LFO DEST: PITCH, FILTER, SHAPE, AMP.
  • RATE is free in Hz; turn it left past the slowest and it goes in time with the tempo (16BAR and 8BAR, V10.27, then 4BAR, 2BAR, 1BAR, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8D, 1/4T, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32), locked to the bar while the transport plays (in TRIG, PHASE is its offset), in either MODE: a note never moves it then.
  • MODE TRIG: a new phrase (a note with none held) restarts the LFO at PHASE (LFO 2) and fades it in again over FADE; a note played legato over another does not. MODE FREE: no note restarts anything: the LFO just runs, and FADE fades it in only once, when the project loads or when you turn MODE to FREE. In FREE, PHASE is dimmed: the phase TRIG had is kept for when you go back to TRIG. (Until 0.9.18 FREE was PHASE turned left past 0, and FREE still faded in again on every phrase; projects keep their mode: PHASE FREE opens as MODE FREE.)
  • MOD matrix: 4 slots per track (KNOB 1 picks the slot).
  • Sources: OFF, LFO, ENV, VEL, KEY, RAND, MODW (MIDI CC1), AT (aftertouch), EXPR (CC11), M1–M4, STEP (MSEQ), NOISE (a smooth random wander, a new value about every 46 ms: a living wobble on the filter, the pan, a send), PROX (V10.14), ENV2 (V10.22), IN ENV (V10.54: the level of what comes in on the audio input, see Sound from outside), T1 ENV – T6 ENV (another track's level) and OCT+ / OCT− (V10.7.22: the expression keys).
  • Destinations: PITCH, CUT, SHP, AMP, PAN, DIST, CHO, DLY, REV, RATE (LFO rate), VIB, E1–E8 (the engine's own EDIT knobs, shown by name), CLIP and PNCH (the master), and (0.7.0) the FX buses: D.TIM D.FB D.TON D.MIX (DELAY TIME, FDBK, TONE, MIX), R.SIZ R.DMP (REVERB SIZE, DAMP), C.RAT C.DEP (CHORUS RATE, DEPTH). AMT 64 at a full source = the parameter's whole range; every track's slots on the same bus add. A STEP source (the mod sequence) on D.TIM sequences the delay time.
  • AMT (V10.8.51): −200 … +198 % (it was −100 … +98 %). 100 % is the old full amount, so a slot can now push twice as far. The macros' routes (FX › PUNCH IN › MACROS, AMOUNT) go as far. Projects, presets and routes saved before load as they were.
  • MSEQ: a 16-step modulation sequencer per track, like a CV sequencer. KNOB 1 picks the step, KNOB 2 sets its level, LEN and SLEW; DIV on MSEQ 2. Use it from MOD with SRC STEP.

Macros M1–M4

  • Hold LFO: KNOB 1–4 become M1–M4, and the map shows where each one goes ("NO ROUTE: MOD SRC" if nowhere).
  • Let go: they stay latched — KNOB 1–4 keep moving the macros on any page — until you press LFO again.
  • Every power-on starts with random routes (two per track) on tracks that have none. F3 rolls new routes on the tracks that are sounding; G3 clears them. (V10.8) Random routes (power-on, F3, GEN, the dice) never aim at PITCH: a macro drifting the pitch put whole tracks out of tune. Set a PITCH route by hand on LFO > MOD.
  • Routes are ordinary MOD slots (SRC M1–M4): edit them by hand on LFO > MOD. Macro values are saved with each section.

11. Performance

Live sequences: the black keys of SEQ › STEP FX (V10.8.35)

GLO › LIVE (0.9.11) was removed in V10.8.3; its modifiers came back in V10.8.35, compact, on the black keys of SEQ › STEP FX. Each track's four sequences A–D are played from HOME › JAM.

On SEQ › STEP FX (and STEP FX 2) the white keys hold step components; the black keys 1 to 9, counted from the left, change how the sequencer walks the selected track, never the steps:

Black key What it does How
1 RATE x2 (twice as fast) held
2 RATE x3/2 held
3 RATE x2/3 held
4 REVERSE (backwards) held
5 PING-PONG (there and back) held
6 RANDOM (steps at random) held
7 THIN (half the steps silent) held
8 GIRO − (the playhead a step back) a press
9 GIRO + (the playhead a step on) a press
  • The held ones come in on the next 1/16 and, let go, the track is back in phase: it lands where it would have been had you touched nothing. Several at once add up (the last RATE and the last direction count).
  • GIRO stays: the other key undoes it, or PLAY again.
  • None of this is saved or changes the written sequence. A banner names each one as you press it.
  • The black keys 10 and 11 are still page back / on.

Punch-in FX (hold FX)

Effects that act while their key is held and go back exactly when you let go. The audio ones work on the master: the whole mix, what comes in on an EXT track too. This is the factory map (V10.7.59); the punch-in editor (OCT+ on FX › PUNCH IN) lets you change what each key does.

  • On the audio (the white keys at the left): REPEAT 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 (F3 G3 A3): a stutter of what just played; REVERSE (B3): each stretch, the one before it backwards; FREEZE (C4): the reverb frozen (nothing new goes into it and its SIZE goes to the top). On the blacks: TAPE STOP (A#4): the mix slows down like a tape to silence; PITCH UP / PITCH DOWN (C#5 D#5): the mix's pitch ramps 12 semitones up or down over a bar and stays there; STRETCH (F#5): half a beat recorded, then played twice as slow at its own pitch, round and round. REPEAT, REVERSE, TAPE STOP and STRETCH come in on the next 1/16 while playing; of the buffer effects the last one pressed plays. Below about 81 BPM, REPEAT 1/8 records at a lower quality (lo-fi), and much slower it is shown dimmed.
  • On the notes: OCT− / OCT+ (D4 E4), 1/2 TEMPO (F4), DEC− (short, plucky) / DEC+ (long) (G4 A4), STUTTER 1/8 / 1/16 (B4 C5), ATK+ (slow attacks, drums too) (D5), ARP (E5; on a DRUM track a new fill every press), RANDOM (F5). They come in on the next 1/16 and act on every track. G#4 LOOP 3: every track repeats its last 3 steps while held; let go and it is back where it would have been.
  • Knobs while FX is held (V10.7.59): the four macros M1–M4, moving whatever you routed them to on FX › MACROS. They start from the value they had and go back to it when FX is let go (with FX LATCH they stay; OCT− ALL OFF puts them back). The earlier knobs (FILTER, CRUSH, THROW, DEPTH) are gone: to throw a track into the delay, route a macro to DLY (it moves every track's delay send).
  • Black keys 1–6: mute T1–T6 while held (not saved).
  • G5 CLR AUTO: FX + G5 empties the punch-in lane (its automation) and nothing else, stopped or playing; while recording it erases only where the playhead passes.

The punch-in lane: each section has a lane, 64 steps of 1/16 (4 bars) by default; LEN and RES keep the project's value and are no longer edited on the device. With REC armed and playing (not during a song), the note effects (D4–F5) you hold are recorded into it, one per step (the audio ones and the mutes are not recorded). Hold FX + G5 while playing to erase where the playhead passes; stopped, FX + G5 erases the whole lane. REC held + FX also clears it (along with the track's FX automation). Saved with the section. The page that drew it (FX › PUNCH, with LEN, RES and the lane's cells) is gone (V10.8.27, V10.8.33): FX › PUNCH IN has the macros M1–M4 on its knobs and opens the editor with OCT+.

Lock: hold FX until its map opens and let go without touching anything: the FX layer stays open ([FX] LOCKED), as the macros do with LFO; the keys play the effects (momentary: held on, let go off), the knobs are FX's macros and OCT− is ALL OFF, with both hands free. Press FX again to unlock (latched effects you left on stay on). Held with keys or knobs, FX works as before and closes when let go.

FX LATCH (MENU > CONTROL > FX LATCH, OFF by default; ON by default from 0.6.44 to 0.6.63): ON, a key pressed with FX toggles its effect on and off, the knob macros keep their values, FX + OCT− turns everything off (FX ALL OFF). Latched effects are not recorded into the lane.

Mutes and solos

  • GLO held: black keys 1–6 mute T1–T6 (latched, saved with the project and in scenes); F3–D4 solo while held; black keys 7–10 mute the DRUM-X groups; E4 unmutes everything.
  • MIXER's KNOB 3 is the selected track's MUTE; KNOB 4 is BPM or, after a tap of OCT+, the DJ FILTER (V10.8.38).
  • EDIT held on a DRUM track: black keys 1–8 mute each DRUM-X sound.
  • FX held: black keys 1–6 mute while held.

Live layers and the song

The SAVE layer (section jumps on the bar, quick chains, store, recall, the JAM take's REC) is described in 7. GLO + PLAY restarts from the top at once, without stopping; SEQ + PLAY (V10.8.40) is RESYNC: every track from its first step on the next bar.

12. Saving and loading

This is the chapter to read carefully. JIANT keeps several kinds of data in different places, saved in different ways.

The big picture

  • The music is what's playing now, in RAM: all six tracks' sounds and steps, automation, effects, tempo.
  • Sections (A–D of each of the 6 projects) are where you save music permanently, in flash.
  • The arrangement (rows, END, scenes) belongs to the project and saves itself.
  • User presets (32 slots) save single sounds.
  • Settings (the MENU, TRACKS, LOAD) save themselves.
  • The autosave is a safety copy of the music, so you find it again after power-off. It is not a save into a section, and it does not happen at power-off.

What is saved where

What Where it lives How it gets saved Survives power-off?
The music now (sounds, steps, automation, tempo, effects, kit, macros, punch-in lane, SLICER) RAM Not saved by itself — store it into a section. The autosave keeps a copy. Only via the autosave
A section (A–D of a project) Flash SAVE › PART SLOTS › SAVE (stopped), or SAVE layer C4–F4 / OCT+ Yes (layer stores: once you stop)
The arrangement (rows, bars, END, scenes) of each project Flash (song index) Automatically, ~2 s after a change while stopped Yes
User presets U01–U32 (one sound + a 16-step pattern) Flash SAVE > USER > SAVE (stopped) Yes
Settings (MENU, TRACKS, LOAD, favourites) Flash Automatically (MENU: when it closes; while playing: after you stop) Yes
The autosave Flash, its own place 10 s after the last change, stopped and idle, at most once a minute Yes (restored at power-on if RESTORE LAST is ON)
The FM6 voice bank B1–B32 Flash, its own place Sent from the web editor Yes (not in the backup: keep the .syx)
UNDO RAM — No

How the autosave really works

  • It writes a copy of the music after 10 seconds without changes, only when the transport is stopped, no key or button is held and nothing is sounding, and at most once a minute.
  • It does not save when you switch off. If you change something and power off within those seconds, that last change is lost. To be safe: stop, wait ~10 s, or better, save into a section.
  • At power-on the device starts at zero, as NEW PROJECT leaves it (V10.6e: T1 DRUM-X, T2 ANALOG, T3 PHASE, T4 FM6, T5 VOICE, T6 ANIMAL, each its preset's sound, dry; no steps). With MENU > SYSTEM > RESTORE LAST ON the autosave becomes the music instead (the screen says RESTORED). RESTORE LAST is OFF by default since 0.6.40: no autosave at all.
  • After a crash, a hang or a failed start, the autosave is not restored (the music that was playing could be what crashed).

SAVE's chain: TOOLS · PROJECT · SOUND

SAVE is a chain of five pages in three groups, as every section: SELECT walks TOOLS → PART SLOTS → PROJECTS → USER → PRESETS, a SAVE tap jumps to the next group (round). At power-on SAVE opens PROJECTS. (The song's pages, JAM · TAKE · ARRANGE, are HOME's since V10.7.63; until 0.9.1 SELECT zoomed LIBRARY ↔ PROJECT ↔ SOUND.)

Group Pages What the screen shows Knobs
TOOLS TOOLS The tools as a list. TARGET, ACTION, —, DO (OCT+ held)
PROJECT PART SLOTS · PROJECTS PART SLOTS: the open project's four parts large, each with its name (unnamed: its bars in the song, 12 BARS, 0 BARS in no row; USED until V10.8.47; or EMPTY), the one playing marked PLAYING (NOW until V10.8.47); under them the song's rows as chips, ARRANGE PART+BARS (A8 = part A, 8 bars). / PROJECTS: the six projects as tiles: the number, the name (its part A's), the four parts A–D as chips (stored: in the part's colour; empty: dark); the project open tinted and framed violet. PART, PLAY/EDIT (V10.8.47; was LOAD), ERASE (V10.17), SAVE / PROJECT, LOAD, ERASE, SAVE
SOUND USER · PRESETS The track's being (its engine's creature, alive with its sound), the track and its sound under it; at the right the 32 user slots (a stored one: its engine's creature small and its name) or the factory sounds. SLOT, LOAD, ERASE, SAVE / No., ENG, FAV, LIST
  • SAVE from another page comes back to the SAVE page you left; USER and PART SLOTS come with their SAVE already picked: SAVE, OCT+, OCT+ stores the sound (or the part), as before. Reached from inside, SAVE is not picked for you (KNOB 4 to the right).
  • The other projects' tiles are read from the flash a project a frame (the headers only: no loading, nothing the audio notices) and kept until a project is saved, loaded or renamed.
  • The footer says SAVE · PROJECT · PROJECTS 3/5. The OCT+ / OCT− hints are not drawn on these pages: the armed card says OCT+.

To save a project section

  1. Stop the transport (saving needs it stopped: otherwise STOP TO SAVE).
  2. Press SAVE and turn SELECT to PART SLOTS (the PROJECT group's first page).
  3. KNOB 1: the part A–D, drawn large with its name (or its bars in the song, or EMPTY).
  4. KNOB 4 to the right: SAVE is picked ([OCT+]). Press OCT+.
  5. If the part already holds something: OVERWRITE PROJECT A? (with its name). OCT+ YES.
  6. The NAME screen opens with a name ready. Edit it or not, then OCT+ writes. OCT− cancels and writes nothing.
  7. The screen says SAVED.

A section stores the music including the tempo and global effects. The project's name is its section A's name. PART SLOTS always works on the project that is open. To write into another project, see Copying.

To erase a section (V10.17)

  1. Stop the music. SAVE › PART SLOTS, KNOB 1 to the part.
  2. KNOB 3 to the right: ERASE is picked. Press OCT+: ERASE PART B? (with its name).
  3. OCT+ erases it (OCT− cancels): the part is EMPTY again, in flash too (its chip goes dark on PROJECTS). The music you are hearing stays as it is.

A whole project: SAVE › PROJECTS, KNOB 1 the project, KNOB 3 ERASE, OCT+: ERASE PROJECT n?.

To load a section

  1. SAVE › PART SLOTS, KNOB 1 the part.
  2. KNOB 2 to the right (PLAY/EDIT; LOAD until V10.8.47; the footer says OCT+ PLAY), press OCT+.

While the loop (or a quick chain) plays, the part comes in on the next bar, as SAVE + F3–B3 does (V10.8.47; it cut in at once before). Stopped, or while a song plays, it loads as before: it stops playback and replaces the music: sounds, steps, automation, the kit, the punch-in lane, the macros, and the tempo, effects, MIDI routing and clock settings stored with it. The arrangement stays. If you didn't mean it, GLO + G4 (UNDO) brings back what you had.

Quick store while playing (SAVE layer)

Hold SAVE and press C4–F4 (SAVE A–D; the screen says SAVED A) to store the music into section A–D of the current project, or OCT+ (SAVE) to store into the section playing. This works while playing, without naming. The store is in RAM at once and goes to flash when you stop. If you power off before stopping, it's lost — so stop before switching off.

Saving over a part (V10.8.52): if the part already holds music, the screen first asks OVERWRITE A?, with UNDO: GLO + G4 under it. OCT+ saves, OCT− leaves the part as it was. It asks once for each part, until another project opens. After saving, GLO + G4 puts the part's old content back; press it again to save once more. An empty part is saved at once.

Copying
