  • A section to another letter: PLAY/EDIT it, then SAVE it into the other letter (SAVE › PART SLOTS); or, playing, hold SAVE and press F3 (PLAY A), then D4 (SAVE B). See Copy, paste and duplicate.
  • The whole song to another project ("save as"): stopped, SAVE › PROJECTS, KNOB 1 to the other project (it is not opened), KNOB 4 SAVE, OCT+ (see SAVE SONG AS). A project with music asks OVERWRITE PROJECT n? first. On the NAME screen KNOB 3 picks SONG (everything) or LOOP (the music now, alone); the screen says SAVED SONG n (or SAVED LOOP n).
  • A generator draft (V10.8.52): saved this way, the draft ends: project n is the open project from then on, so SAVE + C4, the flash writes and the autosave go there, and RESTORE LAST brings this song back after power-off. (Before V10.8.52 it stayed a draft and RESTORE LAST gave back the music from before the generator.)

Switching projects

  • On SAVE › PROJECTS, KNOB 1 only picks a project (V10.7.20): nothing is opened. KNOB 2 LOAD + OCT+ opens it, KNOB 4 SAVE + OCT+ writes the song you have into it, KNOB 3 ERASE + OCT+ empties it.
  • With the SAVE layer's KNOB 1 (hold SAVE, turn, let go) the project changes and its section A becomes the music (if it has one). The previous music is replaced and UNDO cannot bring it back — save it first.
  • Both need the transport stopped (STOP TO CHANGE PROJECT / STOP TO CHANGE SONG). Sections stored with the SAVE layer are written to flash before switching.

Naming (the NAME screen)

Opens when you save a section or a user preset, and with SAVE held + C5 (NAME, 0.9.2; until 0.9.1 an EDIT tap) on SAVE › USER, PART SLOTS or PROJECTS (renames the selected slot, part or project; only the name is written). Up to 12 characters, upper case.

Control Does
White keys Letters phone-style: AB, CD, EF, GH, IJK, LM, NO, PQ, RS, TU, VW, XYZ, then 123, 456, 789, 0-. — tap again within 0.8 s for the next character
Black keys (by name) F# cursor left, G# space, A# cursor right, C# delete, D# switch ABC / 123 (digits and symbols, one per key)
KNOB 1 move the cursor
KNOB 2 change the character at the cursor
OCT+ / OCT− write / cancel

An empty name: a project section gets none, a user preset an automatic one.

The same screen types a VOICE track's lyric (EDIT > WORDS, OCT+): up to 63 characters, the field scrolls with the cursor, KNOB 3 throws the dice, and OCT+ sets it even while playing (it is not a flash write).

User presets (SAVE > USER)

32 slots for single sounds. SAVE comes back to this page with SAVE already picked (when you left SAVE on it, as at power-on), so SAVE, OCT+, OCT+ saves the selected track's sound with the offered name.

  • KNOB 1: the slot (U01–U32). KNOB 2 LOAD, KNOB 3 ERASE (asks first), KNOB 4 SAVE (asks before overwriting, then NAME). Turn the knob right to pick, OCT+ to do it. Saving and erasing need the transport stopped.
  • A user preset stores the engine, its sound parameters and a 16-step pattern; an FM6 sound keeps its patch.
  • It does not store the DRUM-X kit (that lives in the project sections).
  • Loading one loads the sound only.
  • Your user presets also appear when browsing with PRESETS, after the factory sounds.

Old projects and old settings (V10.8.51, V10.8.59)

  • Projects saved before V10.7 (before the SLICER bus, with the step components of before 0.9.9, a retired engine such as SAMPLE, PHYS, GRAIN or SLICE, or the old GM drum part) are no longer converted on load (V10.8.51). Loading one says OLD PROJECT: OPEN IN STUDIO (LOAD no longer says EMPTY SLOT for them). The project is never erased or written over by loading: it stays in the flash as it was. Open it with JIANT Studio's converter, which loads it and saves it in today's format; or make a complete backup first.
  • The very old formats (FUN7 to FUNB: Felucca 1.0 / 1.1 and JIANT up to 0.5) say the same, but Studio's converter does not read them either: open them in V10.7.13 or earlier and save them again there.
  • Settings (V10.8.59): the first settings formats, PER1 and PER2 (Felucca's, before JIANT 0.6), are no longer migrated. If your FM-1 still had them, the global settings (the MENU) start from their defaults once; set them again. The later formats (PER3, PER4) are read as before.

Saving FAQ

I switched off and my last changes are gone. The autosave only writes after 10 s of no changes while stopped, at most once a minute, never at power-off. Stop and wait a moment, or save into a section.

It says STOP TO SAVE. Saving into a section or a user preset writes flash, which pauses the audio for a moment, so it only happens stopped. Press PLAY to stop and try again (the NAME screen stays open; PLAY there only stops).

It says SAVED (NO FLASH). The flash chip wasn't detected, so the save only went to RAM. It survives a reset, not a power-off. Restart the device; if it keeps saying it, see 16.

It says SECTION 90% FULL / TOO FULL TO SAVE / SECTION FULL. A section has a fixed size. Very busy music (six tracks of chords on all 64 steps plus lots of automation) can outgrow it. Saving a section that doesn't fit says SECTION FULL and leaves the stored one untouched. Shorten patterns, clear unused steps or automation.

I stored with the SAVE layer while playing and lost it. Layer stores reach flash when you stop. Stop before switching off.

Is my arrangement saved? Yes, automatically, a couple of seconds after each change while stopped.

Where's my drum kit in a user preset? User presets don't store the DRUM-X kit; save the project section instead.

Can I back everything up? Yes: the web editor's complete backup includes all 6 projects (a backup made before V10.6p holds 8: restoring it brings 1–6 back and says which stayed in the file) with their sections, arrangements and scenes, the user presets and the settings. See 15.

13. System: TRACKS, LOAD and the MENU

TRACKS (GLO > SYSTEM, KNOB 1 — also MENU > AUDIO > TRACKS)

  • 4 (the default): T1–T4 play; T5 and T6 are asleep. They keep their sound, steps and mix and cost nothing. If a note is sent to an asleep track (a key, MIDI, its steps) or PLAY starts with steps on them, the screen says T5-T6 ASLEEP and GLO>SYSTEM>TRACKS 6. Asleep tracks are dim on the GLO map, greyed on HOME and the MIXER.
  • 6: all six tracks play. Watch the header's load.

LOAD (GLO > SYSTEM, KNOB 2 — also MENU > AUDIO > LOAD (SYSTEM until 0.9.11))

How heavy the sound may get.

LOAD What changes while it sounds
FULL (default) Everything as set.
LITE SHIMMER and CLOUD reverbs play as ROOM, RESO as SPRING; the GRAIN delay plays plain; FM6 plays two voices. The screen draws lighter: the beings and graphs animate at about 20 frames a second with simpler outlines, and values change at once (no rolling digits).
ECO LITE, plus every reverb plays as a light SPRING, no SLICER (its tracks go straight to the mix), no chorus (their pages are hidden), at most 4 voices per synth track and 6 voices between all tracks (8 otherwise, 12 with both cores; the drums count too). When the load climbs, nearly silent tails are let go sooner. The screen at about 14 frames a second, the beings simpler still.

LOAD only changes how things are rendered: projects keep their settings and sound as saved on FULL (or on another FM-1). The cards of swapped effects say LITE or ECO. LOAD frees CPU, not RAM: the firmware reserves all its memory at start-up. The CPU card (KNOB 4 on SYSTEM) and the header's load (a number 0–99 since V10.8.45) show the audio load. TRACKS and LOAD are device settings, not part of a project.

SYSTEM 2 (GLO > SYSTEM 2)

Gone in V10.8.38. It was a status page (USB, TRS IN, BT) with nothing to edit. Bluetooth is set in the MENU (hold HOME, tab SYSTEM, row BLUETOOTH; OCT+ there opens the PROX page). GLO's SETUP group is now GLOBAL · SYSTEM · KEY SPLIT · KEY SPLIT 2.

ROUTE (GLO > SYSTEM, KNOB 3)

CH1-6: MIDI channels 1–6 play tracks 1–6, channels 7–16 are ignored. SEL: every channel plays the selected track.

GLOBAL (GLO > GLOBAL)

BPM (40–240), SWING, CLOCK (INT, USB +BT, TRS: follow MIDI clock and start/stop from that input; USB +BT is USB or Bluetooth), TUNE (±50).

The MENU (hold HOME)

SELECT walks every row (0.9.2), all four tabs in one chain (DISPLAY → CONTROL → AUDIO → SYSTEM; it stops at the first and the last), ALGORITHM jumps to the next / previous tab (its first row), any knob or OCT+ / OCT− changes the value; PRESETS does nothing here. HOME closes it (settings are saved then). The screen shows the tab's rows, the selected row's four as cards (ROWS 1–4, ROWS 5–8, ROWS 9–12) with their knob's number; the tabs on top, the footer MENU · DISPLAY · SCOPE 2/37. The header says MENU · DISPLAY.

Tab Row Values
DISPLAY COLOR GREY, GREEN, AMBER, ICE, VIOLET, ROSE, PAPER, HI-CON, NIGHT, MONO, JIANT (default)
DISPLAY SCOPE OFF (default), ON — (0.9.7) an engine's EDIT pages: OFF the creature on the whole panel, centred, the page's name and the sound's name small in its corners; ON the creature on the left, the SCOPE card and the chips as before. Settings saved before 0.9.7 load as OFF
DISPLAY LARGE OFF, ON (big labels and values)
DISPLAY ANIM ON, OFF (values snap; the power-on signature appears whole)
DISPLAY LEDS OFF, DIM LO, DIM HI (default), INV — (0.7.3) the idle glow's LEDs take turns frame to frame, so the glow no longer hums through the speaker once the music stops
DISPLAY SCREEN OFF NEVER (default), 5 MIN, 15 MIN, 30 MIN, 60 MIN
DISPLAY SAVER OFF, 1 MIN, 3 MIN (default), 5 MIN, 10 MIN — (V10.8.56) the screen saver: a VISUAL figure after that long with no panel input; see VISUAL and SAVER
DISPLAY HELP ON, OFF — (V10.7.60) a knob's meaning in the header where it is not obvious, and JAM's and TAKE's help line
DISPLAY PRESETS SCROLL (the PRESETS knob walks the sounds), MENU (the list opens as you turn) — (V10.7.81)
DISPLAY PANEL AUTO (default), A, B — (V10.8.63) how the screen is set up; see PANEL
CONTROL HOLD 0.3 s, 0.4 s (default), 0.5 s, 0.6 s — how long until a held button opens its layer
CONTROL KNOB ACCEL ON (default), OFF
CONTROL FX LATCH OFF (default since 0.6.64), ON
CONTROL BPM LOCK OFF, ON — DICE ALL keeps the tempo (the tempo is GLO + SELECT, GLO's F4 TAP or GLOBAL's BPM)
CONTROL SCALE LEDS OFF, ON — the keys of the scale glow, the root brighter
CONTROL MIDI OUT KEYS, CLOCK, ALL, OFF — what goes out over USB MIDI (and Bluetooth; see 14)
CONTROL MIDI MAP FACTORY (the standard CC map), CUSTOM ADD (the map and your learned CCs), CUSTOM (your learned CCs alone) — see MIDI LEARN
CONTROL LEARN OFF, SEL TRACK, FIXED TRK, CLEAR ALL — arms MIDI LEARN when the MENU closes; not saved
CONTROL VELOCITY OFF, SOFT, NORMAL (default), HARD — the keys play as hard as you strike them (F3..C5; the top row C#5..G5 has no sensor and follows your recent dynamics). The curve: SOFT louder for less, HARD needs more. OFF: every key 100, exactly as before. See Key velocity and aftertouch
CONTROL VEL MIN 1, 10, 20 (default), 30, 40, 50, 64, 80 — the softest strike's velocity (the range is scaled, no step)
CONTROL AFTERTOUCH OFF, LOW, MID (default), HIGH — pressing a held key harder: the matrix's AT source (new sounds route it to the filter, CUT +20), recorded, and sent as channel aftertouch with MIDI OUT ALL
CONTROL VEL LEARN ON (default), OFF, RESET — each key learns your soft, normal and hard strikes as you play (kept in the settings); RESET puts the factory calibration back, then learns again
AUDIO SPEAKER EQ FLAT, LOWCUT, BASS+ (an EQ on the master for the small speaker; also reaches the outputs and USB)
AUDIO USB LEVEL MASTER (USB follows the MASTER knob), FIXED (USB at full level), −6 / −12 / −18 / −24 dB (USB fixed and attenuated: for a phone or a computer whose input clips at the full level)
AUDIO CLICK OFF, REC (while a track is armed and playing), ON
AUDIO CLICK LEVEL LOW, MID, HIGH
AUDIO COUNT-IN OFF, 1 BAR, 2 BARS
AUDIO TRACKS 4 (default), 6
AUDIO LOAD ECO, LITE, FULL (default) — the same as GLO › SYSTEM KNOB 2
AUDIO OCT BEND OFF, 1, 2 (default), 3, 4, 5, 7, 12 ST — (V10.6z4) the expression keys: OCT+ held on a note bends up this far, OCT− a vibrato; OFF: OCT is the octave even with a note held (see Useful combinations)
SYSTEM USB AUDIO (stereo USB audio and MIDI, the default; was CONSOLE until V10.6d, when the serial console left), STEREO (audio + MIDI only, class 0; was OFF: helps macOS 13–15 see the USB audio input), STEMS (0.7.1: an 8-channel audio input, see "Stems" below), IN+OUT (0.7.5: stereo audio both ways, see "USB audio in" below), STEMS+IN (0.8.0: the stems with the audio output too, see "Stems with a voice" below)
SYSTEM RESTORE LAST OFF (default: no autosave, power-on at zero), ON (the last session back at power-on)
SYSTEM CPU CORES 1 CORE, 2 CORES (default) — from the next start; (V10.6z2) the second core only starts on the stock power settings (not after a SAFE START)
SYSTEM CPU CLOCK 360 MHZ (default), 320 MHZ — from the next start
SYSTEM BLUETOOTH OFF, ON (Bluetooth MIDI: ADV, then CONN), AIR (listens only: PROX and SWARM) — OCT+ on the row opens the PROX page (FAR / NEAR); see Bluetooth
SYSTEM CALIBRATION OCT+ opens HARDWARE CALIBRATION (teach each button and knob)
SYSTEM ABOUT OCT+ opens: version, QR code, LAST CRASH (kept across power-off) and credits (scroll with SELECT, OCT− back). V10.8.45 removed the CPU clock and rails lines and the hex lines of a crash since power-on; V10.8.49 the AUDIO LOAD lines (the header's number shows the load)

INIT SYSTEM is no longer in the MENU: SAVE › TOOLS › CLEAR PROJECT does it. If you hear clicks, watch the header's load number and look at ABOUT's LAST CRASH: a photo of that screen helps when you report a problem.

14. MIDI and USB

A practical guide (playing from a keyboard, CCs, clock, a Circuit Tracks recipe, what it cannot do): docs/MIDI.md.

  • USB is class-compliant MIDI and audio: the master output reaches the computer as a USB audio input.
  • MIDI IN over USB and the TRS jack. ROUTE decides which track each channel plays (see 13). Incoming notes on an armed track are recorded like the keys.
  • MIDI OUT (over USB; MENU > CONTROL > MIDI OUT, 0.6.72), each track on its channel (T1 = channel 1 … T6 = channel 6):
  • KEYS (the default): the keys send their notes, as before.
  • CLOCK: and the clock (24 a beat) with START / STOP, while the tempo is the FM-1's own (CLOCK INT): a drum machine or a DAW follows it. The clock runs while stopped too, so the follower knows the tempo before PLAY.
  • ALL: and every note the FM-1 plays: the sequencer, the arp, PLAYHEADS and the punch-in repeats, with the punch-ins' OCT− / OCT+ and RANDOM on them; each note gets its note-off, and STOP, a panic or a change of the setting end whatever is still on. Record the FM-1's music into a DAW as MIDI, or play other synths from it.
  • OFF: nothing.
  • PROGRAM CHANGE (0.6.72): program n on the channel a track plays loads the PRESETS list's sound number n + 1 (every engine's presets in their order, then the user presets) into that track; the selection stays where it was. (0.9.9) The engines in 0.9.8's order, ANALOG, FM6, PHASE, MATH (LOFI's number, V10.6h), VOICE, WHEEL, NOISE, DRUM, ANIMAL, whatever the PRESETS page shows (it starts with DRUM-X now): a MIDI setup's program numbers keep loading the sounds they did. Programs reach the list's first 128 sounds: since 0.8.3 that ends inside ANIMAL's presets (it comes last), so the user presets after it are picked on the device or from the editor.
  • Sections and projects (0.6.80): channel 16 is the song's: its PROGRAM CHANGE never loads a sound (whatever ROUTE). Programs 0–3 jump to section A–D of the project (playing: on the next bar, as the song layer's keys; stopped: at once; an empty one is said so); programs 16–21 load project 1–6 with its section A (stopped only, as SAVE › PROJECTS' LOAD). A foot controller or a DAW can run a set.
  • Not possible: MIDI OUT on the TRS jack (the FM-1's jack is an input only: no output line goes to it). Bluetooth MIDI works since V10.12: see Bluetooth MIDI and PROX.
  • Clock: GLO > GLOBAL > CLOCK USB or TRS follows that input's clock and Start / Continue / Stop. With an external clock, TAP and GLO + PLAY restart are disabled.
  • Controllers (on the track the channel plays): CC5 glide, CC7 level, CC10 pan, CC71 resonance and CC74 cutoff (the engine's own, where it has them), CC72 release, CC73 attack, CC75 decay, CC91 reverb send, CC93 chorus send, CC94 delay send; CC16–23 the engine's own eight values (EDIT 1 / EDIT 2's knobs, E1–E8, whatever the engine: CC16 is KNOB 1 of EDIT 1), CC102 / CC103 the post filter's cutoff / resonance, CC104 drive, CC105 sustain (0.6.96). CC1 (mod wheel), CC11 (expression) and channel aftertouch are sources in the MOD matrix (MODW, EXPR, AT). Pitch bend, sustain (CC64), All Sound Off (CC120) and All Notes Off (CC123) work. A CC is recorded as automation like a knob move.
  • NRPN (V10.6z3): every parameter automation can record (the sound, the mix, the effects, E1–E8 of any engine) and the globals (tempo, swing, the buses, the SLICER, the DJ FILTER ..; not the clock, routing, loads or the engine switch) have an NRPN, with up to 14 bits of resolution. CC99 0 + CC98 the parameter's number on the channel the track plays (channel 16 also with ROUTE CH1-6: the selected track); CC99 1 + CC98 the global's number, on channel 16 (or any channel the FM-1 hears); then CC6 (and CC38 for the fine part) the value, over the parameter's whole range. The numbers and ranges: docs/NRPN.md (made from the firmware itself). The CCs above stay as they were. With MIDI OUT ALL, turning a knob on the panel sends its NRPN (a track's on its channel, a global's on channel 16): a DAW records the moves and plays them back to the FM-1.
  • For apps (V10.6z3): the editor protocol (SysEx, web/EDITOR_PROTOCOL.md) is a versioned contract (1.0) that only grows; an app can also follow the transport, the punch-ins and each MUTATE as they happen, with no MIDI OUT setting.
  • USB MIDI and audio name: "FM-1" (since V10, 2026-10-30, so the apps made for the FM-1 find it; 0.9.12–V9 "JIANT", 0.7.0–0.9.11 "JIANT FM"; "FM-1 Update" while a package installs). In a DAW the MIDI port is "FM-1": Ableton Live and other Windows programs list "FM-1" (a second one "2- FM-1"), macOS the device "FM-1" and its port "FM-1", Linux "FM-1 MIDI 1". Up to 0.9.11 Windows could keep showing "Felucca" (it remembered the first name it saw); from 0.9.12 it reads the name again. If macOS still shows an old name, open Audio MIDI Setup > MIDI Studio with the FM-1 unplugged, delete its old entry, and plug it in again. The web editor and the installer also accept a device still named "JIANT", "JIANT FM" or "Felucca".

SCENE: one key plays the whole band (V10.24)

SCL › SCENE (SCL, then SCL again until SCENE, or SELECT). Each track gets a role; with SCENE ON every key you play reaches all the tracks with a role at once, each in its own way, all from that one note and the key (SCL):

Role What the key plays on that track
KEEP nothing: the track plays its own sequence (a kit is always KEEP)
CHORD the key's chord of the scale (the track's CHORD type; OFF: a triad); the track's voice becomes POLY
ARP that chord into the track's arp (the arp turns on, UP, if it was off)
BASS the key an octave down
LEAD the key an octave up
DRUM (a kit) the key writes a beat of its own (V10.6j; KNOB 4 STYLE: FOUR, BREAK, HALF, SPARSE, or GEN, V10.6r: the kit and beat GENE writes for the last genre, each key BASE, DENSE, BREAK or FILL)
  • KNOB 1 SCENE OFF / ON, KNOB 2 the TRACK, KNOB 3 its ROLE, KNOB 4 that track's CHORD type; on BASS and LEAD their PATTERN over the key's chord (V10.6j; BASS: ROOT PUMP OCTAVE R-5 WALK ROLL BOUNCE ACID; LEAD: HOOK ARC RISE STEPS SPARSE BOUNCE CONVRG RANDOM; V10.6m: GEN, a line in the last GENE genre's style), on DRUM its STYLE.
  • At power-on SCENE is OFF and every track KEEP (V10.26). OCT+ on this page dices the roles: each role goes to one track at most, so two tracks never play the same thing and never two play chords (it keeps the polyphony); the kit stays KEEP. OCT− sets every track KEEP. Turned ON with no role set, SCENE dices one. Giving a track a role another track has (KNOB 3) sends that other track to KEEP. T5 and T6 need 6 TRACKS (MENU).
  • REC armed and playing: every track with a role records what it played into its own steps (chords into one step, the arp its notes), so one take writes the whole scene; the KEEP tracks are untouched.
  • The page shows the six tracks, their roles and the notes the last key made on each.
  • SCENE and the roles are the session's: they start OFF at power-on.

Bluetooth MIDI and PROX (V10.13–V10.20)

  • Connect: MENU › SYSTEM › BLUETOOTH ON (with the music stopped the first time). The row shows ADV (waiting) and CONN once an app is connected. Connect from a Bluetooth MIDI app on the phone or computer (it appears as JIANT FM-1); keep the app in the foreground, phones cut Bluetooth for apps in the background.
  • MIDI in: what the app sends plays the FM-1 exactly as USB-MIDI does (notes, CC, program change, bend, clock with CLOCK USB +BT, MIDI LEARN and MAP). MIDI out: what MENU › CONTROL › MIDI OUT lets out (KEYS / CLOCK / ALL) goes to the app too. No SysEx (the editor and updates stay on USB).
  • PROX: a modulation source from how close the connected phone is (its Bluetooth signal, filtered). It follows the phone, not a hand. On the BLUETOOTH row (CONN) press OCT+: the PROX page. Phone away (a metre or so): OCT− (FAR). Phone on the FM-1, top left: OCT+ (NEAR). Then on a track's MOD page pick SRC PROX (e.g. DEST CUT). It fades to 0 when the phone disconnects. The page also shows the link (L1, packets read / received) and the raw signal words.
  • AIR (V10.35, an experiment): the third value of the BLUETOOTH row. The radio stops advertising (no MIDI) and only listens to every Bluetooth device around: phones, watches, headphones, TVs. PROX then follows how strongly they are heard, which a body or a hand near the antenna (top left of the back) shadows, so no phone is needed in your hand. On the BLUETOOTH row (AIR) press OCT+, calibrate FAR (away) and NEAR (hand on it) as above. It needs some Bluetooth devices nearby; with none it stays at 0.

USB HOST: a keyboard or an audio interface straight in (V10.41, experimental)

MENU › SYSTEM › USB › HOST, then close the MENU: the FM-1's USB port becomes the host of a class compliant USB-MIDI keyboard or controller (no computer in between), alone or behind a hub. What it plays reaches the FM-1 as USB-MIDI does: notes, CC, program change, bend, the clock and start / stop (CLOCK USB +BT), MIDI LEARN and MAP. - Power: the FM-1 does not power the port. Use a keyboard with its own power supply, or put a powered USB hub between them. - An audio interface (V10.53): if what you plug in is a class compliant USB audio interface (audio class 1.0, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz or, since V10.57, 48 kHz), its input is the FM-1's audio input: a track with the EXT engine takes it (see Sound from outside). - Messages: USB HOST: PLUG A MIDI KEYBOARD, USB MIDI KEYBOARD READY, USB AUDIO IN READY: USE INPUT (an audio interface), NOT USB MIDI OR AUDIO 16BIT 44.1-48K (a device that is neither), LOW SPEED: NOT SUPPORTED, USB DEVICE LOST (it reconnects by itself). - More keyboards (V10.8.69): the FM-1 now accepts keyboards whose USB description it used to refuse: a MIDI output-only interface listed before the one with the input, an interrupt input that asks to be polled every frame (interval 0), and any packet size from 4 to 64 bytes. It also tries a keyboard three times (a bus reset each time, with a longer pause after it) and gives it more time after it gets its address, so a keyboard slow to answer no longer reads NOT USB MIDI. If it still says so, unplug the keyboard, plug it in again, and check its power. - While HOST is on there is no USB to a computer: no editor, no stems, no MIDI to the computer. Any other USB value turns it off. HOST is never saved: the FM-1 always powers on as a USB device, so the installer and the editor always work. - Input only: nothing is sent to the keyboard. Its code lives in the Bluetooth area of the flash (a broken install says USB HOST: INSTALL AGAIN). From Melodee (Kerem Kilic; the USB host enumeration by recursivefieldinstruments).

MIDI LEARN (0.9.12)

Any knob of a track's sound to any CC of your controller, on the device (from Felucca 1.5's MIDI LEARN):

  1. MENU › CONTROL › LEARN: SEL TRACK (the CC follows whichever track is selected when it comes) or FIXED TRK (the CC stays on the track it was learned on). Hold HOME, ALGORITHM to the CONTROL tab, SELECT to LEARN, then HOME to close the menu: learning starts.
  2. Turn a knob on any page that edits a track's parameter (HOME, EDIT, ENV, LFO, FX, the MIXER, GLO's levels): the screen says LEARN T2 CUT: SEND A CC (or its CC if it already has one).
  3. Move the controller's knob (send the CC): CC21 > T2 CUT. From then on that CC sets T2's CUT as the knob does (0–127 over its range, recorded as automation like a knob), on any channel and over USB or the TRS jack.
  4. Turn the next knob, send the next CC … LEARN OFF when you are done (with LEARN on, knobs keep picking).
  • One CC sets one parameter; a parameter has one CC: learning it again replaces the old one. Ten at most (LEARN FULL: clear one by learning its CC to another knob, or everything with LEARN CLEAR ALL).
  • Never learned (CC7 RESERVED, and they keep doing their own): CC0 / 32 (bank select), CC1 (mod wheel), CC6 / 38 / 96–101 (data entry, RPN), CC11 (expression), CC64 (sustain) and CC120–127 (channel modes). The standard map's CCs (CC5 7 10 16–23 71–75 91 93 94 102–105) can be learned: with MIDI MAP on CUSTOM ADD, a learned CC wins over the map's meaning of that number.
  • Kept with the settings (not in a project; a settings backup carries it); MENU › CONTROL › LEARN CLEAR ALL (when the MENU closes) forgets them all. ROUTE still decides which channels are heard (CH1-6 ignores channels 7–16).
  • MENU › CONTROL › MIDI MAP decides what the CCs do: FACTORY the standard map alone, CUSTOM ADD the map and your learned CCs (learning with FACTORY switches to it), CUSTOM your learned CCs alone. Learned CCs work over USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth.

Stems (0.7.1)

Two ways to get each track on its own, to post-process them one by one in a DAW:

  • Over USB, live: MENU > SYSTEM > USB > STEMS. The device re-enumerates as an 8-channel USB audio input at 44.1 kHz, 16 bit (set the DAW's input to the device, 8 channels): channels 1–6 are the six tracks, each mono with its LEVEL, DIST, SLICER routing and mutes in and its PAN left out (what it adds to the mix, L + R halved); channels 7–8 are the FX return in stereo (the DELAY, REVERB and CHORUS buses, the SLICER's when it is on). All before the master: no leveler, limiter, CLIP or MASTER knob on them, so the sum of the eight is the mix as the buses hear it. USB LEVEL at −6 dB or lower gives headroom. The serial console is off in this mode; USB-MIDI, the editor and the installer still work. The speaker and the headphones play the master as always.

0.9.8: clean stems. Until 0.9.7 the 8-channel endpoint said 720 bytes (45 frames) while the FM-1 sends 46 frames whenever its clock gets ahead (often: it runs a little fast): the host dropped each such packet and paused, the FM-1's ring filled and whole blocks of 32 frames were lost, about a hundred times a second, in every channel at once: clicks, and a chopped, "separated by AI" sound in each stem (the stereo mix modes were not affected). Now 736 bytes; the ring also keeps a millisecond more in hand in STEMS and STEMS+IN, and a frame repeated after an underrun is made up spread over a packet instead of skipped. Update the FM-1 and the app (JIANT Stems 1.1), and record again: a take made with 0.9.7 cannot be mended afterwards. A track through the SLICER now has its own sound as the SLICER let it through in its stem (its repeats in the first such track's stem, or with the SLICER's FX ON in the FX return), so the eight still add up to the mix (until 0.9.7 that track was in its stem dry and again, sliced, in the FX return). What a stem is: exactly what the track adds to the mix in that take, so it nulls against the track rendered alone in the same take. The things that make one track depend on the others are in it, as in the mix: DUCK (the kick's pump on the other tracks), and the shared voices (8 among all tracks; LOAD ECO: 6, 4 a track, and with the load budget tight the tails already under −50 dB are trimmed): a note another track's note took the voice from ends early (a 6 ms fade). In the mix that is masked; soloed, a dense song can sound gated. For stems, record at LOAD FULL when the CPU allows it, and keep the song's polyphony within the budget. - From a backup, offline: the emulator page's "Stems". Back up the FM-1 (the editor's or the installer's "Back up"), open the emulator page, unfold "Stems", load the backup file, pick a song (its rows play once; a LOOP song once round) or the live section with a bar count, and press Render. Each track is rendered alone with its own share of the DELAY, REVERB and CHORUS (the other tracks' sends left out), plus the whole MIX (the master as the FM-1 plays it), all the same length, 16-bit 44.1 kHz stereo, in one ZIP: T1.wav .. T6.wav and MIX.wav (a silent track is left out). Faster than real time, no USB limits, nothing on the device.

Sound from outside: the USB input and the EXT engine

The FM-1 does not only make sound: it listens too. A voice, a guitar, another synth or a loop from the computer comes in as one more track and goes through everything JIANT does: the filter, the combs, lo-fi, the SLICER, the punch-ins, the effects; and it can modulate the other tracks as well.

1. How the audio comes in. Three ways; in all three the input is stereo (IN 1 the left, IN 2 the right).

  • From the computer or the phone: MENU › SYSTEM › USB › IN+OUT (0.7.5). The FM-1 re-enumerates (the serial console is off) and the host lists "JIANT FM" as a USB speaker too, stereo, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz. Choose the FM-1 as the output in the host's sound settings (or in the DAW / the app), set 44.1 kHz, and play. The FM-1 follows the host's clock (~3.6 ms behind); if the host stops sending, the input fades out and comes back when it resumes. Some hosts make a newly connected USB audio device the default output: that is why IN+OUT is a choice of its own, not on by default.
  • From a USB audio interface plugged into the FM-1: MENU › SYSTEM › USB › HOST (V10.53). A class compliant interface, 16 bit at 44.1 kHz (or 48 kHz since V10.57: the FM-1 converts it), with one or two inputs. The screen says USB AUDIO IN READY: USE INPUT. The FM-1 does not power the port: the interface needs its own supply or a powered hub. While HOST is on there is no USB to the computer (no editor, no recording over USB), and HOST is not saved: pick it again after power-on.
  • With STEMS+IN (see below): the audio the host sends comes in and returns recorded on a stem of its own.

2. An EXT track makes it sound. Since V10.56 the input only sounds where a track with the EXT engine takes it (before, it came in by itself on the last track; it changed because an app that monitors what it records sent the FM-1's own output back, a feedback loop). Pick a track, and with PRESETS go to EXT's sounds: IN 1, IN 2, IN 1+2, STEREO IN, MIC GATE, SPACE IN, TRANCE GATE, RING IN, CRUSH IN. Its two EDIT pages are named INPUT and COLOR:

Page KNOB 1 KNOB 2 KNOB 3 KNOB 4
INPUT SOURCE: IN 1, IN 2, 1+2 (both summed, mono), STEREO (the whole image), SWARM GAIN: 64 = as it comes, 127 = +12 dB GATE: a noise gate (0 off) MODE: THRU or KEYS
COLOR WIDTH: the stereo width (SOURCE STEREO, MODE THRU) RING: ring modulation (MODE KEYS) BITS: fewer bits RATE: samples held, 1 to 32
  • The screen shows the two inputs as meters (lit: the ones SOURCE takes), GATE's level across them and, between them, IN ENV's level.
  • GATE opens when the input goes over its level and closes when it falls under three quarters of it: it takes out the background noise between phrases.
  • Two EXT tracks can take IN 1 and IN 2 each, with a chain of their own: a microphone and a guitar, say.
  • Then, as any track: FILTER, DIST, LEVEL, PAN, the sends, MUTE and the MOD matrix. On STEREO, DIST also narrows the image a little.
  • SOURCE SWARM is not the audio input: it is the Bluetooth instrument (see EXT › SWARM). SWARM and a USB input on another track can play together.

3. THRU and KEYS; RING. With MODE THRU the input sounds all the time. With MODE KEYS it sounds only while a note plays, at the track's envelope (ENV: ATK, DEC, SUS, REL): the keys and the sequencer's steps open and close it. Write 1/16 steps with a short DEC and a held pad coming in turns into a trance gate in time; a voice turns into percussion. On KEYS, RING multiplies the input by a sine at the pitch of the note you play: ring modulation that follows the keys, from metallic to robotic. (On KEYS the input plays in mono.)

4. FILTER and the combs. The EXT track's EDIT › FILTER filters the input: LP, HP, BP with CUT and RES, and COMB / COMB-, a feedback comb tuned to the newest note the track played (see FILTER). With COMB and a high RES, a noise or a voice rings like a string at the note you play; COMB- sounds hollower. Move CUT with the LFO, the envelope or IN ENV so the filter breathes.

5. Lo-fi: BITS, RATE, DIST. BITS lowers the resolution (grain, quantisation noise); RATE holds each sample up to 32 times (aliasing, an old sampler's sound); the track's DIST (FX › DIST) saturates.

6. Stutter: the SLICER. On FX › SL BUS turn the EXT track on (and FX to cut the returns too) so it goes through the SLICER. MODE GATE cuts it in patterns (PAT 1–16); MODE STUT records the steps that play and repeats the last one on the others: a stutter in time, RATE 1/8 to 32T and DEPTH the repeat's level. SL PITCH tunes each repeat with a 16-step sequence. With LOAD ECO there is no SLICER.

7. Audio punch-ins. Hold FX and play the keys: REPEAT, REVERSE, FREEZE, TAPE STOP, PITCH UP / DOWN and STRETCH act on the whole mix, your input included, and it all comes back when you let go. While FX is held the knobs are the macros M1–M4. See Punch-in FX.

8. The sends. The EXT track's sends (FX › SENDS) take the input into CHORUS, DELAY and REVERB, the same buses the synths use. To throw it into the echo at the right moment, dub style, route a macro to DLY on FX › MACROS and turn it with FX held: it raises every track's delay send, the input's too, and when FX is let go it is back where it was.

9. The input as a modulator: IN ENV. In the matrix (LFO › MOD), the source IN ENV is the level of what comes in (up at once, down in about 50 ms; it watches both inputs). Send it to any destination of any track: CUT, PITCH, AMP, PAN, a send. It works even when no track plays the input: the input can be a controller only. With a negative amount it ducks: the synths go down when you speak. (JIANT Studio calls it FOLLOW.) The sources T1 ENV – T6 ENV do the same with another track's level.

10. Recording. What is recorded over USB has the input in it as its track mixed it: IN+OUT sends the host the stereo master; STEMS+IN sends each track apart, the FX return and the voice on two channels of its own (see below). With an interface on the HOST port there is no USB audio to the computer: record from the audio output.

Stems with a voice (0.8.0, test version)

MENU > SYSTEM > USB > STEMS+IN is STEMS and IN+OUT together, for the phone app: the phone's microphone goes out to the FM-1, comes into the last track (its LEVEL, PAN, MUTE and its CHORUS, DELAY and REVERB sends: your voice through that track's effects; if a track has the EXT engine, it comes in on that one instead), and 10 channels come back: T1–T6, the FX return L R, then the voice as the track mixed it and the voice as it came. The voice has a channel of its own (not in the track's stem), so the app can move it earlier by the round trip's latency and the voice lands in time with what you heard; the second voice channel is the reference the app measures that latency against. The voice's share of the FX return cannot be moved (it is mixed with every track's): its reverb and delays stay the latency late (~20–30 ms: in a reverb it sounds like pre-delay). The phone app reads and writes the FM-1 with its own USB driver (Android passes only some of a USB device's channels to apps). Test version: the app is JIANT Probe for now (its test 7).

15. Web tools: emulator, installer, editor, backup

All three run in the browser and update themselves with every change to the firmware.

Emulator — https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/emu/

The same code as the FM-1, with sound, in the browser. Play it with the mouse or the computer keyboard: Z–' and Q–O rows are the keys, 1 to = the buttons from FX to REC, [ ] OCT− / OCT+, ↑ ↓ SELECT, ← → ALGORITHM; Shift-click holds a button. Great for learning the layers without the device.

Installer — https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/webapp/installer/

Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Chrome on Android (USB OTG), the FM-1 connected straight in.

  • Install the current JIANT (it checks the FM-1 first: official V16, official V15 or JIANT only). Back up first when you update from V10.6o or earlier: this version keeps 6 songs (8 before), and very old projects (before 1.0.3) no longer open. Earlier versions stay in the version list.
  • Return to official: give it M-VAVE's unmodified FM-1.fwsc of V16 or V15 (checked locally in the browser). It first saves a complete backup (current music, saved music, sound banks and settings). Use this before installing JIANT if your FM-1 runs another custom firmware (Felucca, Skiff, baudgirl…), and whenever you want to go back to stock. The official firmware cannot open JIANT music; to restore the backup later, reinstall JIANT and use the editor.

Velocity view — https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/webapp/vel/

(V10.6z5, V10.6z7) Each note's velocity and each key's calibration, live, over USB (Chrome or Edge; protocol 1.1 or later). From V10.8.45 on the firmware has no velocity diagnostic: the page connects but shows no presses or captures (the keys' velocity and pressure work as always). See Key velocity and aftertouch. The velocity diagnostic (the presses it captured) left the firmware in V10.8.45: the step-by-step test in VELOCITY_DIAG.es.md is for older versions.

Editor — https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/webapp/editor/

Every parameter from the computer, over USB. Tabs: Sound, 6-OP FM, Sequencer, Tracks, Library, Projects, Settings.

  • 6-OP FM: edit FM6 patches, import .syx, and Send to the device's voice bank (B1–B32).
  • Sound, on a VOICE track (0.8.5): the Lyric box: LANG, LYRIC and the lyric's text, Send writes it to the track (accents and ñ converted).
  • Projects: the project slots, and the Complete backup: Save backup and Restore backup.

The complete backup

Save backup downloads one file with: the current music, all 6 projects with their 4 sections each, the arrangements and scenes, the 32 user presets (with their FM6 patches) and the settings. Restore backup replaces all of that on the device (keep USB connected). The FM6 voice bank (B1–B32) is not included: keep your .syx files.

Back up before updating, before returning to stock, and whenever you finish something you love.

Studio › Projects — https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/studio/

JIANT Studio's Projects page (Chrome or Edge, the FM-1 on USB) keeps backups in the browser and holds two tools for the FM-1's projects.

Project library (V10.8.54; it needs JIANT FM V10.8.54 or later). Read the projects lists the six projects: each one's name and which parts A–D it holds, the open one marked OPEN and a GEN draft GEN. - Rename: type a name (up to 12 characters, in capitals) and press Enter; it changes on the FM-1 at once. Name parts names B, C or D (A's name is the project's). - Copy to… and Move to… another project (1–6), and Delete. Export downloads a project as a file; Import here writes a file Studio exported into that place. - Before anything is overwritten or deleted, Studio asks, and downloads a copy of what was there. - The open project cannot be overwritten, moved, deleted or imported over. Nothing is done while the FM-1 plays: press STOP and try again.

Old projects (before V10.7). Since V10.8.51 the FM-1 no longer converts projects saved before V10.7 when it loads them: it says OLD PROJECT: OPEN IN STUDIO and leaves the slot untouched. Studio converts them: - Check and convert the FM-1 first keeps a full backup of the FM-1 in this browser ("Before converting"). Then it looks for the old projects and converts only those. It lists them and asks before it writes them to the FM-1. Then open them on the FM-1 (SAVE › PROJECTS). - Convert a backup file… does the same to an old backup file: the converted copy is downloaded as a new file (its name ends in "-converted").

16. Troubleshooting and FAQ

The installer does not install: what to do

Installer: https://juanjiant-bit.github.io/JIANT/webapp/installer/. When something fails it shows a What to do box with the steps for that error; if that is not enough, press COPY REPORT and paste it into your message (the browser, the MIDI ports it saw, the FM-1's firmware, the step it stopped at).

  • "This browser has no WebMIDI": Chrome or Edge on a computer. iPhone and iPad cannot (no browser there has WebMIDI); Safari has none; Android Chrome with an OTG cable may work, a computer is safer.
  • MIDI not allowed / blocked: the icon left of the address → Site settings → MIDI devices → Allow; reload. Brave: Shields off for the site.
  • FM-1 not found: switch it on; a USB data cable (many only charge); straight into the computer, no hub. Then try Is it in boot mode (WL80UBOOT)?.
  • Another program is using its MIDI port (Windows: one program per port): close the M-VAVE app, the DAW, MIDI-OX and other tabs with the JIANT editor; replug, reload, press Install.
  • An older official firmware (V14, V13…): Return to official (V16 or V15, no backup needed), then Install.
  • Felucca, Skiff or another custom firmware: Return to official first. It saves that firmware's backup first (Felucca's with its samples; Skiff's in its own format, for Skiff's editor) or, when it cannot make one, asks before going on without; then Install.
  • Where is FM-1.fwsc? M-VAVE's download page (https://www.m-vave.com/download): FM-1, firmware V16 (what it offers now), unzip it, the file FM-1.fwsc (718,196 bytes; V15's, if you kept it, is 699,956 bytes). We cannot host it: it is M-VAVE's. Picking the ZIP, another version or a JIANT package is told apart.
  • Stopped half way (update mode not found, stopped, connection lost): do not switch it off; replug and press the same button: it resumes. Windows may take a minute to install the update mode's driver the first time.
  • Black screen: connect it and press Install again; WL80UBOOT is the chip's boot mode (another cable, straight in; else FM-1 Transporter).
  • Page not found: use the address above exactly; old links (/JIANT/installer/, /JIANT/webapp/, a link with :1:1 stuck to it) now redirect by themselves.

The firmware

MENU › SYSTEM › BLUETOOTH says MISSING (was NO SEG), or "BLUETOOTH PART MISSING: REINSTALL: JIANT INSTALLER". The Bluetooth part of JIANT (it also holds GEN, the songs' saving, USB HOST and more) was not installed: reinstall with the web installer (above). Other flashing tools write only the main firmware.

My songs are not kept after power-off (a newer FM-1). FM-1s sold from late 2026 (the logo on the front) have a different flash chip (JEDEC 0xB36014). JIANT before V10.6z did not know it and ran from RAM only: nothing was saved, GENE was missing and the device could not update itself. Install the current version (the installer writes from the computer, so it works on those units): from then on it saves normally.

Songs 7 and 8 are gone. Since V10.6p JIANT keeps 6 songs (projects; the flash of 7 and 8 is kept for a drum sample bank). An FM-1 left on song 7 or 8 opens on song 6, with a one-time notice if they held music. A backup made before updating still holds them: move what you need into 1–6 with an earlier version, or keep the file.

It says SAFE START. A start that hung was reset, and this start skipped the power setup (V10.46). It plays on one core then (V10.6z2: the second core starts only on the stock power settings); the next normal power-on is back to two.

T5 or T6 is silent. TRACKS is set to 4 (the default): T5 and T6 are asleep. GLO > SYSTEM > TRACKS 6 (or MENU > AUDIO > TRACKS). The screen tells you when you play into an asleep track.

After clearing a sequence, notes still played on all tracks. This was fixed in v0.6.28: a clear now ends the punch-in lane's repeats (STUTTER, ARP), a DRUM track with no steps gets no ARP fill, and a section jump or quick chain waiting for the bar is called off. If something still plays after a clear, it may be the punch-in lane: hold REC and press FX to erase it (or SEQ + REC to clear everything).

Two cores (0.6.71) and MENU › SYSTEM › CPU CORES (0.9.12). The second core renders some synth tracks; MENU › SYSTEM › ABOUT says CORES 2, or CORES 1 and why. Since 0.9.12 MENU › SYSTEM › CPU CORES chooses 2 CORES (the default) or 1 CORE, kept with the settings, from the next start. If the FM-1 crashes or hangs while both cores work, or the second core misreads, stops answering or faults, it turns 2 CORES off for good and says so (2 CORES OFF AFTER A CRASH / CORE 2 FAILED: 1 CORE, then MENU › SYSTEM › CPU CORES); ABOUT then reads CORES 1 (AFTER A CRASH). Set 2 CORES again only if you want to test it. Hold REC while powering on for one core that session only. With both cores running the tracks share 12 voices instead of 8 (each track still at most 8); on one core (1 CORE set, after a crash, REC held) it is 8, and a second core that stops brings the budget back to 8 from the next note.

It crashes: a red screen "JIANT CRASH" (or "FELUCCA CRASH" before 0.7.0) with numbers. Take a photo of it and tell us the version (MENU › SYSTEM › ABOUT). How to read it:

  • 0.9.12 on: the version, CORE 0 OF 2 (the core that faulted, of how many were running), CODE xx-nn (the cause and the vector, below), then VEC, PC, EMU, DBG, RETS.
  • Before 0.9.12 the same five numbers came unlabelled, in that order, top to bottom: VEC (1 = the CPU exception), PC (where it failed), EMU and DBG (the cause bits), RETS (who called the function that failed).
  • The code: IL illegal instruction, MA misaligned access, DZ divide by zero, ST stack overflow, PC a jump outside the code, WR a write into a protected area, MM the memory unit, BU an access to no memory (a bad pointer), WD a hang (the watchdog reset it: no red screen), ?? none of those.
  • The FM-1 restarts by itself after 4 s. The last crash stays in the settings, also after switching off: MENU > ABOUT > LAST CRASH shows it as one line (IL01 2C 0.9.12 0201ABCD 0201ABCD: code and vector, cores, version, PC, RETS). The editor's settings backup carries it too.
  • For developers: tools/crash_decode.py VEC PC EMU DBG RETS names the function, against the ELF of the version that crashed.

What to try when it crashes now and then (even idle). In this order, a few hours each: 1. MENU › SYSTEM › CPU CORES 1 CORE (0.9.12 does it by itself after the first crash with both cores; before 0.9.12, hold REC at every power-on). 2. MENU › SYSTEM › CPU CLOCK 320 MHZ: the chip at JieLi's rated clock instead of the 360 MHz the FM-1's boot sets (switched at the next power-on; until V10.8.44 ABOUT showed CPU 320 MHZ, since V10.8.45 it has no clock line). About 11 % less CPU: a heavy song may shed voices sooner (LOAD LITE helps). If the FM-1 refuses (its clock is set up differently), it stays at 360 MHz. 3. If it still crashes: the photo, the version and LAST CRASH, please.

Clicks, stutters, the header's load near 99. Keep TRACKS on 4, try LOAD LITE or ECO, use fewer voices (MONO, fewer FM6 tracks), lighter reverbs (CLOUD and SHIMMER are the heaviest). Check MENU > SYSTEM > ABOUT > AUDIO LOAD.

SELECT doesn't change the tempo. Since 0.6.67 SELECT alone scrolls the pages; the tempo is GLO held + SELECT (or GLO's F4 TAP, or GLO > GLOBAL's BPM knob).

The knobs control M1–M4 instead of the page. The macros are latched (header [LFO] LATCH). Press LFO.

A song won't start: "PART EMPTY" / "ADD A SONG ROW". A row points to an empty section, or there are no rows. Save music into that section, or change the row.

It says SONG PLAYS: STOP IT TO EDIT. A song (SONG mode, SAVE + D5, or ARRANGE's PLAY) or a quick chain is playing; stop it to edit steps, use GEN, EUCLID, tools or UNDO (or turn SONG mode off with SAVE + D5 so PLAY plays the loop).

The keys feel inverted / a button does the wrong thing. Run HARDWARE CALIBRATION: hold OCT− and OCT+ while powering on (or MENU > SYSTEM > CALIBRATION) and teach each button and knob. A piano key cancels.

A new USB mode doesn't show up on the phone or computer. Since 0.9.10 the FM-1 leaves the bus for half a second when MENU › SYSTEM › USB changes (it came back after ~25 ms, and some phones and hubs did not notice it had gone, so they kept the old mode); it appears about a second after the menu closes. Older firmware: switch again, or unplug.

SAVED (NO FLASH). The flash chip wasn't detected; saves stay in RAM only. Power-cycle the device. If it persists, back up what you can with the editor and reinstall.

The FM-1 stays black after an interrupted update. Check whether the computer sees it as WL80UBOOT (a USB device 4C4A:8057): that's the chip's boot mode and the installer can write it again (try another cable). To enter update mode deliberately from a running device, hold OCT− + OCT+ for 5 seconds. If that isn't enough, FM-1 Transporter reads and writes the flash with a Seeed XIAO RP2040.

I want the factory firmware back. Use the installer's Return to official section with M-VAVE's V16 or V15 (it backs up first).

I came from baudgirl / Felucca / Skiff. Can I install directly? No: return to official first with the installer, then install JIANT. Going straight from another custom firmware has bricked an FM-1.

Where did my Felucca samples go? JIANT has no user samples; that flash now holds the songs.
